dervis-irab:1-1.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَسائَلُونَ): an imperfect verb; its origin is تتساءلون, and one of the two tāʾs was dropped; that is, you ask one another.
(الْأَرْحامَ): plural of رحم, which is kinship.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ): the i'rab of يا أيها has been given many times before; الناس is a badal (substitute) of «أي»; اتقوا ربكم is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ): الذي is a naʿt (adjective) of «ربكم»; the clause خلقكم is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; من نفس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلقكم; واحدة is an adjective; the clause is resumptive, introduced to treat the beginning of creation and formation. (وَخَلَقَ مِنْها زَوْجَها): the واو is a conjunction; خلق is a past verb; منها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خلق; زوجها is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَبَثَّ مِنْهُما رِجالًا كَثِيراً وَنِساءً): the واو is conjunctive; بث is a past verb; منهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بث; رجالا is a mafʿūl bihi; كثيرا is an adjective; نساء is conjoined to «رجالا». (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسائَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحامَ): the واو is conjunctive; اتقوا الله is an imperative verb [with its agent and object]; الذي is an adjective; the clause تساءلون is the ṣila; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تساءلون; الأرحام is conjoined to الله, and in this conjunction there is an exaltation of the standing of kinship and of the obligation to treat it dutifully and to observe it. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيباً): the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position; إن and its noun; the clause of كان and what falls within its scope is the khabar (predicate) of إن; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «رقيبا»; the noun of كان is latent (mustatir), and رقيبا is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In the above verse there is the device of barāʿat al-istihlāl (artful opening): He opened the sura by alluding to the beginning of creation and formation, pointed to the important role of woman, and enjoined the maintaining of the ties of kinship. Arabic poetry is full of mention of the ties of kinship and their standing with Allah; it is enough for us to point to the ode of Maʿn ibn Aws whose opening line is:
وذي رحم قلمت أظفار ضغنه ... بحلمي وهو ليس له حلم
(And many a kinsman — I clipped the nails of his rancour with my forbearance, while he has no forbearance.)
It is a magnificent ode which hardly any literary book is without; let whoever wishes refer to it.

dervis-irab:2-2.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْيَتامى): those whose fathers have died, so they are left alone without them; اليتم is being alone. From it come الرملة اليتيمة (the solitary sand-dune) and الدرة اليتيمة (the unique pearl). It has been said: the orphan among humans is from the side of the fathers, and among animals from the side of the mothers. اليتامى is a plural of a plural: اليتيم was pluralised as يتمى, like أسرى, then يتمى was pluralised as يتامى, like أسرى into أسارى. It may also be pluralised on the pattern فعائل because اليتيم is treated like nouns such as صاحب and فارس, so one says يتائم and then يتامى by metathesis.
(الحوب), with ḍamma or fatḥa on the ḥāʾ: the great sin; it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of حاب حوبا وحابا.

* I'rab:
(وَآتُوا الْيَتامى أَمْوالَهُمْ): the واو may properly be resumptive, so the clause is resumptive, introduced to begin [explaining] the manner and ways of fearing [Allah]; اليتامى is put first because of complete concern for their affair. It may also properly be conjunctive, joined to what preceded, so that the narrative is continuous. آتوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the واو is the fāʿil (agent); اليتامى is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and أموالهم the second mafʿūl bihi. (وَلا تَتَبَدَّلُوا الْخَبِيثَ بِالطَّيِّبِ): conjoined to what preceded; لا is prohibitive; تتبدلوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the واو is the fāʿil; الخبيث is a mafʿūl bihi; the باء is a preposition and الطيب — which is what is given up — is genitive by it, and the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تتبدلوا. (وَلا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوالَهُمْ إِلى أَمْوالِكُمْ): the واو is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; نأكلوا [Translator's note: so in the source, for تأكلوا] is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا; أموالهم is a mafʿūl bihi; إلى أموالكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "joined to your wealth". (إِنَّهُ كانَ حُوباً كَبِيراً): إن and its noun; the clause of كان with its noun and khabar (predicate) is the khabar of إن; the clause of إن and what falls within its scope is causal, with no grammatical position, and for this reason the hamza of إن is given kasra.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there are instances of eloquence reaching the level of inimitability, which we summarise as follows:
1- Majāz mursal (metonymic trope) in the words of the Exalted: «وآتوا اليتامى أموالهم», because Allah, Glory be to Him, does not command that young orphans be given their wealth — that would be unreasonable; rather, the fact is that Allah commands that wealth be given to those who have reached the age of maturity after having been orphans. So the word اليتامى here is a majāz mursal, because it is used of those who are mature, and the relation is consideration of what they formerly were.
2- Istiʿāra makniyya (implicit metaphor) in the eating of the orphans' wealth: He likened their wealth to food that is eaten, then lent to it the most prominent property of food, which is eating. In this metaphor there are two of the subtlest secrets:
a- The way of eloquence is to forbid the lesser in order to draw attention to the greater, when what is forbidden has degrees. The requirement of this rule would have been to forbid the eating of the orphan's wealth by one who is poor and in need of it, so that the prohibition of the rich would follow a fortiori. So there must be a secret explaining the benefit of singling out the greater for prohibition in this verse, and that is what is understood from the words «إلى أموالكم». The secret in that is that eating the orphan's wealth while having no need of it is the ugliest form of eating, so it was singled out for prohibition to brand whoever falls into it as shameful.
b- The second secret is in singling out eating, because the Arabs held excessive eating to be blameworthy and counted it as gluttony equal to bestiality. So it is as though the one who eats the orphan's wealth — when he has no need of it and has much wealth — is worse than one who eats it while destitute and in severe need of it, even though both share in eating what is forbidden and are strung together on one rope. It is known that the more deeply what is forbidden is steeped in ugliness and the more extreme in hideousness, the more the soul naturally recoils from it.
3- Ṭibāq (antithesis) between الخبيث, which is unlawful wealth, and الطيب, which is lawful and agreeable wealth.

dervis-irab:84-84.t:
* I'rab:
(فَقاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لا تُكَلَّفُ إِلَّا نَفْسَكَ) The fāʾ is al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e.: if the matter is such — the hypocrites not obeying and their holding others back from fighting — then fight, you alone, paying no heed to what they have inclined towards. It is also permissible for the fāʾ to be resumptive, confirming what precedes it. (قاتل) is an imperative verb, and (في سبيل الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قاتل). The clause (لا تكلف إلا نفسك), with the verb in the passive, is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: in the state of your being responsible for yourself alone, for Allah is your Helper and Supporter. (نفسك) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (تكلف). It may also be resumptive, as His informing him ﷺ that He does not charge him with other than himself. (وَحَرِّضِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) is conjoined to (قاتل), and (المؤمنين) is a mafʿūl bihi. (عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَكُفَّ بَأْسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) The clause of hope is a ḥāl, i.e.: rise up alone to fight them, the situation being that their might has been restrained from you. (عسى) is a past verb, one of the verbs of hope which the grammarians call "verbs of approximation" (afʿāl al-muqāraba) by way of taghlīb (applying the name of the predominant member to the whole group); (الله) is its noun, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from (أن) and what falls within its scope is its khabar (predicate). (بأس) is a mafʿūl bihi, and (الذين كفروا) is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct); the clause (كفروا) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (وَاللَّهُ أَشَدُّ بَأْساً وَأَشَدُّ تَنْكِيلًا) The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (أشد) a khabar; (بأسا) is a tamyīz (specification), and (أشد تنكيلا) is conjoined to what precedes.

dervis-irab:85-85.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الكفل), with kasra on the kāf and sukūn on the fāʾ: a double, a portion, a share. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "al-kifl, on the pattern of ḥiml: a double of reward and of sin."
The lexicographers said: the use of al-kifl for evil is more frequent than the use of al-naṣīb for it, although each of them may be used for good, as the Exalted said:
«يؤتكم كفلين من رحمته» (He will give you a double portion of His mercy). Because al-naṣīb is rarely used for evil and al-kifl is often used for it, He differentiated between them in the verse just mentioned, bringing al-kifl with the evil intercession and al-naṣīb with the good one.
(مقيت), with ḍamma on the mīm, i.e.: guardian, witness. It is derived from al-qūt (sustenance), because it holds the soul together and preserves it. Al-Zubayr ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said:
وذي ضغن نفيت السّوء عنه ... وكنت على إساءته مقيتا
(And many a rancorous man I kept harm away from, though I had power over [/ was watchful of] his wrongdoing.)

* I'rab:
(مَنْ يَشْفَعْ شَفاعَةً حَسَنَةً يَكُنْ لَهُ نَصِيبٌ مِنْها) A resumptive clause, brought to show that he ﷺ has a far-reaching hand in urging the believers to fighting and jihād. It goes without saying that intercession (al-shafāʿa) is mediation in bringing a person to a worldly or otherworldly benefit — and what benefit is loftier, more sublime and greater than urging to jihād, since in it lies triumph in this world and the next? (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يشفع) is an imperfect verb, the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (شفاعة) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and (حسنة) an adjective; (يكن) is the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis); (له) is the fronted khabar of the defective (nāqiṣa) (يكن) and (نصيب) its postponed noun; (منها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of (نصيب). The protasis and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of (من). (وَمَنْ يَشْفَعْ شَفاعَةً سَيِّئَةً يَكُنْ لَهُ كِفْلٌ مِنْها) is conjoined to what precedes and parallels it in i'rab. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقِيتاً) The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; (كان) and its noun; (على كل شيء) is attached to (مقيتا), and (مقيتا) is the khabar of (كان).

dervis-irab:86-87.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَسِيباً): al-ḥasīb in this place is of the pattern faʿīl from al-ḥisāb, which is enumeration (al-iḥṣāʾ); from it one says: ḥāsabtu fulānan ʿalā kadhā wa-kadhā (I called so-and-so to account for such-and-such). It is strange that some of the exegetes and grammarians err and say that the meaning of al-ḥasīb is "the Sufficient", from the expression ḥasbiya al-shayʾu meaning "the thing sufficed me", from their saying ḥasbī kadhā wa-kadhā (such-and-such suffices me).

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا حُيِّيتُمْ بِتَحِيَّةٍ فَحَيُّوا بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْها أَوْ رُدُّوها) A resumptive statement, brought to encourage greeting. The origin of al-taḥiyya (greeting) is the prayer for life and its length; then it came to be used for every prayer. (إذا) is an adverb of future time (ẓarf) containing the meaning of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis, which is «حيّوا». The clause (حييتم) is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), and (بتحية) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (حييتم). The fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and the clause (حيوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (بأحسن) is attached to (حيوا), and (منها) is attached to (أحسن). The wāw [Translator's note: the source says "wāw", though the conjunction in the verse is (أو)] is a conjunction, and (ردوها) is conjoined to «حيّو» [Translator's note: so in the source, i.e. حيّوا]. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَسِيباً) The clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) and has no grammatical position; (إن) and its noun, and the clause of (كان) with its noun and khabar (predicate) is the khabar of (إن). (اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ) The clause is resumptive; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (لا) is the lā of generic negation and (إله) its noun; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and «هو» is a badal (substitute) from the position of (لا) together with its noun. The i'rab of the formula of the testimony of faith (kalimat al-shahāda) has already been given. The clause is the khabar of (الله). (لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ) The lām is that of the answer to an omitted oath; (يجمعنكم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; (إلى يوم القيامة) is attached to (يجمعنكم). The clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the omitted oath. (لا) is the lā of generic negation, and (ريب) is the noun of «لا», indeclinable on the fatḥa; (فيه) is attached to an omitted khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَمَنْ أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حَدِيثاً) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and (أصدق) is a khabar; (من الله) is attached to (أصدق), and (حديثا) is a tamyīz (specification).

dervis-irab:88-88.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَرْكَسَهُمْ): He returned them to the status of the polytheists. Al-raks: returning a thing upside down. From it is the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa:
أركسوا في فئة مظلمة ... كسواد الليل ينلرها فتن
(They were turned back into a dark faction, like the blackness of night, trials [overwhelming it].) [Translator's note: the word ينلرها appears so in the source and seems to be a misprint.]

* I'rab:
(فَما لَكُمْ فِي الْمُنافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ) The fāʾ is resumptive; (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of (ما). (في المنافقين) is attached to (فئتين), for it is equivalent to "what is it with you that you divide over the affairs of the hypocrites?"; the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was left standing in its place. It is also permissible for them to be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial), since it was originally an adjective of (فئتين), i.e.: two factions divided over the hypocrites. (فئتين) is a ḥāl from the kāf in «لكم». The Kufans say:
the accusative of «فئتين» is as the khabar of an implied (muḍmara) kāna, the implied form being: "What is it with you that, regarding the hypocrites, you were two factions?" This view is strange, but it is good, and Ibn Jarīr preferred it. (وَاللَّهُ أَرْكَسَهُمْ بِما كَسَبُوا) The wāw is circumstantial; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (أركسهم) is a khabar; (بما) is attached to (أركسهم), and «ما» may be a relative or a maṣdar-forming particle (maṣdariyya); the clause (كسبوا) has no grammatical position in either case. The clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. It is also permissible for the wāw to be resumptive, so that the clause is resumptive. (أَتُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَهْدُوا مَنْ أَضَلَّ اللَّهُ) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī); (أن) and what falls within its scope form an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) which is the object of (تريدون); (من) is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (أضل الله) has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila (relative clause). The clause is resumptive, brought to censure those who disagreed. (وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ سَبِيلًا) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ; (يضلل) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis), jussive (majzūm), and given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (الله) is the fāʿil (agent). The fāʾ connects the apodosis; (لن) is a particle of negation, subjunctive and futurity; (تجد) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by (لن); (له) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, since it was originally an adjective of «سبيلا»; (سبيلا) is a mafʿūl bihi. The clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis), and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of (من).

* Benefits:
What history says:
It is reported that a group of the hypocrites asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission to go out to the desert, pleading as excuse that they found the climate of Medina unwholesome. When they went out, they kept travelling stage by stage until they joined the polytheists. The Muslims then disagreed about them: some said, "They are disbelievers," and some said, "They are Muslims."
In a second report: they were a group who went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Uḥud and then turned back. It is also said: they were a group who outwardly professed Islam and held back from emigrating (al-hijra).
Al-Qurṭubī said: «What is meant by the hypocrites here is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and his companions who deserted the Messenger on the day of Uḥud and returned with their troops after having set out.»
The Muslims disagreed about them: one party said, "Kill them, O Messenger of Allah," because of the sign indicating their disbelief; and another party said, "Do not kill them," because they uttered the two testimonies of faith. The reproach is in reality directed at the second party, who said: «Do not kill them».

dervis-irab:3-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُقْسِطُوا): imperfect of the quadriliteral أقسط, meaning "he acted justly"; the triliteral [قسط] means "he acted unjustly".
(تَعُولُوا): from their saying عال الميزان when the balance tilts, and "So-and-so's balance is عائل", and عال الحاكم في حكمه when the judge is unjust in his judgement. Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī mentioned that عال comes with seven meanings:
The first: عال, i.e. he inclined.
The second: he increased; the third: he was unjust; the fourth: he became poor; the fifth: he burdened; the sixth: he bore the provision of dependants, and from it is the saying: «وابدأ بمن تعول» (and begin with those you support); the seventh: عال, i.e. he overcame, and from it is عيل صبري (my patience was overcome). عال has also occurred with meanings other than the seven mentioned by Ibn al-ʿArabī, among them: عال, it became severe and grew worse, reported by al-Jawharī; عال الرجل في الأرض when the man travelled through the land, reported by al-Harawī; and عال when he rendered [someone] incapable, reported by al-Aḥmar. These are three meanings besides the seven. The fourth: عال, i.e. his dependants became many. So the total meanings of عال are eleven, and more discussion of this root will come in the section of Benefits.
(الصدقات): bridal dowries; its singular is صدقة, with fatḥa on the ṣād and ḍamma on the dāl. The dowry also has many names, among them صدقة with two fatḥas, and with fatḥa then sukūn, and صداق with kasra or fatḥa on the ṣād.
(نِحْلَةً): maṣdar (verbal noun) of نحله كذا, i.e. he gave him such-and-such as a gift, willingly.
(هَنِيئاً مَرِيئاً): two adjectives from هنؤ الطعام أو الشراب, when food or drink is pleasant to swallow with nothing to spoil it. It has been said: الهنيء is what the eater enjoys, and المريء is what has a praiseworthy outcome. The passage of food from the throat to the opening of the stomach is called المريء (the oesophagus) because of the food's passing (مروء) through it, i.e. its going down smoothly.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تُقْسِطُوا فِي الْيَتامى): the واو is resumptive; إن is conditional; خفتم is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); أن is a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative; لا is negating; تقسطوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and what falls within its scope is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في اليتامى is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) تقسطوا; what is meant by that will come in the section of Benefits. (فَانْكِحُوا ما طابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّساءِ مَثْنى وَثُلاثَ وَرُباعَ): the فاء links the apodosis; انكحوا is an imperative verb and the واو is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of jussive as the protasis [Translator's note: so in the source («فعل الشرط»); it is evidently meant as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ)]; ما is a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause طاب has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to طاب; من النساء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the pronoun in طاب]; مثنى, ثلاث and رباع are ḥāls. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī parsed them as a badal (substitute) of «ما». More will be said about them in the section of Benefits. (فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا فَواحِدَةً): the فاء is resumptive; إن is conditional; خفتم is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; أن لا تعدلوا: the interpreted maṣdar is a mafʿūl bihi; فواحدة: the فاء links the apodosis, and واحدة is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, i.e. «فالزموا واحدة» (then keep to one), and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (أَوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ): أو is a conjunction expressing choice, i.e. from among the slave-women in your possession, because of the ease and facility in that. ما is a relative noun conjoined to «واحدة», and the clause ملكت أيمانكم has no grammatical position. (ذلِكَ أَدْنى أَلَّا تَعُولُوا): the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and أدنى its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive; أن لا تعولوا: the interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to أدنى, i.e. nearer to justice and to not being unjust. The jurists have curious explanations for grouping slave-women with free women in ease and facility; you will find some of them in the section of Benefits. (وَآتُوا النِّساءَ صَدُقاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً): the واو is conjunctive; آتوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the واو is the fāʿil; النساء is a mafʿūl bihi and صدقاتهن a second mafʿūl bihi; نحلة is accusative as a maṣdar [mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], because النحلة and الإيتاء are synonyms meaning giving, so it is as though it were said: «وانحلوا النساء صدقاتهن نحلة», i.e. give them their dowries willingly. It may also be accusative as a ḥāl from those addressed, after interpreting it as a derived form, i.e. give them their dowries as givers, willing in the giving; or as a ḥāl from «صدقاتهن», i.e. given as a gift, granted willingly.
It has been said: نحلة from Allah, i.e. a gift from Him and a favour from Him to them. It has also been said: النحلة is creed and religion, and the meaning is: give them their dowries as a matter of religion; in that case it is parsed as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). We have only cited these aspects because they are equally weighty. (فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْساً): the فاء is resumptive; إن is conditional; طبن is a past verb indeclinable on sukūn; the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil, and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; عن شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to طبن; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of شيء; نفسا is a tamyīz (specification). (فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئاً مَرِيئاً): the فاء links the apodosis; كلوه is an imperative verb with its mafʿūl bihi; هنيئا and مريئا are two adjectives of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. «أكلا هنيئا مريئا» (an eating wholesome and pleasant), or a ḥāl from the pronoun, i.e. eat it while it is wholesome and pleasant.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is the device of taghlīb (giving preponderance): He said «فانكحوا ما طاب لكم» and did not say «من», as would be expected from the use of «من» for rational beings and «ما» for non-rational beings — [this is] by taghlīb, because «ما» comes for the attributes of rational beings, and He described them by goodness (الطيب), so the use of «ما» is correct. This is a beautiful secret by which you may measure what occurs like it; so ponder it, and may Allah protect you.

* Benefits:
1- History relates, in explaining the occasion of revelation of this verse, that a man would find an orphan girl marked by beauty and wealth while he was her guardian, and he would marry her, holding her back jealously from others. Perhaps ten of them would gather with him, and he would fear — because of their weakness and the lack of anyone to be angry on their behalf — that he would wrong them of their rights and neglect what was due to them. So it was said to them: if you fear that you will not act equitably — i.e. justly — regarding the orphan women, then marry of others what is good for you. So the verse came warning against entanglement and commanding caution, and among others there is room up to four.
2- (مَثْنى وَثُلاثَ وَرُباعَ) are adjectives diverted (maʿdūla) from repeated numbers, and therefore they are diptotes, i.e. two by two, three by three, four by four. Among the curious things that some — from whom the secrets of the noble Arabic language have escaped — have held to, to permit marrying nine: they said it is because two, three and four total nine, and because the Prophet ﷺ died leaving nine [wives]. This, as you see, arises from ignorance of the secrets of the clear Arabic language, because if you say: «جاء القوم مثنى وثلاث ورباع», its meaning is that they came two by two, three by three and four by four, and you put all of that in the accusative as a ḥāl. The ḥāl is what clarifies the state of the agent or the direct object; you want to clarify how their coming was, i.e. they did not come all together nor singly. Allah, Glory be to Him, made clear what He made permissible of marriage; as for the Prophet ﷺ, that was among his particular characteristics peculiar to him alone.
Moreover, the grammarians have said much about the diverted number: does it run from one to ten, or is it only what the Noble Qur'an pronounced? Some said: it ends at رباع; others said: at سداس; and it was said: at عشار.
Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī has the line:
أحاد أم سداس في أحاد ... لييلتنا المنوطة بالتّناد؟
(Is it one, or six in one — this little night of ours, tied to the Day of Calling?)
They said that Abū al-Ṭayyib committed several solecisms in this line. He said أحاد and سداس, while in eloquent speech only مثنى, ثلاث and رباع have been heard, and there is disagreement over خماس and سداس up to عشار. Another is that he formed the diminutive of ليلة as «لييلة», whereas it is formed as «لييلية». Another is that he made it diminutive, and the diminutive indicates smallness, as if it were short, and then said «المنوطة بالتناد» (tied to the Day of Calling), and nothing would be longer than it then; so the end of his speech contradicts its beginning. We may defend Abū al-Ṭayyib against the contradiction they claim against him, because the diminutive sometimes comes in their speech for magnification, as in the saying of Labīd:
وكل أناس سوف تدخل بينهم ... دويهة تصغّر منها الأنامل
(And every people — there will enter among them a "little" calamity from which the fingertips turn pale.)
So Abū al-Ṭayyib made the night diminutive here for magnification, because he found it so long that he made it tied to the Day of Calling. From this is the Prophet's ﷺ saying to ʿĀʾisha: يا «حميراء»; and it may be that it was made diminutive because of its subtlety and hiddenness — and great matters come from small sparks. As for his saying أحاد and سداس, he used the part, which is one and six, as single numbers, i.e. he did not mean them as one repeated nor six repeated, as is the denotation of the diverted number; rather he intended the single, and used for it the diverted form that indicates multiplicity, figuratively, by applying the name of the whole — which is أحاد and سداس — to the part, which is one-by-one and six-by-six [Translator's note: so in the source]. This usage is figurative, and figurative use is not a solecism. Moreover, عشار has occurred in the poetry of al-Kumayt ibn Zayd, and he is an authority:
فلم يستريثوك حتى رميت فوق الرجال خصالا عشارا
(They did not find you slow until you had shot beyond the men ten by ten in merits.)

Why are they diptotes?
The schools of thought reported on the cause of their being diptotes are four:
1- The view of Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and Abū ʿAmr: diversion (ʿadl) and being an adjective.
2- The view of al-Farrāʾ: they are diptote because of diversion and definiteness by the intended alif and lām, and the alif and lām are prevented from appearing because they are intended as being in annexation.
3- The view of al-Zajjāj: they are diverted from اثنين اثنين, ثلاثة ثلاثة and أربعة أربعة, and diverted from the feminine.
4- What Abū al-Ḥasan reported from some grammarians: the cause preventing declension is the repetition of diversion in it, because it is diverted from the word اثنين and diverted from its meaning. That is because it is not used where the non-diverted numbers are used: you say «جاءني اثنان وثلاثة», but «جاءني مثنى وثلاث» is not permitted unless a plural precedes it, because this category was made to explain the ordering of the action. So if one says «جاءني القوم مثنى», it conveys that the order of their coming occurred two by two. As for the non-diverted numbers, their purpose is only to report the quantity of what is counted, nothing else. Ibn Hishām has a splendid section in Mughnī al-Labīb that he wrote about this verse, in the sixth chapter of his book: «On warning against matters well known among the parsers whereas the correct view is otherwise»; refer to it if you wish.
(هَنِيئاً مَرِيئاً) are parsed as an adjective of the maṣdar and as a ḥāl.
As for the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
هنيئا لك العيد الذي أنت عيده ... وعيد لمن سمى وضّحى وعيّدا
(Wholesome to you be the feast whose feast you are, and a feast for whoever said "bismillah", sacrificed and celebrated.)
— here they must be parsed as a ḥāl, because there is nothing indicating a maṣdar that could properly be described by them. العيد is the fāʿil of هنيئا, because it is a ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle).

dervis-irab:5-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السُّفَهاءَ): the squanderers who spend their wealth on what it ought not to be spent on, or on what is of no profit.
(قِياماً): maṣdar (verbal noun) of قام, i.e. you subsist by it and are revived; had you wasted it, you would be lost; so it is as if it were your subsistence and your revival.
(آنَسْتُمْ): you perceived and ascertained clearly.

* I'rab:
(وَلا تُؤْتُوا السُّفَهاءَ أَمْوالَكُمُ الَّتِي جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ قِياماً): resumptive speech introduced to explain the remaining rulings related to the wealth of orphans. لا is prohibitive; تؤتوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; the واو is the fāʿil (agent); السفهاء is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and أموالكم a second mafʿūl bihi; التي is a relative noun in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of أموالكم; the clause جعل الله لكم is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; قياما is the second mafʿūl bihi of جعل, which is in the sense of صيّر (made into), the first mafʿūl bihi being omitted, the implied form being "which He made for you a means of subsistence"; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قياما». If جعل is in the sense of خلق (created), then قياما is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted referential pronoun, i.e. He made it, it being a means of subsistence. (وَارْزُقُوهُمْ فِيها وَاكْسُوهُمْ وَقُولُوا لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفاً): وارزقوهم — the واو is a conjunction, and ارزقوهم is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ارزقوهم; اكسوهم is conjoined to ارزقوهم; قولوا is likewise conjoined to وارزقوهم; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قولوا; قولا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and معروفا an adjective. (وَابْتَلُوا الْيَتامى حَتَّى إِذا بَلَغُوا النِّكاحَ): the واو is conjunctive and the speech is conjoined; in it is the specification of the time for handing over the orphans' wealth to them. اليتامى is the mafʿūl bihi of the verb ابتلوا; حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition, making reaching [marriageable age] and perceiving maturity the limit for the giving. It has been said: حتى is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya), but conveys limit; it is the حتى after which clauses occur, as in the saying:
فما زالت القتلى تمجّ دماءها ... بدجلة حتى ماء دجلة أشكل
(The slain kept spurting their blood into the Tigris, until the water of the Tigris was reddish.)
إذا is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause بلغوا النكاح is in the position of genitive by annexation. (فَإِنْ آنَسْتُمْ مِنْهُمْ رُشْداً): the فاء links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); إن is conditional; آنستم is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause فإن آنستم has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivising condition; منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آنستم; رشدا is a mafʿūl bihi. (فَادْفَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوالَهُمْ): the فاء is linking; ادفعوا is an imperative verb and the واو is the fāʿil; إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ادفعوا; أموالهم is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (وَلا تَأْكُلُوها إِسْرافاً وَبِداراً أَنْ يَكْبَرُوا): the واو is resumptive; لا is prohibitive; تأكلوها is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا; the واو is the fāʿil and the هاء the object; إسرافا and بدارا are two maṣdars in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. being extravagant and hastening; or they are in the position of a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. because of your extravagance and your hastening [to anticipate] their growing up. أن يكبروا is an interpreted maṣdar, the mafʿūl bihi of the maṣdar, or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi with the mafʿūl bihi omitted; in that case an annexed noun must be implied, i.e. for fear that they grow up. The clause is resumptive. We have made the واو resumptive, although the apparent sense of the speech suggests it is conjunctive, because [otherwise] the meaning would become "hand over [their wealth] and do not consume it", and this is unsound, because the condition and its apodosis are consequent upon reaching marriageable age, so it would entail [the prohibition] being consequent upon what they are consequent upon, and that is impossible. (وَمَنْ كانَ غَنِيًّا فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ): the واو is resumptive; من is a jussivising conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); كان is a defective past verb, its noun latent (mustatir), the implied form being هو; غنيا is its khabar (predicate); the clause of the protasis and its apodosis is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من. فليستعفف: the فاء links the apodosis; the lām is the lām of command, and يستعفف is jussive by it. (وَمَنْ كانَ فَقِيراً فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): conjoined to what preceded, and its i'rab has already been given; بالمعروف is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأكل. The verse divides the situation of the guardian into being rich and being poor: the rich man is content with what Allah has bestowed upon him, and the poor man eats in a fair manner, being as careful as he can out of concern for the orphan's wealth. The clause فليأكل is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is in the position of nominative as the khabar of من. (فَإِذا دَفَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوالَهُمْ فَأَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِمْ): the فاء is resumptive; إذا is an adverb of future time; the clause دفعتم إليهم أموالهم is in the position of genitive by annexation; the فاء links the apodosis; أشهدوا is an imperative verb with its agent, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivising condition; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أشهدوا. (وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ حَسِيباً): the واو is resumptive; كفى is a past verb; بالله: the باء is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and الله is the fāʿil of كفى, genitive in form by the باء; حسيبا is a tamyīz (specification).

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is a curious kind of figure called «the strength of the word for the strength of the meaning», in His words «فليستعفف», for «استعفّ» is more emphatic than «عفّ», as though he seeks an increase of chastity from himself, subduing it and holding it to the integrity that ought to be the guide of the members of society. It is known that if a word is on one pattern and is then transferred to another, larger pattern, it must contain more meaning than it contained at first, because words indicate meanings; so if words are increased, the increase necessitates an increase in meanings. This kind is used only for intensification. Of this is their saying أعشب المكان (the place became grassy), and when they saw an abundance of grass they said اعشوشب. And of it are قدر and اقتدر: the meaning of اقتدر is stronger than the meaning of قدر, and therefore the Exalted said: «فأخذناهم أخذ عزيز مقتدر». Abū Nuwās looked to this subtle point and said:
فعفوت عني عفو مقتدر ... حلت له نقم فألغاها
(You pardoned me with the pardon of one fully empowered, for whom vengeance had become lawful, yet he cancelled it.)
That is: you pardoned me with the pardon of one firmly possessed of power, whom nothing turns back from carrying out his power.

* Benefits:
(كَفى) is a past verb, according to the soundest view; the باء is added redundantly to its fāʿil, as in this verse. It may be added to the mafʿūl bihi, as in the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
كفى بجسمي نحولا أنني رجل ... لولا مخاطبتي إياك لم ترني
(Enough of thinness for my body that I am a man whom, were it not for my addressing you, you would not see.)
It is rare for the fāʿil of كفى to come without the باء, as in the saying of Suḥaym:
عميرة ودّع ان تجهّزت غاديا ... كفى الشيب والإسلام للمرء ناهيا
(Bid farewell to ʿUmayra if you have made ready to set out in the morning; grey hair and Islam suffice as a restrainer for a man.)
The باء is not added to the fāʿil of كفى or to its object when it is in the sense of أجزأ or أغنى (to suffice, to make do), as in the saying:
قليل منك يكفيني ولكن ... قليلك لا يقال له قليل
(A little from you suffices me, but your little is not called little.)
Nor [is it added to] كفى in the sense of وقى, from protection, as in the words of the Exalted: «وكفى الله المؤمنين القتال». Moreover, they criticised Abū al-Ṭayyib for adding it to the fāʿil of كفى in the sense of أجزأ or أغنى, when he said:
كفى ثعلا فخرا بأنك منهم ... ودهر لأن أمسيت من أهله أهل
(It suffices Thuʿal as glory that you are of them, and a time is worthy because you have come to be among its people.)
The critics have expatiated in explaining this line; refer to it in his Dīwān.

Strictness in the matter of the orphan:
Islamic law has been strict in the matter of the orphan and in his treatment in a fair way, while it gave the guardian a right for his managing of [the orphan's] wealth. It is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that a man said to him: "There is an orphan in my care; may I eat from his wealth?" He said: "In a fair manner, without amassing wealth and without protecting your wealth by his wealth." He said: "May I beat him?" He said: "[For] what you would beat your own child for."

dervis-irab:89-89.t:
* I'rab:
(وَدُّوا لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ كَما كَفَرُوا) A resumptive statement brought to continue describing them. (ودوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (لو) is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and it together with the verb after it forms a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the accusative because it is the object of (ودوا), i.e.: they wished for your disbelief. (كما كفروا) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e.: they wished for your disbelief like their disbelief; or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَتَكُونُونَ سَواءً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (تكونون) is conjoined to (تكفرون); the wāw is its noun and (سواء) is its khabar (predicate). (فَلا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنْهُمْ أَوْلِياءَ حَتَّى يُهاجِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) The fāʾ is al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e.: if this is their state — namely wishing for your disbelief — then do not take them as allies. (لا) is prohibitive and (تتخذوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā; (منهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تتخذوا) as its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (أولياء) is the second mafʿūl bihi. (حتى) is a particle of limit and of the genitive; (يهاجروا) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied (muḍmara) an after (حتى), and the preposition and its genitive noun [i.e. the interpreted maṣdar governed by حتى] are attached to (تتخذوا); (في سبيل الله) is attached to (يهاجروا). (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَخُذُوهُمْ وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction and (إن) is conditional; (تولوا) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis). The fāʾ connects the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis); (خذوهم) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (اقتلوهم) is conjoined to (خذوهم); (حيث) is an adverb of place, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, attached to (اقتلوهم), and the clause (وجدتموهم) is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). (وَلا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنْهُمْ وَلِيًّا وَلا نَصِيراً) The wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is prohibitive; (تتخذوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs (al-afʿāl al-khamsa); the wāw is the fāʿil; (منهم) is the first object of (تتخذوا) and (وليا) its second object; (ولا نصيرا) is conjoined to «وليا».

* Benefits:
A delightful discussion:
Al-Zamakhsharī said in the course of his commentary on this verse: «Had it [i.e. فتكونون] been put in the accusative as the answer to the wish (jawāb al-tamannī), it would have been permissible; the meaning is: they wished for your disbelief, and then for your being alike with them in the misguidance they are in and in following the religion of the forefathers.»

Abū Ḥayyān's rejoinder:
Abū Ḥayyān followed this up and said: The wish being expressed by the wording of a verb and yet having an answer is questionable. What is transmitted is only that the verb is put in the accusative in answer to a wish when it is by a particle, such as layta, and law when the two are imbued with the meaning of wishing. As for when it is by a verb, that requires attestation (samāʿ) from the Arabs. Indeed, even if it did occur, the answer-function would not be established in it, because «ودّ» which indicates the meaning of wishing has as its complement only maṣdars, not entities. So if the verb after the fāʾ is put in the accusative, it is not determined that it is a fāʾ of answer, since it may be a case of conjoining an implied maṣdar to an uttered maṣdar, so that it is of the type:
ولبس عباءة وتقر عيني ... أحبّ إليّ من لبس الشفوف
(Wearing a coarse cloak, with my eye content, is dearer to me than wearing sheer fine fabrics.)

dervis-irab:90-90.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَصِرَتْ): from al-ḥaṣar, which is narrowness and constriction. Ḥaṣira al-ṣadru ḥaṣaran (the breast became constricted), of the pattern taʿiba. Ḥaṣira al-qāriʾ: the reciter was prevented from reciting (became tongue-tied), so he is ḥaṣīr. Al-ḥaṣūr is the one who has no desire for women; ḥaṣīr al-arḍ is the surface of the earth; and al-ḥaṣīr is confinement (prison).
(السَّلَمَ): peace and surrender (al-istislām) [Translator's note: the source writes الاستلام, apparently for الاستسلام].

* I'rab:
(إِلَّا الَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ إِلى قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثاقٌ) (إلا) is a particle of exception, and (الذين) is excepted from the pronoun in (خذوهم) and (اقتلوهم). The clause (يصلون إلى قوم), i.e. who are connected to them by kinship, has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (إلى قوم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يصلون). (بينكم) is an adverb of place attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), (بينهم) is an adverb conjoined to the adverb before it, and (ميثاق) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of (قوم). The clause of exception is circumstantial. (أَوْ جاؤُكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ أَنْ يُقاتِلُوكُمْ أَوْ يُقاتِلُوا قَوْمَهُمْ) (أو) is a conjunction joining to (يصلون), falling within the scope of the ṣila; it is also said that it is conjoined to the adjective of (قوم), but the first view is more apparent. The clause «حصرت صدورهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) with "qad" understood, or without understanding it; further explanation of it will come in the section of Benefits. (أن يقاتلوكم) is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: from fighting you, and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (حصرت). You may also make the interpreted maṣdar a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (أو يقاتلوا قومهم) is conjoined to (يقاتلوكم), and (قومهم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَسَلَّطَهُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ) The wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to except this last group from the ruling of seizing and killing, and to include them among those under covenant. (لو) is conditional, and (شاء الله) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the lām connects the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis), and the clause (لسلطهم عليكم) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (فَلَقاتَلُوكُمْ فَإِنِ اعْتَزَلُوكُمْ فَلَمْ يُقاتِلُوكُمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and (لقاتلوكم) is conjoined to (سلطكم) [Translator's note: so in the source, i.e. سلطهم], so it serves as a tawkīd (emphasis) of the apodosis, or as a badal (substitute) from the first.
A discussion of this lām will come in the section of Benefits. (فإن): the fāʾ is resumptive and (إن) conditional; (اعتزلوكم) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, in the position of the jussive as the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (لم يقاتلوكم) is conjoined to (اعتزلوكم). (وَأَلْقَوْا إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلَمَ) is likewise conjoined. (فَما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سَبِيلًا) The fāʾ connects the apodosis and (ما) is negating; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (جعل) is a past verb that puts two objects in the accusative; (الله) is the fāʿil; (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted first mafʿūl bihi; (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and (سبيلا) is the second mafʿūl bihi.

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām spoke about this verse and produced something delightful, saying: As for His saying: «أو جاءوكم حصرت صدورهم», the majority held that «حصرت صدورهم» is an informative (khabariyya) clause. Then they differed. A group, among them al-Akhfash, said:
it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «جاء» with «قد» implied. Know that implying «قد» is obligatory according to the Basrans: they say that when a past-tense clause occurs as a ḥāl it must be joined with qad, either overt or implied (muqaddar). As for al-Akhfash, he does not consider it obligatory with the past verb when it occurs as a ḥāl; he says that the past-tense clause occurs as a ḥāl and is joined with «قد» if it is present, and if it is not present it needs no implied form.
This is supported by the reading of al-Ḥasan: «حصرة صدورهم», i.e. in the state of their being ḥaṣira, that is, constricted. Others said: it is an adjective, and so needs no implying of «قد».
Then these differed. It was said: the thing described is an omitted accusative, i.e.: "a people (qawman) whose breasts are constricted"; they held that implying a noun is easier than implying a particle.
And it was said: it is a mentioned genitive, namely «قوم» mentioned earlier, so there is no implying at all, and what lies between them is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ). This is supported by the fact that it was read with «أو» dropped; on that basis «جاءوكم» is an adjective of (قوم) and «حصرت» is a second adjective.
And it was said: it is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from «جاءوكم», because the coming includes the constriction; but this is far-fetched, because the constriction is an attribute of those coming.
Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Mubarrad said: the clause is performative (inshāʾiyya), its meaning being a supplication, like "may their hands be fettered", so it is resumptive. This was rejected on the ground that praying against them that their hearts be too constricted to fight their own people is not sound. It was answered that what is meant is praying against them that they be deprived of the capacity to fight altogether, in contempt of them.

A discussion of the lām in «ولقاتلوكم»:
Ibn ʿAṭiyya named this lām "the lām of correspondence and pairing" (lām al-muḥādhāh wa-l-izdiwāj), because it is in the position of the first; had there been no first, you would say: لقاتلوكم [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended form is presumably قاتلوكم without the lām]. Abū Ḥayyān said in comment on that: «Calling this lām the lām of correspondence and pairing is a strange naming; I have not seen it except in the expression of this man and the expression of Makkī before him.»

Comment on this discussion:
I say: there is no benefit beneath this discussion, which leads the student astray and avails nothing. I have pointed to this in the section of I'rab: it is no more than an emphasis of the apodosis, so it belongs to the category of repetition and substitution. We have only cited it for familiarisation, and so that the student may be safe from being deceived by the misleading name when he comes across it in their i'rab.

dervis-irab:91-91.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أُرْكِسُوا فِيها): they were overturned in it in the worst way. It has already been mentioned.
(ثَقِفْتُمُوهُمْ): thaqifa al-shayʾa thaqfan, of the pattern taʿiba: he took it. Thaqiftu al-rajula fī al-ḥarb: I caught up with the man in war; thaqiftuhu: I overcame him; thaqiftu al-ḥadītha:
I understood the speech quickly. Al-tathqīf originally means straightening crooked spears and reeds and making them even. From this meaning arose tathqīf al-ghulām, i.e. refining the boy and straightening his conduct; then al-thaqf came to mean caution and quickness of understanding. Finally the meaning was renewed in our age and became specific to learning and culture (al-thaqāfa) in knowledge. On this basis we observe the development of the language in every Arab country, just as the sons of every generation in every land of mankind have seen how their language rose with their rise and declined with their decline.

The living development of language:
Thus there is no social event or scientific or political awakening that is not accompanied by a development in the language or in meanings or in both together — we mean in the creation of new words for certain meanings, or the creation of new meanings for certain words, or in all of that. No one acquainted with the history of the Arabs and their literature is unaware of the linguistic revolution that Islam, for example, brought about alongside the religious, social and intellectual revolution.
Living examples of this living development will come to us in this wondrous Book.
From this starting point the necessity of this book for our developing youth becomes clear, so that in its light they may see the secrets of what they gather, and by its glow perceive the meaning of movement in the minds of those who went before; thereby the linguistic mind continues on the path of developing movement instead of stagnating in the stillness of material that was once among the products of the moving linguistic mind.

* I'rab:
(سَتَجِدُونَ آخَرِينَ يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَأْمَنُوكُمْ) A resumptive statement brought to establish the state of another group of the hypocrites, other than those alluded to before. The sīn is for continuous future; a delightful discussion of it will come in the section of Benefits.
(تجدون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); (آخرين) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause (يريدون) is an adjective of (آخرين); (أن) and what falls within its scope form an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) that is the object of (يريدون). (وَيَأْمَنُوا قَوْمَهُمْ) is conjoined to what precedes. (كُلَّما رُدُّوا إِلَى الْفِتْنَةِ أُرْكِسُوا فِيها) (كلما) is an adverb of time containing the meaning of condition; its i'rab has already been given. The clause (ردوا إلى الفتنة) is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), or has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī); the wāw is a nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The clause (أركسوا فيها) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, and (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أركسوا). (فَإِنْ لَمْ يَعْتَزِلُوكُمْ وَيُلْقُوا إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلَمَ) The fāʾ is resumptive and (إن) conditional; (لم) is a particle of negation, of conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and of the jussive; (يعتزلوكم) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم), and it is in the position of the jussive as the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (ويلقوا إليكم السلم) is conjoined to it. (فَخُذُوهُمْ وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ حَيْثُ ثَقِفْتُمُوهُمْ) The fāʾ connects the apodosis, and the clause (خذوهم) is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis); (اقتلوهم) is conjoined to (خذوهم); (حيث) is an adverb of place, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, attached to (اقتلوهم), and the clause (ثقفتموهم) is in the position of the genitive by annexation. (وَأُولئِكُمْ جَعَلْنا لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطاناً مُبِيناً) The wāw is a conjunction; (أولئكم) is a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (جعلنا) is a khabar (predicate); (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as the first mafʿūl bihi; (عليهم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (سلطانا) is the second mafʿūl bihi and (مبينا) an adjective.

* Benefits:
An important discussion of the sīn:
The sīn is a particle that enters upon the imperfect verb and makes it purely future and continuous. The sīn was brought here as an indication that their trifling with the believers is a continuing matter, even though it had taken place in the past. That is because men of the disbelievers, when they came to Medina, would embrace Islam so that [the Muslims] would not fight them, and when they came to their own people they would disbelieve.
So the Lord, Glorified and Exalted, brought the sīn as an indication that this state of theirs is a continuing habit of theirs and that they had not abandoned it, even though it had occurred in the past.
Ibn Hishām claimed that the continuity is derived only from the imperfect verb, just as you say:
"So-and-so entertains guests and does good deeds", meaning that this is his custom; and that the sīn conveys the future, since continuity can only be in the future. Al-Zamakhsharī claimed that when it enters upon a verb that is loved or disliked, it conveys that it will occur without fail; and I have not seen anyone who understood the reasoning for that. Its reasoning is that it conveys the promise of the verb's occurrence, so its entering upon what conveys a promise or a threat requires emphasising it and confirming its meaning, because it is information upon information, and the object [of both] is one.

dervis-irab:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(لِلرِّجالِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوالِدانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ): resumptive speech introduced to refute the practice of the Jāhiliyya of not giving inheritance to women and young children. للرجال is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); نصيب is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); مما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of نصيب; the clause ترك الوالدان is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; الأقربون is conjoined to الوالدان. (وَلِلنِّساءِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوالِدانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ): conjoined to what preceded. (مِمَّا قَلَّ مِنْهُ أَوْ كَثُرَ نَصِيباً مَفْرُوضاً): the preposition and its genitive noun are a badal (substitute) of the preceding «مما»; the clause is the ṣila; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قلّ; أو كثر is conjoined to قلّ. نصيبا مفروضا may be parsed as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it stands in its place, the implied sense being "a giving"; it may also be parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «قلّ», i.e. of what he left, little or much. Al-Zamakhsharī chose to make it accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) through an omitted verb meaning "I mean a share", but there is no need for that.

dervis-irab:8-9.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا حَضَرَ الْقِسْمَةَ أُولُوا الْقُرْبى وَالْيَتامى وَالْمَساكِينُ): the واو is resumptive; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause حضر القسمة is in the position of genitive by annexation; القسمة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أولو القربى is the fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the واو because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural; اليتامى and المساكين are conjoined to أولو القربى. (فَارْزُقُوهُمْ مِنْهُ وَقُولُوا لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفاً): the فاء links the apodosis of إذا; ارزقوهم is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivising condition; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) قولوا [Translator's note: so in the source; منه evidently belongs with ارزقوهم]; قولا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and معروفا an adjective. (وَلْيَخْشَ الَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعافاً): the واو is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; يخش is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām; الذين is a relative noun, the fāʿil; لو is conditional; تركوا is a verb with its agent; من خلفهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تركوا; ذرية is a mafʿūl bihi and ضعافا an adjective. (خافُوا عَلَيْهِمْ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivising condition; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خافوا; the object of خافوا is omitted, its implied form being "being lost and wandering"; more on it will come in the section of Rhetoric. (فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ): the فاء is causal, because fearing [Allah] (التقوى) is caused by the fear which is dread; the lām is the lām of command; يتقوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām; the واو is the fāʿil and الله the mafʿūl bihi. (وَلْيَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيداً): the clause is conjoined to فليتقوا; قولا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq and سديدا an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is the device of ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf (concision by omission), here in the omission of the object of خافوا, so that the mind may go every way in supplying it, and may display ingenuity in picturing the fear of the inevitable fate to which the affair of the weak ones comes in this life. You may supply it with the like of being lost, wandering, and being scattered in the paths of life and its branching ways, without a guardian to take care of them or a manager to manage their affairs. The poet glanced at the sky of this meaning in his delightful saying, excusing himself for fear and for staying behind, giving his daughters as the reason:
لقد زاد الحياة إليّ حبا ... بناتي إنهنّ من الضعاف
أحاذر أن يرين البؤس بعدي ... وأن يشربن رنقا غير صاف
وأن يعرين إن كسي الجواري ... فتنبو العين عن كرم عجاف
ولولاهن قد سوّيت مهري ... وفي الرحمن للضعفاء كاف
(My daughters have made life dearer to me, for they are among the weak. I fear they will see misery after me, and drink turbid, unclear water, and go naked when other girls are clothed, so that the eye turns away from noble [girls] grown lean. Were it not for them I would have saddled my colt — and in the Most Merciful there is sufficiency for the weak.)
Moreover, the omission of the direct object from speech has subtleties and wonders, as in our saying: "So-and-so loosens and binds, ratifies and annuls, harms and benefits." The basis in that is establishing the meaning intended in the mind for the thing absolutely.

* Benefits:
The view of the author of al-Mughnī and a discussion of it:
There has been much disagreement about this «لو». We shall cite the view of the author of al-Mughnī on the i'rab of this verse, then discuss it; that is not without enjoyment and benefit. He said: «The second category of «لو» is that it be a particle of condition in the future, except that it does not make jussive, as in the saying of Tawba ibn al-Ḥumayyir about Laylā al-Akhyaliyya:
ولو أن ليلى الأخيلية سلّمت ... عليّ ودوني جندل وصفائح
لسلّمت تسليم البشاشة أو زقا ... إليها صدى من جانب الأرض صائح
(If Laylā al-Akhyaliyya were to greet me while rocks and slabs lie over me, I would return the greeting of cheerfulness, or an owl-spirit would cry out to her from a side of the earth.)
and the words of the Exalted: «وليخش الذين ...» the verse; i.e. let those fear who, if they were on the verge of and close to leaving... We have interpreted leaving as being on the verge of leaving only because the address is to the guardians [of the will], and it is directed to them only before leaving, because after it they are dead.» This is what he said in al-Mughnī. The interpretation mentioned is not restricted to the address being to the guardians; rather it holds even if we say it is to the heirs or to those sitting with the sick man as well. In that case the mention of the guardians is not for exclusion but is limiting oneself to one of the meanings. The author of al-Kashshāf indicated that «تركوا» must be taken as being on the verge, not for what the author of al-Mughnī mentioned, but so that خافوا may properly occur as the apodosis, because fear is absent after death, so no fear can arise after leaving. If you say: what is the meaning of «لو تركوا» and its apodosis occurring as the ṣila of الذين? I say: its meaning is: let those fear whose description and state is that, if they were on the verge of leaving behind them offspring — and that is when death is upon them — they would fear for them being lost after them, because of the departure of their guardian and provider.

dervis-irab:10-10.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوالَ الْيَتامى ظُلْماً): resumptive speech introduced to forbid the wronging of orphans by guardians and executors. إن and its noun; the clause يأكلون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; أموال اليتامى is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ظلما is a ḥāl (circumstantial) to be interpreted [as a derived form], i.e. being wrongdoers. You may parse it as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the conditions for the accusative being fulfilled. You may also parse it as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) explaining the kind of eating, i.e. an eating of wrongdoing. (إِنَّما يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ ناراً وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيراً): إنما is the restraining [ما] and the restrained [إن], with no governing effect; يأكلون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the واو is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the first إن; في بطونهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يأكلون, or to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «نارا» and was then put first; نارا is a mafʿūl bihi; سيصلون is conjoined to يأكلون; سعيرا is a mafʿūl bihi.

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains a beautiful embodiment that appears in two of the devices of bayān:
1- Prolixity (ishāb) in their saying «في بطونهم»: He mentioned the bellies, because eating settles only in them, embodying the hideousness of the crime committed by eating the orphan's wealth. Like it is «قد بدت البغضاء من أفواههم», i.e. they mouthed it and said it with full mouths.
2- Majāz mursal (metonymic trope) in the eating of fire, the relation being causality: fire is not eaten; rather what is eaten is what causes it and leads to it, which is the orphan's wealth.
3- «يأكلون» came in the imperfect without the sīn of the future, and سيصلون with the sīn, because since the word «نارا» was unrestricted, it was restricted in His words «سعيرا», as that is the blazing embers.
4- Taʿrīḍ (allusion): by mentioning the bellies He alluded to their baseness and the lowliness of their state, which is the contemptibility of their souls [Translator's note: the source reads «وهو أن أنفسهم», evidently for «هوان أنفسهم»], and the Arabs held that to be blameworthy. Do you not see how al-Ḥuṭayʾa contented himself in his satire with this much, hinting at it, in his saying:
دع المكارم لا ترحل لبغيتها ... واقعد فإنك أنت الطاعم الكاسي
(Leave noble deeds — do not set out in quest of them; sit, for you are the one who is fed and clothed.)
i.e. the one fed and the one clothed.
[Translator's note: the source announces two devices but lists four.]

dervis-irab:92-92.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الدية): it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); then it was applied to the wealth taken for killing (blood-money). One says: wadā, yadī, diyatan, like washā, yashī, shiyatan and washyan; the fāʾ (first radical) of the word was dropped.

* I'rab:
(وَما كانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أَنْ يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِناً إِلَّا خَطَأً) A resumptive statement brought to establish the rulings on killing. The wāw is resumptive; (ما) is negating, and here it has the sense of a prohibition entailing unlawfulness. (كان) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; (لمؤمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (كان); (أن يقتل مؤمنا) is an interpreted maṣdar, the postponed noun of (كان). (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). As for (خطأ), it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) interpreted as a derived word, i.e.:
"erring"; or accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: except by error; or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) by way of description, i.e.: an erroneous killing; or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). Al-Zamakhsharī put this last before the other views, saying: «If you ask: by what is خطأ accusative? I say: by its being an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu), i.e.: it is not proper for him to kill him for any reason whatsoever except for error alone.»
In my view the views are equal; further discussion of it will come in the section of Benefits. (وَمَنْ قَتَلَ مُؤْمِناً خَطَأً فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (قتل) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (مؤمنا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the i'rab of (خطأ) has already been discussed. (فتحرير): the fāʾ connects the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis), and (تحرير) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e.: "then upon him is the freeing of a slave" — and this is better and more fitting than making it the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: "then what is obligatory is the freeing of a slave". (مؤمنة) is an adjective of (رقبة). The nominal clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (وَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلى أَهْلِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَصَّدَّقُوا) The wāw is a conjunction, and (دية) is conjoined to (تحرير رقبة); (مسلمة) is an adjective, and (إلى أهله) is attached to (مسلّمة). (إلا أن يصدقوا) is an exception from the most general of states or the most general of times, i.e.: except in the state of giving charity — so it is a ḥāl — or "when they give in charity", so it is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (مسلمة). An expanded treatment of this will come in the section of Benefits. It has also been said that it is a disjoined exception (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ). (فَإِنْ كانَ مِنْ قَوْمٍ عَدُوٍّ لَكُمْ) The fāʾ is resumptive and (إن) is a conditional jussive particle; (كان) is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, and the noun of (كان) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa"; (من قوم) is attached to an omitted khabar of (كان); (عدو) is an adjective of (قوم), and (لكم) is attached to an omitted adjective of (عدو). (وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ) The wāw is circumstantial; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (مؤمن) a khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (تحرير) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e.: "then upon him is the freeing of a slave"; its i'rab has already been given. (وَإِنْ كانَ مِنْ قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثاقٌ) The wāw is a conjunction and (إن) conditional; (كان) and its latent noun; (من قوم) is its khabar; (بينكم) is an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar, (بينهم) is conjoined to (بينكم), and (ميثاق) is a postponed mubtadaʾ. (فَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلى أَهْلِهِ) The fāʾ is connective; (دية) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e.: "then upon him is blood-money", and the reverse is also permissible, as already stated. (مسلمة) is an adjective, and (إلى أهله) is attached to (مسلمة). (وَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ) is conjoined to what precedes. (فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتابِعَيْنِ) The fāʾ is resumptive; (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ; (لم يجد) is in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ connects the apodosis; (صيام) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, or the reverse; the clause (فصيام) is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; (شهرين) is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct) and (متتابعين) an adjective; and the protasis with its apodosis is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «من». (تَوْبَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً) (توبة) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e.: He legislated that for you as a mercy from Him and a means of repentance. It may also be accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e.: He turned to you in repentance (tāba ʿalaykum tawbatan). (من الله) is an adjective. The wāw is resumptive; (كان) and its noun, and (عليما حكيما) are its two khabars.

* Benefits:
1- On (خطأ):
I said in the I'rab that it is permissible to parse (خطأ) as a disjoined exception (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ) [Translator's note: the I'rab section above does not in fact list this option for خطأ; it mentions the disjoined exception only for «إلا أن يصدقوا»], because it is not of [the genus of] the first, and error does not fall under legal obligation (taklīf).
The meaning is: but if he kills by error, then its ruling is such-and-such. It is a fine parsing. Abū al-Baqāʾ and Abū Ḥayyān inclined to this parsing, and it is also what Sībawayh, al-Zajjāj and al-Ṭabarī chose. It belongs to the disjoined exception, which must be in the accusative, and which the people of Arabic call munqaṭiʿ. From it is the saying of Jarīr:
من البيض لم تظعن بعيدا ولم تطأ ... على الأرض إلا ريط برد مرحّل
(One of the fair women, who has not journeyed far, and has not trodden upon the ground except [upon] the hem of an embroidered cloak.)
He means: she has not trodden upon the ground except that she treads on the train of the cloak — and the train of the cloak is not part of the ground.

2- On «إلا أن يصدقوا»:
I said in the I'rab that it is permissible to make «أن يصدقوا» excepted from the most general of times, so that it is an adverb (ẓarf). Abū Ḥayyān considered this interpretation far-fetched, saying: «As for making an and what follows it an adverb, that is not permissible. The grammarians stated this explicitly and forbade saying «أجيئك أن يصيح الديك» (I will come to you that the cock crows) meaning the time of the cock's crowing. As for forming from it a maṣdar that would be in the place of a ḥāl, they likewise stated explicitly that it is not permissible. Sībawayh said, regarding the Arabs' saying «أنت الرجل أن تنازل وتخاصم» (you are the man to fight and dispute), in the sense of "you are the man for fighting and disputing", that the accusative is as an object of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi), because the future cannot be a ḥāl. So according to what we have established, its being a disjoined exception is the correct view.»

dervis-irab:93-93.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِناً مُتَعَمِّداً فَجَزاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ خالِداً فِيها) The wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to threaten the killer and to declare him criminal. (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يقتل) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (مؤمنا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (متعمدا) a ḥāl (circumstantial). (فجزاؤه): the fāʾ connects the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis); (جزاؤه) is a mubtadaʾ and (جهنم) its khabar (predicate), or the reverse; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (خالدا) is a ḥāl, and (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خالدا». (وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَلَعَنَهُ) The wāw conjoins to something implied (muqaddar) that is indispensable for the speech to cohere, and this implied element is indicated by the conditional sentence, i.e.: Allah has ruled that his recompense is that, and He is angry with him. (وَأَعَدَّ لَهُ عَذاباً عَظِيماً) is likewise conjoined.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse is the device of murāʿāt al-naẓīr (observing the congruent), which has been discussed before: it is that the speaker brings what suits the content. This verse is replete with words denoting anger, threat, menace, thunder and lightning, to indicate that the crime of killing is among the greatest of crimes and the most extreme in evil, because of the destruction of the edifice of society that results from it. How beautiful is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ in this regard: «This human being is the building of Allah; accursed is he who destroys His building.»

dervis-irab:94-94.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السَّلامَ), and al-salam with fatḥa on the sīn and the lām: greeting and surrender. It has been read with both.
(ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ): you travelled in it for trade or a military expedition.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) Its i'rab has already been given. (إِذا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَتَبَيَّنُوا) A resumptive statement brought to warn against rushing into killing. (إذا) is an adverb of future time (ẓarf) containing the meaning of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis; the clause (ضربتم) is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); (في سبيل الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ضربتم). The fāʾ connects the apodosis of (إذا); (تبينوا) is an imperative verb and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَلا تَقُولُوا لِمَنْ أَلْقى إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلامَ: لَسْتَ مُؤْمِناً) The wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is prohibitive; (تقولوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and the wāw is the fāʿil; (لمن) is attached to (تقولوا); the clause (ألقى إليكم السلام) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (إليكم) is attached to (ألقى), and (السلام) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «لست مؤمنا» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying), and (مؤمنا) is the khabar (predicate) of (لست). (تَبْتَغُونَ عَرَضَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of (تقولوا), i.e.: do not say that statement seeking booty and transient goods. (فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَغانِمُ كَثِيرَةٌ) The fāʾ gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) for the prohibition, and the clause has no grammatical position; (عند الله) is an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (مغانم) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) and (كثيرة) an adjective. (كَذلِكَ كُنْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَمَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ) The clause is resumptive, brought to liken their present state to the state they had been in. (كذلك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar of (كنتم); or the nominal kāf alone is the fronted khabar of (كنتم) and (ذلك) is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). (من) is a preposition, and (قبل) is an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فمنّ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the clause (منّ الله) is conjoined to (كنتم); (عليكم) is attached to «منّ». (فَتَبَيَّنُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيراً) The grammarians in general made it a conjunction joining to the first (تبينوا), the command to ascertain being repeated for emphasis. In my view the fāʾ is al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), and there is no emphasis there, because the first command is specific to those whom you kill, while the second command is general, as though it establishes a comprehensive ruling, i.e.: if you know this and grasp its consequences, then ascertain.
(إن الله): (إن) and its noun; the clause of (كان) and what follows it is its khabar, and the clause is for giving the reason. (خبيرا) is the khabar of (كان); the clause (تعملون) has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of (ما); and (بما) is attached to «خبيرا».

dervis-irab:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي أَوْلادِكُمْ): resumptive speech introduced to begin detailing the rulings of inheritance given in summary in His words: «للرجال نصيب». يوصيكم is an imperfect verb; the كاف is its fronted object and الله its postponed fāʿil (agent); في أولادكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يوصيكم. (لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ): a resumptive clause introduced to explain the injunction. للذكر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); مثل is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted, postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "a share like". So the clause is as if explaining the first, and it is in the position of accusative as the speech quoted by يوصيكم, because it has the sense of saying. The male is preferred with this advantage because he is the one responsible for providing, and because the female will turn, by virtue of the task entrusted to her, to managing the affairs of the house and caring for and raising the children; so that required making his share of the inheritance ample.
