(فَإِنْ كُنَّ نِساءً فَوْقَ اثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثا ما تَرَكَ): the فاء is of ramification (tafrīʿiyya), and the clause after it has no grammatical position because it is like a resumptive and causal clause; إن is conditional; كنّ is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the nūn is its noun and نساء its khabar; فوق is an adverb of place attached to an omitted adjective of نساء, i.e. exceeding two; it may also be a second khabar of كان. فلهن: the فاء links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); لهن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; ثلثا is the postponed mubtadaʾ, the sign of its nominative being the alif because it is dual; ما is a relative noun in the position of genitive by annexation; the clause ترك is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause فلهن ثلثا is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (وَإِنْ كانَتْ واحِدَةً فَلَهَا النِّصْفُ): the واو is conjunctive; إن is conditional; كانت is a defective past verb, the تاء being the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis; its noun is latent (mustatir), the implied form being هي, i.e. the [female] child; واحدة is the khabar of كانت; the فاء links the apodosis; لها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; النصف is the postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (وَلِأَبَوَيْهِ لِكُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِنْ كانَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ): the واو is conjunctive, joining [this] to what preceded to begin the inheritance of ascendants. لأبويه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; لكل واحد is a preposition and its genitive noun; the apparent sense of the speech suggests that they are a badal (substitute) with repetition of the preposition, and this is what most parsers stated, al-Zamakhsharī at their head. He supported this substitution by saying: «Had it been said "ولأبويه السدس", the apparent sense would be that they share in it; and had it been said "ولأبويه السدسان", it would suggest dividing the two sixths between them equally or otherwise. If you say: why was it not said "ولكل واحد من أبويه السدس"? And what benefit is there in mentioning the two parents first and then substituting for them? I say: because in substitution and detailing after summarising there is emphasis and strengthening, like what you see in combining the thing explained with the explanation.» This is what al-Zamakhsharī said, and all the parsers and exegetes have transmitted it word for word; but there is a criticism of this i'rab, which you will see in the section of Benefits. منهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of واحد; السدس is the postponed mubtadaʾ; مما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause ترك is the ṣila; إن is conditional; كان له ولد: كان with its fronted khabar and postponed noun; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then to each one [is the sixth]"; and the conditional clause is resumptive. (فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَوَرِثَهُ أَبَواهُ): the فاء is resumptive; إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; يكن is a defective imperfect verb, jussive; له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; ولد is its postponed noun; ورثه is conjoined to لم يكن; the هاء is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and أبواه the fāʿil. (فَلِأُمِّهِ الثُّلُثُ): the فاء links the apodosis; لأمه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; الثلث is the postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (فَإِنْ كانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ فَلِأُمِّهِ السُّدُسُ): conjoined to what preceded. (مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي بِها أَوْ دَيْنٍ): the words of the parsers and exegetes have been confused about what this preposition and its genitive noun attach to. Al-Zamakhsharī attached them to the preceding division of inheritances, not to what immediately follows them alone; al-Zamakhsharī means to say that they are attached to His words «يوصيكم الله» and what comes after it. In this attachment there is noticeable confusion, and therefore Abū Ḥayyān turned from it to attaching them to an omitted verb, i.e. they are entitled to that after a bequest. In this there is an impotent laxity and an evasion of attachment, which we wish to avoid in the Noble Qur'an. Abū al-Baqāʾ attached them to an omitted ḥāl from السدس, its implied form being "being due after a bequest", and this is more confused than the first two. So it is better to attach them — as I see it — to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. the division of these shares is after a bequest. The clause يوصي — with the active and the passive, and it has been read in both — is an adjective of وصية; أو is a conjunction for permitting both things; دين is conjoined to وصية. (آباؤُكُمْ وَأَبْناؤُكُمْ لا تَدْرُونَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ لَكُمْ نَفْعاً): the clause is parenthetical between His words «من بعد وصية» and His words «فريضة من الله». آباؤكم is a mubtadaʾ and أبناؤكم is conjoined to «آباؤكم»; the clause لا تدرون is the khabar; أيهم: an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and أقرب its khabar; the clause is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of تدرون because [the verb] has been suspended (ʿulliqa) by the interrogative; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أقرب; نفعا is a tamyīz (specification). أيّ may also be parsed — as Sībawayh says — as a relative, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, being the object of تدرون, with أقرب the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "they are nearer"; as for the second object of تدرون, it is omitted. Both aspects are acceptable and admissible. (فَرِيضَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً): فريضة is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb understood from the preceding clause, from the injunction; thus they parsed it. Against this is that فريضة is not a maṣdar but a فعيلة in the sense of مفعولة; so it is better to make it an emphatic ḥāl. من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of فريضة; إن and its noun; the clause كان عليما حكيما is its khabar; the clause of إن and what falls within its scope is causal, with no grammatical position.

* Benefits:
We said that all the parsers have joined in parsing «لكل واحد» as a badal with repetition of the preposition. Against this i'rab there is an objection that must be taken into account: on this supposition it would be a substitution of a thing for the [same] thing (badal al-shayʾ min al-shayʾ), the two being like one entity, and the original form of the speech would be: "and the sixth is for his two parents, for each one of them." The requirement of limiting oneself to the substituted-for [noun] is that the two share in the sixth, as He said: «فإن كن نساء فوق اثنتين فلهن ثلثا ما ترك», which required their sharing in it. But the badal — if the first were supposed to be disregarded — would require each of them to have the sixth individually, without sharing. This contradicts the nature of this kind of badal, because in this kind it is necessary that what the substituted-for and the substitute convey be one; its only benefit is emphasis by the combination of the two nouns, nothing else, with no additional meaning. So when the difference between them is established, the substitution mentioned becomes impossible. Nor may it properly be a badal of division (badal al-taqsīm) either on this i'rab, otherwise an additional meaning in the badal would be entailed [Translator's note: the source has «يدل التقسيم», evidently for «بدل التقسيم»]. So the right course then is to supply an omitted mubtadaʾ, as though it were said: "and for his two parents is a third"; then, having mentioned their share in summary, He detailed it with His words: "and for each one of them the sixth". The omission of the mubtadaʾ is permissible because the detailing necessarily indicates it, since each of them being entitled to a sixth entails both together being entitled to a third; and Allah knows best. Nor, on this view, is it sound to make it a badal of division. Do you not see that if you said: "The house, all of it, is for three: for Zayd, for ʿUmar and for Khālid", this would be a sound badal and division, because if you deleted the substituted-for and said: "The house is for Zayd, for ʿUmar and for Khālid", without adding anything in the badal, it would be sound. But if you said: "The house is for three: Zayd has a third of it, ʿAmr has a third of it and Khālid has a third of it", it would not be sound as a badal of division, because if you deleted the substituted-for the speech would become: "The house: Zayd has a third of it, ʿUmar has a third of it and Khālid has a third of it", and this is resumptive speech, because you have added to it the meaning of distinguishing what belongs to each one of them, which the substituted-for does not give; and in the badal of a thing for the [same] thing there is no room for additional meaning.
For this reason it was necessary to parse لكل واحد as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, as though it were said: "and for his two parents is a third", i.e. for each of them the sixth. This is a point of great subtlety.

dervis-irab:95-96.t:
* Vocabulary:
(غير أولي الضرر): i.e. those with disabilities, such as blindness, lameness, chronic illness and the like.

* I'rab:
(لا يَسْتَوِي الْقاعِدُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) A resumptive statement brought to explain the disparity of the ranks of the believers according to the disparity among them in jihād. (لا) is negating, and (يستوي) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the ḍamma being implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (القاعدون) is its fāʿil (agent); (من المؤمنين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from «القاعدون» and from the pronoun concealed in it. (غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ وَالْمُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ) (غير) is a badal (substitute) from «القاعدون». We have not made it an adjective, because «غير» does not become definite through annexation, owing to its being steeped in indefiniteness, and it is not permissible for the adjective and the thing described to differ [in definiteness]. Al-Zamakhsharī paid no heed to what is established in grammar and made it an adjective. It may also be accusative as an exception, but the first is preferable, as is established in the books of grammar, because the speech is negated; and it has been read so [in the accusative].
It may also be genitive as an adjective of (المؤمنين); al-Aʿmash also read it in the genitive. A discussion of it will come in the section of Benefits. (أولي الضرر) is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct), genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. (المجاهدون) is conjoined to «القاعدون»; (في سبيل الله) is attached to «المجاهدون», and (بأموالهم) is also attached to it; (أنفسهم) is conjoined to «بأموالهم». (فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ الْمُجاهِدِينَ بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ عَلَى الْقاعِدِينَ دَرَجَةً) The clause is explicative (mufassira), having no grammatical position, explaining the non-equality between the two groups. (فضل الله) is a verb and its fāʿil; (المجاهدين) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the yāʾ; the clause (فضل الله المجاهدين) explains the non-equality between the two groups. (بأموالهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «المجاهدين», and (أنفسهم) is conjoined to (أموالهم); (على القاعدين) is attached to (فضل). (درجة) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is the instrument of preference and of raising in rank, so it is like your saying: "I struck him a whip" (ḍarabtuhu sawṭan). Some parsed it as an adverb (ẓarf), and that is not far-fetched.
Others parsed it as a ḥāl, and it then requires an implied muḍāf, i.e.:
"possessors of a degree". Some said it is a tamyīz (specification), and there is no harm in this view.
What we have chosen is the most preferable. (وَكُلًّا وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنى) The wāw is parenthetical; (كلّا) is a fronted mafʿūl bihi of «وعد», (الله) is the fāʿil, and (الحسنى) is the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is parenthetical. (وَفَضَّلَ اللَّهُ الْمُجاهِدِينَ عَلَى الْقاعِدِينَ أَجْراً عَظِيماً) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes. (أجرا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq because it is synonymous with (فضل), or because it is its instrument, along the lines of
"a degree" and "a whip"; further discussion of it will come in the section of Benefits. (عظيما) is an adjective.
(دَرَجاتٍ مِنْهُ وَمَغْفِرَةً وَرَحْمَةً) (درجات) is a badal from «أجرا»; (منه) is attached to an omitted adjective of (درجات); (مغفرة) and (رحمة) are conjoined to (درجات). Al-Zamakhsharī put them in the accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq with their verb implied, in the sense: "and He forgave them and had mercy on them with forgiveness and mercy" — and perhaps this is better, for the sake of observing congruity. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً) The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; (كان) and its noun, and (غفورا رحيما) are its two khabars (predicates); the clause is resumptive or circumstantial.

* Benefits:
What Ibn Yaʿīsh says:
Ibn Yaʿīsh said, when discussing «غير أولي الضرر»: «It has been read in the nominative, the genitive and the accusative. The nominative is as an adjective of «القاعدون»; its nominative cannot be as a badal in exception, because the implied form would then become: "None are equal except those with disability", and the meaning is not that; the meaning is only: the healthy who sit back and those who strive are not equal. The genitive is as an adjective of (المؤمنين), and the meaning is:
the healthy who sit back among the believers and those who strive are not equal — and the meaning in both is one. The accusative is as an exception.»

The grammarians between the badal and adjective analyses of (غير):
The grammarians have weighed [lit. wavered between] the badal and the adjective analyses of «غير». Whoever argued for the badal said: making «غير» an adjective requires interpretation, because «غير» does not become definite through annexation, and it is not permissible for the adjective and the thing described to differ in definiteness and indefiniteness; its interpretation is either that «القاعدون», since they are not specific individuals but the genus is meant by them, resemble the indefinite and so are described by it as the indefinite is described; or that «غير» may become definite when it occurs between two opposites. Whoever argued for the adjective said: its nominative cannot be as a badal in exception, because the implied form would then become: "the healthy who sit back and those who strive are not equal" — as Ibn Yaʿīsh said [Translator's note: so in the source; in the Ibn Yaʿīsh quotation above, the implied form that rules out the badal is "none are equal except those with disability", while "the healthy who sit back and those who strive are not equal" is given as the intended meaning]. This is one of their subtleties that indicate brilliance and keenness of mind, so reflect, and may Allah guide you.

Al-Zamakhsharī's view on the i'rab of (أجرا):
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Why are درجة, أجرا and درجات accusative? I say: His word «درجة» is accusative because it occupies the position of the single instance (al-marra) of preferring, as though it were said: He preferred them with one preference; its parallel is your saying: "he struck him a whip", in the sense: he struck him one blow.
As for أجرا, it is accusative by (فضل) because it has the sense of "He rewarded them with a reward"; and درجات and رحمة are a badal from أجرا. It is also permissible for «درجات» to be accusative in the way «درجة» is, as you say:
"he struck him whips", in the sense of blows — as though it were said: and He preferred him with preferences. And «أجرا عظيما» is accusative as a ḥāl from the indefinite noun «درجات», placed before it. And «مغفرة ورحمة» are accusative with their verb implied, in the sense: and He forgave them and had mercy on them with forgiveness and mercy.»

dervis-irab:97-99.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ ظالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ) A resumptive statement establishing the state of a group who embraced Islam but did not emigrate, and were killed on the day of Badr along with the disbelievers — although emigration (al-hijra) was a pillar or a condition in Islam; then it was abrogated after the Conquest [of Mecca]. (إن) and its noun; the clause (توفاهم الملائكة) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The origin of (توفاهم) is (تتوفاهم); one of the two tāʾs was dropped according to the established rule. Ibn Jarīr and others allowed it to be a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and that is not far-fetched. (الملائكة) is the fāʿil (agent) and (ظالمي أنفسهم) a ḥāl (circumstantial). As for the khabar (predicate) of (إن), it may be omitted, its implied form being: "Those whom the angels take [in death] perished"; or the khabar may be His saying: (قالوا فيم كنتم؟); or it may be:
(فأولئك مأواهم جهنم), the fāʾ entering the khabar redundantly (zāʾida) by likening the relative noun to a conditional noun. (قالُوا فِيمَ كُنْتُمْ؟) The pronoun in (قالوا) refers to the angels; the clause is either a khabar, as we stated before, or resumptive, explaining the omitted clause. (فيم):
(في) is a preposition, and the interrogative (ما) is in the position of the genitive by (في); its alif was dropped because the preposition entered upon it. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar of (كنتم), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying). (قالُوا كُنَّا مُسْتَضْعَفِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ) The pronoun in (قالوا) refers to those whom the angels take; the clause of saying is resumptive, and the clause (كنا مستضعفين في الأرض) is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl; (مستضعفين) is the khabar of (كنا), and (في الأرض) is attached to (مستضعفين). (قالُوا: أَلَمْ تَكُنْ أَرْضُ اللَّهِ واسِعَةً فَتُهاجِرُوا فِيها) The pronoun in (قالوا) refers to the angels, and the clause is resumptive. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī), for reproach; (لم) is a particle of negation, of conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and of the jussive; (تكن) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم»; (أرض الله) is the noun of (تكن) and (واسعة) its khabar; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl. The fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya); (تهاجروا) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied (muḍmara) an after the fāʾ of causation, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (فيها) is attached to (تهاجروا). (فَأُولئِكَ مَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ) The fāʾ is connective because of the scent of condition in the relative noun; (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (مأواهم) is a [second] mubtadaʾ, and (جهنم) is the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative. The clause (فأولئك) is either the khabar of «إن الذين», as we stated before, or resumptive.
(وَساءَتْ مَصِيراً) The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; (ساءت) is a past verb of blame (dhamm); (مصيرا) is a tamyīz (specification), and the specifically blamed (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e.: Hell. (إِلَّا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الرِّجالِ وَالنِّساءِ وَالْوِلْدانِ) (إلا) is a particle of exception, and (المستضعفين) are excepted from them because of their weakness and their inability to emigrate, so the exception is connected (muttaṣil). It has also been said:
the exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), because those from whom the exception is made are either disbelievers or sinners by staying behind while being able to emigrate, so the oppressed weak are not included among them. (من الرجال) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, and (النساء) and (الولدان) are conjoined to (الرجال). (لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًا) The clause (لا يستطيعون) is an adjective of (المستضعفين). Describing a definite noun with a clause — which is indefinite — is permitted because the definite noun here does not refer to a specific thing in itself, along the lines of the poet's saying:
ولقد أمر على اللئيم يسبني ... فمضيت ثمّت قلت: لا يعنيني
(I pass by the base man who reviles me, and I go on, then say: "He does not mean me.")
(حيلة) is the object of (يستطيعون); the clause (ولا يهتدون) is conjoined to the clause (لا يستطيعون); (سبيلا) is the object of (يهتدون), or accusative by removal of the preposition — and perhaps that is more firmly grounded in eloquence — i.e.: to a way among the various ways. (فَأُولئِكَ عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَعْفُوَ عَنْهُمْ) The fāʾ is al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), because it occurs in the apodosis of an implied condition, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, i.e.: if you want to know their fate, then those... (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (عسى) is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb, one of the verbs of hope; (الله) is the noun of (عسى), and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is its khabar; the verbal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَفُوًّا غَفُوراً) The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; (كان) and its noun, and (عفوا غفورا) are its two khabars.

dervis-irab:12-12.t:
* Vocabulary:
(كَلالَةً): maṣdar (verbal noun) of كلّ فلان, when he is neither a child nor a parent [of the deceased], i.e. he fell short (كلّ) of attaining the immediate kinship. Al-Ṭirimmāḥ said, describing the bull:
يهزّ سلاحا لم يرثه كلالة ... يشكّ به منها غموض المغابن
(He brandishes a weapon he did not inherit through distant kin, with which he pierces the hidden folds of their armpits.)
The scholars of jurisprudence and exegesis have spoken much about al-kalāla, and more will be said about this word in this sura.

* I'rab:
(وَلَكُمْ نِصْفُ ما تَرَكَ أَزْواجُكُمْ): the واو is a conjunction; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); نصف is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ما is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ترك is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; أزواجكم is the fāʿil (agent). (إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌ): إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; يكن is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and it is also the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); لهن is the fronted khabar of يكن and ولد its postponed noun; the conditional clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. (فَإِنْ كانَ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌ): the فاء is conjunctive; إن is conditional; كان with its fronted khabar and postponed noun; the clause is conjoined. (فَلَكُمُ الرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْنَ): the فاء is linking; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; الربع is the postponed mubtadaʾ; مما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause تركن is the ṣila; the clause joined with the فاء is the apodosis. (مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِينَ بِها أَوْ دَيْنٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl; وصية is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause يوصين is a naʿt (adjective) of وصية; بها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يوصين; أو is a conjunction and دين is conjoined to وصية. (وَلَهُنَّ الرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌ فَإِنْ كانَ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌ فَلَهُنَّ الثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ تُوصُونَ بِها أَوْ دَيْنٍ): the i'rab of all of this has been given before, so turn back to it. (وَإِنْ كانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلالَةً): the واو is conjunctive; إن is conditional; كان may be either defective (nāqiṣa) or complete (tāmma). If it is defective, رجل is its noun, the clause يورث, in the passive, is its khabar, and كلالة is a ḥāl. If it is complete, رجل is the fāʿil, the clause يورث is an adjective, and كلالة is a ḥāl. كلالة may also be parsed as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), its meaning then being kinship; or as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar if its meaning is inheritance, i.e. he is inherited from with an inheritance of kalāla. Some permitted it to be a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), but I do not find that acceptable. (أَوِ امْرَأَةٌ وَلَهُ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ): أو is a conjunction and امرأة is conjoined to رجل; وله: the واو is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; أخ is the postponed mubtadaʾ; أو is a conjunction and أخت is conjoined to أخ. (فَلِكُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ): the فاء is linking; لكل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; واحد is muḍāf ilayhi; منهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of واحد; السدس is the postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause joined with the فاء is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (فَإِنْ كانُوا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذلِكَ فَهُمْ شُرَكاءُ فِي الثُّلُثِ): the فاء is resumptive; إن is conditional; كانوا is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; the واو is the noun of كان and أكثر its khabar; من ذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أكثر; the فاء is linking; هم is a mubtadaʾ and شركاء a khabar; في الثلث is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شركاء. (مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصى بِها أَوْ دَيْنٍ): its i'rab has been given before, so renew your acquaintance with it. (غَيْرَ مُضَارٍّ وَصِيَّةً مِنَ اللَّهِ): غير مضار is a ḥāl from the pronoun of يوصى; وصية is an emphatic mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of يوصيكم; من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of وصية. (وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌ): the واو is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ, and عليم and حليم are its two khabars.

* Benefits:
1- A curious discussion:
Al-Shalawbīn said: it was related to me that a grammarian was asked about the i'rab of «كلالة» in the words of the Exalted: (وَإِنْ كانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلالَةً). He said: "Tell me: what is al-kalāla?" They told him: "The heirs when there is among them no father or higher, and no son or lower." He said: "Then it is a tamyīz (specification)." The explanation of his view is that the original form would be: «وإن كان رجل يرثه كلالة»; then the agent was omitted and the verb made passive, so the pronoun became nominative and latent; then كلالة was brought as a tamyīz.
Ibn Hishām's rejoinder:
Ibn Hishām replied to this grammarian, saying: «This grammarian was right in his question and wrong in his answer, for specifying by the agent after omitting it undoes the purpose for which it was omitted, and goes back on what the clause was built upon, namely folding away mention of the agent in it. For this reason there is nothing in their speech like: ضرب أخوك رجلا.» Ibn Hishām digressed, as is his habit, until he said: «The correct view in the verse is that «كلالة» is with an implied annexed noun, i.e. ذا كلالة (one of kalāla), and it is either a ḥāl from the pronoun of يورث — so «كان» is defective and يورث is the khabar, or complete and يورث is an adjective — or it is a khabar, and يورث is an adjective. Whoever explained «كلالة» as the deceased who left neither child nor parent, it is likewise a ḥāl or a khabar, but it does not need an implied omitted annexed noun. And whoever explained it as kinship, it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi.»
2- It is the custom of the Arabs, when they alternate between two nouns with أو, to refer the pronoun back to both of them together — you say: «من كان له أخ أو أخت فليصلهما» (whoever has a brother or a sister, let him keep ties with them both) — or to one of them, whichever you wish: you say «من كان له أخ أو أخت فليصله», and if you wish, «فليصلها».

dervis-irab:13-14.t:
* I'rab:
(تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ): resumptive speech introduced to explain that the preceding legislation is among the limits of Allah for His servants, so that they act by them and do not transgress them. تلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and حدود الله a khabar (predicate). (وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ): the واو is resumptive; من is a jussivising conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; يطع الله ورسوله is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); يدخله is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the هاء is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); جنات is accusative by removal of the preposition, or a second mafʿūl bihi by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause of the condition and the apodosis is in the position of nominative as the khabar.
(تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها): the clause تجري is a naʿt (adjective) of جنات; من تحتها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) تجري; الأنهار is the fāʿil (agent); خالدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial); فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خالدين. (وَذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): the واو is circumstantial or resumptive; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, الفوز a khabar and العظيم an adjective. (وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَهُ يُدْخِلْهُ ناراً خالِداً فِيها وَلَهُ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ): its i'rab has been given before, so turn back to it.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse there is a strange device called «combining the differing and the agreeing» (jamʿ al-mukhtalifa wa-l-muʾtalifa). It is defined as the speaker intending to put on a par two persons praised, or two blamed, or two of whom one is praised and the other blamed, and then afterwards aiming to give one preference over the other in a way that does not detract from the other; so for the sake of that preference he brings meanings that differ from the meanings of equality. He put in the plural the pronoun of those abiding forever in the Garden, because everyone who enters the Garden abides in it forever, or because of the differing degrees of those abiding. As for the people of the Fire, among them are those who abide forever and those who do not, from the disobedient among the believers. So the plural was permissible there and was not permissible here [Translator's note: so in the source; the wording of «هناك» and «هنا» appears reversed relative to the reasoning given]. Because those abiding forever in the Fire are a single group, whereas those abiding forever in the Gardens are ranks according to the differences of their degrees. This is among the loftiest levels of bayān. Among its beautiful examples in poetry is the saying of al-Khansāʾ, when she wanted to put her brother Ṣakhr on a par in merit with her father while observing the right of the parent; she said:
جارى أباه فأقبلا وهما ... يتعاوران ملاة الحضر
وهما وقد برزا كأنهما ... صقرآن قد حطا على وكر
حتى إذا نزت القلوب وقد لزت هناك العذر بالعذر
وعلا هتاف الناس أيهما ... قال المجيب هناك: لا أدري
برقت صحيفة وجه والده ... ومضى على غلوائه يجري
أولى فأولى أن يساويه ... لولا جلال السنّ والكبر
(He raced his father, and the two came on, taking turns with the mantle of the race; the two, when they came out, were like two falcons alighting on a nest; until, when hearts leapt and cheek-straps were pressed against cheek-straps, and the people's shouting rose — "Which of them?" — the one answering there said: "I do not know"; the page of his father's face shone forth, and he went on running in his vigour; [the son] was very near to equalling him, were it not for the majesty of age and seniority.)
She put them on a par in boldness, plunging into the depths of war, speed in running and racing in the first line; الحضر, with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, is racing and running, and الملاة, with ḍamma on the mīm, is الريطة, which is any thin garment. Then in the second line she put them on a par by making them like two swift falcons. In the third line she wanted to describe the battle [Translator's note: so in the source; the line describes the race], and how some of the cheek-pieces (عذر) [of the horses] were pressed against others, which indicates equality in running. In the fourth line the people asked which of them was the father and which the son, because of how much they resembled each other. Then in the fifth line she ended by giving preference to the father through the shining of the page of his face, i.e. his face came out of the dust before the face of his competitor, by being ahead. In the sixth line she said that the son was able to equal the father were it not for the courtesy he kept, together with dutifulness to his father and knowledge of his right; so he held back his rein and lowered the wing of his merit, in order to prefer his father in merit over himself. Like it is [the verse] of Naṣr Allāh ibn Aḥmad al-Baṣrī, known as al-Khubzʾaruzzī, who was unlettered, baked rice-bread in Basra and recited love poetry. Of that is his saying:
رأيت الهلال ووجه الحبيب ... فكانا هلالين عند النظر
فلم أدر من حيرتي فيهما ... هلال السما من هلال البشر
ولولا التّورّد في الوجنتين ... وما لاح لي من خلال الشعر
لكنت أظن الهلال الحبيب ... وكنت أظن الحبيب القمر
(I saw the crescent and the face of the beloved, and they were two crescents to the sight; in my bewilderment over them I did not know the crescent of the sky from the crescent among mankind; were it not for the rosiness of the cheeks and what gleamed to me through the hair, I would have thought the crescent the beloved, and thought the beloved the moon.)
He first put them on a par, then turned back and preferred the beloved to the crescent.
2- Between the singular and the plural:
Abū al-Suʿūd al-ʿImādī, Mufti of Constantinople, leapt in his exegesis to the summit of acuity when he determined, by a happy inspiration, that the subtle point of the singular in His words «خالدا» is that it announces that entering the abode of punishment in a state of solitude is more severe in bringing on desolation, whereas the gatherings of the Garden are among close friends and loved ones, and gathering together is more conducive to dispelling desolation.

dervis-irab:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
(وَاللَّاتِي يَأْتِينَ الْفاحِشَةَ مِنْ نِسائِكُمْ): resumptive speech introduced to begin the rulings on the adulteress. The واو is resumptive; اللاتي is a relative noun; the clause يأتين الفاحشة is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; من نسائكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَاسْتَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ أَرْبَعَةً مِنْكُمْ): the فاء is linking, because of the flavour of condition in the relative noun; for that reason it is permissible for the command to be given as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) in His words استشهدوا. You may also make the khabar omitted, i.e. "in what is recited to you is the ruling on those who...". عليهن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استشهدوا; أربعة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective). (فَإِنْ شَهِدُوا فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ فِي الْبُيُوتِ): the فاء is resumptive; إن is conditional; شهدوا is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the فاء is linking; أمسكوهن is an imperative verb, the واو being the fāʿil (agent) and the هاء the mafʿūl bihi; في البيوت is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أمسكوهن; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (حَتَّى يَتَوَفَّاهُنَّ الْمَوْتُ أَوْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لَهُنَّ سَبِيلًا): حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; يتوفاهن is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; the هاء is a mafʿūl bihi and الموت the fāʿil; the implied أن and what falls within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of genitive by حتى, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to أمسكوهن; أو is a conjunction; يجعل is an imperfect verb conjoined to «يتوفاهن»; الله is the fāʿil; لهن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «سبيلا» and was put first; سبيلا is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَالَّذانِ يَأْتِيانِها مِنْكُمْ فَآذُوهُما): the واو is a conjunction; اللذان is a mubtadaʾ, and by them He meant the adulterer and the adulteress; the clause يأتيانها is the ṣila, and the pronoun refers to الفاحشة; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the فاء is linking; آذوهما is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object, and the clause is the khabar; its like has been given before. The meaning of الإيذاء (harming) is reviling, rebuking and beating. (فَإِنْ تابا وَأَصْلَحا فَأَعْرِضُوا عَنْهُما): فإن: the فاء is resumptive and إن conditional; تابا is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; أصلحا is conjoined to «تابا»; the فاء is linking; the clause أعرضوا عنهما is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ تَوَّاباً رَحِيماً): إن and its noun; the clause of كان with its latent (mustatir) noun and its khabar is in the position of jussive as the apodosis [Translator's note: so in the source; it is evidently meant as the khabar of إن]; رحيما is the second khabar of كان.

dervis-irab:100-100.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المراغم), with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the dotted ghayn: a place to go, a stronghold, a place of movement; so it is a noun of place. It was used to convey that the emigrant rubs his people's noses in the dust, i.e. humiliates them. Al-raghm is humiliation and abasement; its origin is the nose sticking to al-raghām — with fatḥa on the rāʾ — which is dust. Raghima anfuhu raghman, of the pattern qatala:
a metonymy for humiliation, as though it stuck to the dust in abasement and humiliation. It becomes transitive with the alif, so one says: arghama Allāhu anfahu (may Allah rub his nose in the dust), and "I did it ʿalā raghmi anfihi" — with fatḥa or ḍamma on the rāʾ — i.e. I angered him; and "this is a targhīm for him", i.e. a humiliation. This is one of the idioms that run in their speech using the names of body parts without intending the parts themselves; rather, they assigned them to meanings other than the apparent ones, and the apparent sense of the names has no share in them by way of literal meaning. From this is their saying: "his speech is under my foot" and "his need is behind my back", meaning neglect and disregard. In al-Qāmūs: "al-raghm: aversion — and it is pronounced with any of the three vowels — like al-marghama; and raghimahu, like ʿalimahu and manaʿahu: he disliked it."

* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ يُهاجِرْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يَجِدْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُراغَماً كَثِيراً وَسَعَةً) A resumptive statement brought to explain the state of those who emigrate in the way of Allah. The wāw is resumptive; (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يهاجر) is an imperfect verb, the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (في سبيل الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يهاجر); (يجد) is an imperfect verb, the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis); the protasis and its apodosis are in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «من». (مراغما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), (كثيرا) an adjective, and (سعة) is conjoined to «مراغما». (وَمَنْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُهاجِراً إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ) The i'rab of its parallel has already been given; (مهاجرا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and (إلى الله ورسوله) is attached to «مهاجرا». (ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ الْمَوْتُ فَقَدْ وَقَعَ أَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ) (ثم) is a conjunction, and (يدركه) is conjoined to (يخرج); the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi, and (الموت) is the fāʿil (agent) of (يدركه). (فقد): the fāʾ connects the apodosis, and (قد) is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); the clause (وقع أجره على الله) is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من»; (على الله) is attached to (وقع). (وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً) A resumptive clause; its i'rab has already been given.

dervis-irab:101-101.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُناحٌ) A resumptive statement brought to explain the rulings on shortening the prayer. The wāw is resumptive; (إذا) is an adverb of future time (ẓarf) containing the meaning of condition; the clause (ضربتم في الأرض) is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). The fāʾ connects the apodosis of (إذا); (ليس) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (ليس), and (جناح) is its postponed noun; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (أَنْ تَقْصُرُوا مِنَ الصَّلاةِ) The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: in shortening the prayer, and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of (جناح); (من الصلاة) is attached to (تقصروا). The discussion of shortening the prayer is treated at length in the books of jurisprudence. (إِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) (إن) is conditional; (خفتم) is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and it is in the position of the jussive as the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (أن) and what falls within its scope form an interpreted maṣdar that is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (خفتم); (الذين كفروا) is the fāʿil, and the clause (كفروا) is a ṣila (relative clause). The conditional clause is resumptive, and the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: then there is no blame on you in shortening. (إِنَّ الْكافِرِينَ كانُوا لَكُمْ عَدُوًّا مُبِيناً) The clause gives the reason for the preceding permission to shorten. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (كانوا) is its khabar; the wāw is the noun of (كان); (لكم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (عدوا) is the khabar of (كان), and (مبينا) an adjective.

dervis-irab:102-102.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا كُنْتَ فِيهِمْ فَأَقَمْتَ لَهُمُ الصَّلاةَ) The wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, beginning the rulings on the prayer of fear (ṣalāt al-khawf). The address is to the Prophet ﷺ, and there is no proof in it for whoever held the view that the prayer of fear is not to be performed after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; rather, the address is comprehensive and covers every imam.
It is also permissible for the wāw to be a conjunction, so that the statement is joined to what precedes.
(إذا) is an adverb of future time (ẓarf) containing the meaning of condition; the clause (كنت) is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); the tāʾ is the noun of (كان), and (فيهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of (كنت). The pronoun refers to those travelling in the land or to those in fear; both are possible. The fāʾ is a conjunction; (أقمت) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (لهم) is attached to (أقمت); the clause is conjoined to the clause (كنت); and (الصلاة) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (فَلْتَقُمْ طائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ مَعَكَ) The fāʾ is connective; the lām is the lām of command; (تقم) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; (طائفة) is the fāʿil; (منهم) is attached to an omitted adjective; and (معك) is an adverb of place attached to (تقم). (وَلْيَأْخُذُوا أَسْلِحَتَهُمْ):
(وليأخذوا) is conjoined to (فلتقم), and (أسلحتهم) is a mafʿūl bihi. (فَإِذا سَجَدُوا فَلْيَكُونُوا مِنْ وَرائِكُمْ) The i'rab of its parallel has already been given; (من ورائكم) is attached to an omitted khabar of (فليكونوا). (وَلْتَأْتِ طائِفَةٌ أُخْرى لَمْ يُصَلُّوا فَلْيُصَلُّوا مَعَكَ) Likewise conjoined; the clause «لم يصلوا» is a second adjective of (طائفة); (فليصلوا) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and (معك) is an adverb of place attached to (فليصلوا). (وَلْيَأْخُذُوا حِذْرَهُمْ وَأَسْلِحَتَهُمْ) Likewise conjoined. (وَدَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ تَغْفُلُونَ عَنْ أَسْلِحَتِكُمْ وَأَمْتِعَتِكُمْ) The clause is resumptive, brought to stress extra caution, because the enemy supposes that the prayer is a likely occasion for laying down arms. (ود الذين) is a verb and its fāʿil; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (لو) is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), so it is a particle-relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī), and together with what follows it forms a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the accusative because it is the object of (تود) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the verse is ودّ]. The clause (تغفلون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative; (عن أسلحتكم) is attached to (تغفلون), and (أمتعتكم) is conjoined to (أسلحتكم). (فَيَمِيلُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَيْلَةً واحِدَةً) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and (يميلون) is conjoined to (تغفلون); (عليكم) is attached to (يميلون); (ميلة) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and (واحدة) an adjective. (وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ كانَ بِكُمْ أَذىً مِنْ مَطَرٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is the lā of generic negation and (جناح) its noun; (عليكم) is attached to an omitted khabar of «لا». (إن) is conditional; (كان) is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (بكم) is attached to the omitted fronted khabar of (كان), and (أذى) is its postponed noun; (من مطر) is attached to an omitted adjective of (أذى). The jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: then there is no blame on you. (أَوْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضى أَنْ تَضَعُوا أَسْلِحَتَكُمْ) (أو) is a conjunction, and (كنتم) is conjoined to (كان بكم أذى); (مرضى) is the khabar of (كنتم). (أن تضعوا) is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: in that you lay down; the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (جناح) or to an omitted adjective of it; (أسلحتكم) is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَخُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ) Likewise conjoined. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذاباً مُهِيناً) (إن) and its noun; the clause (أعد للكافرين) is its khabar; (عذابا) is the object of (أعد), and (مهينا) an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is the conjoining of the literal to the figurative, which is at the summit of eloquence and at the very threshold of fluency. The weapons are literal, and caution (al-ḥidhr) is figurative, because He meant by it one of the instruments that warriors use in their wars; therefore He combined it with the weapons in the "taking", making them both as if they were things taken. Among the delightful instances of this figure used together with the literal is the saying of Abū Tammām al-Ṭāʾī describing a band of riders:
وركب يساقون الركاب زجاجة ... من السير لم تقصد لها كفّ قاطب
(And riders who give their mounts to drink a glass of travel, for which no mixing hand was ever extended.)
The figure is in his saying «زجاجة», i.e. a drink in a glass. The meaning is: they make the mounts drunk with fatigue, so it is as if they gave them to drink a drink for which no mixing hand reached out — i.e. it is not in reality a drink that the cupbearer hands to his companion deliberately. This correspondence between the figurative and the literal is not easily grasped except by people of refined nature and delicate taste; so understand it, draw analogies from it, and may Allah protect you.

dervis-irab:103-104.t:
* I'rab:
(فَإِذا قَضَيْتُمُ الصَّلاةَ فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ قِياماً وَقُعُوداً وَعَلى جُنُوبِكُمْ) The fāʾ is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to establish what is recommended after performing the prayer of fear in the complete manner explained. (إذا) is an adverb of future time (ẓarf) containing the meaning of condition; the clause (قضيتم الصلاة) is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); the fāʾ is connective, and the clause (اذكروا الله) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (قياما) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), (قعودا) a second ḥāl, and (على جنوبكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted third ḥāl by way of conjunction. (فَإِذَا اطْمَأْنَنْتُمْ فَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ) Its i'rab has already been given, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes. (إِنَّ الصَّلاةَ كانَتْ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتاباً مَوْقُوتاً) The clause gives the reason for what came before. (إن) and its noun; the clause (كانت) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); (على المؤمنين) is attached to «موقوتا»; (كتابا) is the khabar of (كانت), and (موقوتا) an adjective, i.e.: delimited by times. (وَلا تَهِنُوا فِي ابْتِغاءِ الْقَوْمِ) The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; (لا) is prohibitive, and (تهنوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لا»; (في ابتغاء القوم) is attached to (تهنوا). (إِنْ تَكُونُوا تَأْلَمُونَ فَإِنَّهُمْ يَأْلَمُونَ كَما تَأْلَمُونَ) (إن) is a conditional jussive particle; (تكونوا) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); the wāw is the noun of (كان), and the clause (تألمون) is its khabar. The conditional clause has no grammatical position because it gives the reason for the prohibition. (فإنهم): the fāʾ connects the apodosis; (إن) and its noun, and the clause (يألمون) is its khabar; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis). (كما تألمون) is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or as a ḥāl; parallels of it have already come. (وَتَرْجُونَ مِنَ اللَّهِ ما لا يَرْجُونَ) is conjoined to the clause (يألمون); (ما) is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (ترجون), and the clause (لا يرجون) has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila (relative clause). (وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً) Its i'rab has been given many times.

dervis-irab:105-106.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ بِالْحَقِّ) A resumptive statement warning against haste in judgement, and it is general. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (أنزلنا) is its khabar (predicate); (إليك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزلنا); (الكتاب) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (بالحق) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (لِتَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ بِما أَراكَ اللَّهُ) The lām is for giving the reason (taʿlīl), and (تحكم) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun — the lām of reason and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the implied an and the verb (تحكم) — are attached to (أنزلنا). (بين الناس) is an adverb attached to (تحكم), and (بما) is attached to (تحكم). The clause (أراك الله) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The "showing" (al-irāʾa) here has the sense of knowing and knowledge, so the kāf is its first object and the second is omitted, being the omitted resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid), i.e.: "by what Allah has shown it to you" (bimā arākahu Allāh). (وَلا تَكُنْ لِلْخائِنِينَ خَصِيماً) The wāw is a conjunction and (لا) prohibitive; (تكن) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا); the noun of (تكن) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; (للخائنين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خصيما), and (خصيما) is its khabar. (وَاسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً)
is conjoined to what precedes; the i'rab of its parallels has already been given.

dervis-irab:107-108.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَخْتانُونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ): they cause suspicion to themselves and betray themselves by sins.
(يَسْتَخْفُونَ): they conceal themselves.
(يُبَيِّتُونَ): they plot the matter by night. It is hardly used except for evil. The wording of al-Mubarrad in his al-Kāmil:
«One says: bayyata fulān such-and-such, when he did it by night; and in the Qur'an:
«وإذ يبيتون ما لا يرضى من القول», i.e. they turned that over among themselves by night.»

* I'rab:
(وَلا تُجادِلْ عَنِ الَّذِينَ يَخْتانُونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction and (لا) prohibitive; (تجادل) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and the fāʿil (agent) is "anta"; (عن الذين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تجادل); the clause (يختانون أنفسهم) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ مَنْ كانَ خَوَّاناً أَثِيماً) This gives the reason for the prohibition. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يحب) is its khabar (predicate); (من) is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (كان) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (خوانا) is the khabar of (كان) and (أثيما) an adjective — or they are two khabars of (كان). (يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَلا يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَهُوَ مَعَهُمْ) The clause is resumptive, brought merely to report that they seek concealment; or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «من», taking it as a relative noun. The clause (ولا يستخفون من الله) is conjoined to the first. The wāw is circumstantial; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the adverb (معهم) is attached to an omitted khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl. (إِذْ يُبَيِّتُونَ ما لا يَرْضى مِنَ الْقَوْلِ) (إذ) is an adverb (ẓarf) for narrating a past state; the clause (يبيتون) is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); (ما) is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi; the clause (لا يرضى) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (من القول) is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطاً) The i'rab of its parallels has been given many times.

* Rhetoric:
1- Hyperbole (al-mubālagha) in His saying «خوانا أثيما»: He used two of the intensive patterns (ṣiyagh al-mubālagha), because Allah knew of Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq — who stole a coat of mail from a neighbour of his and deposited it with a Jew — excess in treachery and indulgence in sins.
2- The figurative usage (majāz) in "concealing oneself" (al-istikhfāʾ): concealing oneself from Allah is impossible, because Allah knows what is open and what is hidden; so it is a figure for shame (al-ḥayāʾ).

dervis-irab:109-109.t:
* I'rab:
(ها أَنْتُمْ هؤُلاءِ جادَلْتُمْ عَنْهُمْ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) A resumptive statement brought to rebuke the people of Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq — the Banū Ẓafar of the Anṣār, who tried to cover up his crime and his theft. (ها) is for drawing attention (tanbīh); (أنتم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (هؤلاء) its khabar (predicate), and the clause (جادلتم) is a second khabar. Some parsed (هؤلاء) as one addressed in the vocative with the vocative particle omitted, the vocative clause being parenthetical — and that is correct. (عنهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جادلتم); (في الحياة) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and (الدنيا) is an adjective. (فَمَنْ يُجادِلُ اللَّهَ عَنْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (من) is an interrogative noun of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يجادل الله) is a khabar; (عنهم) is attached to (يجادل), and (يوم القيامة) is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl. (أَمْ مَنْ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكِيلًا) (أم) is a conjunction; (من) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; (يكون) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو», referring to «من»; the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «من». (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «وكيلا», and (وكيلا) is the khabar of (يكون).

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is iltifāt (a shift of person), in His saying: «ها أنتم جادلتم عنهم ...»
for He moved from the third person to direct address, to confront them face to face with rebuke and disapproval.

dervis-irab:110-112.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءاً أَوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ) A resumptive statement brought to urge Ṭuʿma to repent; yet despite that he persisted in riding the back of transgression and refused to repent. The wāw is resumptive; (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يعمل) is an imperfect verb, the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis), and the fāʿil (agent) is "huwa"; (سوءا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أو) is a conjunction, and (يظلم نفسه) is conjoined to (يعمل), (نفسه) being a mafʿūl bihi. (ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ يَجِدِ اللَّهَ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً) (ثم) is a conjunction, and (يستغفر الله) is conjoined to what precedes; (يجد الله) is the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis), and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of «من». (غفورا) is the second mafʿūl bihi, and (رحيما) an adjective. (وَمَنْ يَكْسِبْ إِثْماً فَإِنَّما يَكْسِبُهُ عَلى نَفْسِهِ) is conjoined to what precedes and parallels it in i'rab. The clause (فإنما) is the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of (من). (على نفسه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يكسبه), because the evil consequence of the sin attaches to it. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً) Its i'rab has already been given. (وَمَنْ يَكْسِبْ خَطِيئَةً أَوْ إِثْماً) Its i'rab has already been given. (ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِ بَرِيئاً) is conjoined to (يكسب); the pronoun is singular by way of taghlīb (giving precedence) to the sin (al-ithm); (به) is attached to «يرم», and (بريئا) is a mafʿūl bihi. (فَقَدِ احْتَمَلَ بُهْتاناً وَإِثْماً مُبِيناً) The clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». The meaning is: he incurs two punishments.

dervis-irab:17-18.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَعْتَدْنا): We have made present and prepared; and it is عتيد, i.e. present and prepared. Its origin is أعددنا; the first dāl was changed into tāʾ.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّمَا التَّوْبَةُ عَلَى اللَّهِ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السُّوءَ بِجَهالَةٍ): resumptive speech to begin the discussion of repentance and its conditions. إنما is the restraining [ما] and the restrained [إن]; التوبة is the mubtadaʾ (subject); على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); للذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); the clause يعملون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; السوء is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بجهالة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. in the state of their being ignorant and foolish. (ثُمَّ يَتُوبُونَ مِنْ قَرِيبٍ): ثم is a conjunction, to indicate that the repentance came late but was accepted in any case before the time of the death-throes and the beholding of death; يتوبون is conjoined to يعملون; من قريب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتوبون. (فَأُولئِكَ يَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ): the فاء is resumptive; أولئك is a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يتوب الله عليهم is the khabar. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً): the واو is resumptive; كان with its noun and khabar, and حكيما is a second khabar. (وَلَيْسَتِ التَّوْبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ): the واو is conjunctive; ليس and its noun; للذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar; the clause يعملون السيئات is the ṣila. (حَتَّى إِذا حَضَرَ أَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ): حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; إذا is an adverb of future time; the clause حضر أحدهم الموت is in the position of genitive by annexation; أحدهم is a fronted mafʿūl bihi and الموت the postponed fāʿil (agent). «حتى» did not put «إذا» in the genitive because conditional particles are not governed by what precedes them; rather, the whole conditional clause is in the position of genitive by حتى, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to يعملون. (قالَ إِنِّي تُبْتُ الْآنَ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivising condition; إن and its noun; the clause تبت is its khabar; الآن is an adverb attached to تبت; the clause is in the position of accusative as the speech quoted by قال (maqūl al-qawl). (وَلَا الَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ): the واو is conjunctive; لا is negating; الذين is conjoined to الذين يعملون; the clause يموتون is the ṣila; the واو is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); هم is a mubtadaʾ and كفار a khabar; the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (أُولئِكَ أَعْتَدْنا لَهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً): the clause is resumptive, and you may make it explicative; in either case it has no grammatical position. The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and the clause أعتدنا is the khabar; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعتدنا; عذابا is a mafʿūl bihi and أليما a naʿt (adjective).

* Benefits:
1- This verse has occupied the scholars, the parsers and the exegetes, and we shall summarise for you some of their views on His words «بجهالة»:
a- It is every act of disobedience that the servant commits in ignorance, even if it is deliberate, because ignorance calls to it and makes it attractive to the servant.
b- The meaning of «بجهالة» is that they do not know the true nature of the punishment in it as a thing is known necessarily.
c- The meaning of «بجهالة» is that they are ignorant that these are sins and acts of disobedience, so they commit them either through a mistaken interpretation or through falling short in inferring their ugliness. Al-Rummānī considered this view weak, because it is contrary to what the exegetes agreed upon, and because it would entail that there is no repentance for one who knew they were sins.
2- Moreover, we cannot avoid pointing to the disagreement that arose between Ahl al-Sunna and the Muʿtazila over His words «على الله». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «He means: acceptance and forgiveness are only obligatory upon Allah for these», and in that he follows the way of the Muʿtazila. Ahl al-Sunna refuted this view on the grounds that it is an analogy of the Creator with the truth [Translator's note: so in the source («على الحق»); probably «على الخلق», "with creation"], and that it is an unrestricted [expression] from which the tongue of the rational person refrains — to the end of that unique debate.
3- Abū Ḥayyān said: «التوبة is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is «على الله»; «للذين» is attached to what «على الله» is attached to; the implied form is: repentance is established upon the bounty and beneficence of Allah for those who...»
4- Abū al-Baqāʾ said: on this view «للذين يعملون السوء» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in His words «على الله», the governor in it being the adverbial phrase and [the notion of] being established, i.e. fixed for those who... Abū al-Baqāʾ also permitted that the khabar be «للذين», with «على الله» attached to an omitted [element] and also being a ḥāl from an omitted [element], the implied form being: repentance only, when it is — or since it is — upon Allah, is for those who...; كان being complete, and the one to whom the ḥāl refers being the agent pronoun of كان. We have cited these views only as training in what our scholars disciplined themselves in for understanding the Book of Allah the Exalted, and what we have cited is sufficient.

dervis-irab:19-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ): imperfect of عضل على فلان, i.e. he made his affair narrow for him and came between him and what he wants. العضل is confinement and constriction; and عضّلت المرأة بولدها is said when her womb is choked by her child, so that part of it comes out and part remains; so its use [here] is figurative. Among fine poetry is the saying of Aws:
ترى الأرض منا بالفضاء مريضة ... معضّلة منا بجمع عرمرم
(You see the land, because of us, sick in the open plain, choked by us with a vast host.)
Al-Nābigha repeated this meaning, saying in describing an army:
لجب يظلّ به الفضاء معضّلا ... يدع الإكام كأنهن صحاري
(A clamorous [army] by which the open space remains choked; it leaves the hillocks as though they were deserts.)
What is meant by it here in the verse is: do not prevent your wives from marrying others by holding on to them until you inherit from them while they are unwilling. When a man married a woman and she was not to his liking, he would confine her with bad treatment and coercion, so that she would ransom herself from him with her wealth and seek divorce (khulʿ); so the Exalted said: «ولا تعضلوهن لتذهبوا ببعض ما آتيتموهن». Moreover, we have previously discussed the occurrence of ʿayn and ḍād as the first and second radicals of a word, and what they then signify of meanings of strength and intensity.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has been given many times. (لا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَرِثُوا النِّساءَ كَرْهاً): resumptive speech introduced to do justice to woman from the injustice and wrongs she used to be subjected to. لا is negating; يحل is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يحل; أن ترثوا النساء: the interpreted maṣdar is the fāʿil (agent) of يحل; النساء is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); كرها — with ḍamma or fatḥa on the kāf, these being two readings — is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. unwilling. (وَلا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذْهَبُوا بِبَعْضِ ما آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ): the واو is conjunctive; لا is negating; تعضلوهن is conjoined to ترثوا, i.e. nor that you constrain them. لتذهبوا: the lām is causal, and تذهبوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to تعضلوهن; ببعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تذهبوا; ما is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause آتيتموهن is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ): if the exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), the interpreted maṣdar must be accusative as the excepted; if it is joined to what precedes, the exception is from the most general of states, so it is parsed as a ḥāl. Abū Ḥayyān parsed it as excepted from the most general of times or causes, so in his view it is accusative as an adverb of time, or as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), as though it were said: do not constrain them at any time except the time that they commit..., or do not constrain them for any cause except that they commit...; both are acceptable. يأتين is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn because it is attached to the nūn of the feminine plural, in the position of accusative by أن; بفاحشة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأتين; مبينة, with fatḥa or kasra on the yāʾ, two readings. (وَعاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): the واو is conjunctive; عاشروهن is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the واو is the fāʿil and the هاء the mafʿūl bihi; بالمعروف is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. being good and gracious in word and deed. (فَإِنْ كَرِهْتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئاً وَيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيْراً كَثِيراً): the فاء is resumptive; إن is conditional; كرهتموهن is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). فعسى: the فاء is linking, and عسى here is complete (tāmma); it is an inflexible (jāmid) verb, and أن with what follows it is its fāʿil. يجعل is an imperfect verb conjoined by the واو to تكرهوا, accusative like it; the واو is its fāʿil [Translator's note: so in the source; the fāʿil of يجعل is evidently اللهُ]; فيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يجعل, standing as the second object of يجعل; خيرا is its first object and كثيرا an adjective.

dervis-irab:20-21.t:
* Vocabulary:
(القنطار): it has been discussed before; what is meant by it here is great wealth, from قنطرت الشيء, when you raised it; and from it is القنطرة (the arched bridge), because it is a lofty structure. [The poet] said:
كقنطرة الرومي أقسم ربّها ... لتكتنفن حتى تشاد بقرمد
(Like the Byzantine's arched bridge, whose master swore it would be enclosed until it was built up with baked brick.)
(البهتان): to confront a man with a vile matter with which you accuse him while he is innocent of it, because at that he is dumbfounded (يبهت), i.e. bewildered. Among the verses in which the word بهت is used, expressing a psychological state, is the saying:
وما هي إلا أن أراها فجاءة ... فأبهت حتى ما أكاد أجيب
(It is only that I see her suddenly, and I am dumbfounded so that I can hardly answer.)
All verbs whose first radical is bāʾ and second radical hāʾ relate to a feeling of the soul. We have counted many of them, and not one of them deviates from this remarkable definition. Of that is بهج به and ابتهج, i.e. it pleased him, which is a matter relating to the core of the soul. Al-Nābigha said:
كمضيئة صدفيّة غوّاصها ... بهج متى يرها يهلّ ويسجد
(Like a shining shell-pearl whose diver is overjoyed; whenever he sees it he cries out and prostrates.)
And بهره: it overcame him; and بهرا is an imprecation against him to be overcome. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
ثم قالوا: تحبها؟ قلت: بهرا ... عدد الرّمل والحصى والتراب
(Then they said: "Do you love her?" I said: "Overwhelmingly — as many as the sand, the pebbles and the dust.")
And بهرج في كلامه, i.e. he mixed into it what grieves the soul. Discussion of this would be long.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمُ اسْتِبْدالَ زَوْجٍ مَكانَ زَوْجٍ): the واو is resumptive; إن is conditional; أردتم is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the تاء is the fāʿil (agent); استبدال زوج is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); مكان زوج is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) استبدال. (وَآتَيْتُمْ إِحْداهُنَّ قِنْطاراً فَلا تَأْخُذُوا مِنْهُ شَيْئاً): the واو is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); آتيتم is a verb with its agent, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); إحداهن is the first mafʿūl bihi and قنطارا the second mafʿūl bihi. فلا: the فاء is linking and لا prohibitive; تأخذوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; the واو is the fāʿil; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تأخذوا; شيئا is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (أَتَأْخُذُونَهُ بُهْتاناً وَإِثْماً مُبِيناً): the hamza is for interrogation, rebuke and disapproval; the clause is resumptive; تأخذونه is an imperfect verb, its agent and its direct object; بهتانا is a ḥāl or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); إثما is conjoined to بهتانا and مبينا is a naʿt (adjective). (وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ وَقَدْ أَفْضى بَعْضُكُمْ إِلى بَعْضٍ وَأَخَذْنَ مِنْكُمْ مِيثاقاً غَلِيظاً): the واو is a conjunction; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; تأخذونه is an imperfect verb, its agent and its direct object; the واو is circumstantial; قد is a particle of realisation; أفضى بعضكم is a verb and its agent; إلى بعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أفضى; أخذن is conjoined to أفضى, the nūn being the fāʿil; ميثاقا is a mafʿūl bihi and غليظا an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
Kināya (metonymy) in "going in unto" (الإفضاء) a thing, because it expresses direct contact with it. What is meant by الإفضاء in this place is sexual intercourse according to al-Shāfiʿī, and that is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās; or [it is] privacy [with her] even without intercourse, as is the choice of Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Farrāʾ.

dervis-irab:113-113.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَتُهُ) The wāw is a conjunction, or resumptive, completing the story of the Banū Ẓafar who tried to lead the Prophet astray, but Allah protected him. In fact the address is general, covering all people in the various circumstances of time and place.
(لولا) is a particle of non-occurrence due to occurrence (ḥarf imtināʿ li-wujūd) containing the meaning of condition; (فضل الله) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted; (عليك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فضل), and (رحمته) is conjoined to (فضل). (لَهَمَّتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُضِلُّوكَ) The lām occurs in the apodosis of (لولا), and the clause (همت طائفة) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. An objection may be raised to this regarding the negation of the intention [since they did in fact intend it], because (لولا) entails the non-occurrence of its apodosis due to the occurrence of its condition; but what is negated in reality is the effect of the intention. All of this will come in its place in this book. (أن يضلوك) is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (همت), i.e.: they intended to lead you astray. (وَما يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ) The wāw is circumstantial and (ما) negating; (يضلون) is an imperfect verb, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and (أنفسهم) is the object of (يضلون); the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَما يَضُرُّونَكَ مِنْ شَيْءٍ) The wāw is a conjunction and (ما) negating; (يضرونك) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is conjoined to (يضلون). (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (شيء) is genitive in wording and accusative in position as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.:
any harm at all. (وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ) The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, containing the sense of a reason for what precedes; (الكتاب) is a mafʿūl bihi, and (الحكمة) is conjoined to (الكتاب). (وَعَلَّمَكَ ما لَمْ تَكُنْ تَعْلَمُ) is conjoined to what precedes; (ما) is a relative noun, the second object of (علمك); the clause (لم تكن) is a ṣila (relative clause), and the clause (تعمل) [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the verse is تعلم] is the khabar of (تكن). (وَكانَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ عَظِيماً) Likewise conjoined; (كان) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, (فضل الله) its noun and (عظيما) its khabar; (عليك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (فضل).

dervis-irab:114-114.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَجْواهُمْ): al-najwā is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), meaning confiding in secret; it may be applied to persons figuratively — the Exalted said: «وإذ هم نجوى» (and when they are [people] in private conference). Al-najwā occurs only between two or more.

* I'rab:
(لا خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِنْ نَجْواهُمْ) A resumptive statement brought to complete the story of the Banū Ẓafar, and it is general with respect to all people. (لا) is the lā of generic negation and (خير) its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; (في كثير) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar (predicate); (من نجواهم) is attached to an omitted adjective of (كثير). (إِلَّا مَنْ أَمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ أَوْ مَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ إِصْلاحٍ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ) (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and (من) is a relative noun, a badal (substitute) from «كثير» or from «نجوى»; on this view the exception is connected (muttaṣil), with a muḍāf omitted [i.e. "except the confiding of whoever enjoins..."]. It has also been said that it is accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because «من» is for persons and confiding is not of their genus; the meaning would then be: but whoever enjoins charity, in his confiding there is much good. (بصدقة) is attached to (أمر), and what follows it is conjoined to it; (بين الناس) is an adverb of place attached to (إصلاح). (وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ ابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِ اللَّهِ) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is a conditional jussive noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يفعل) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (ذلك) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (ابتغاء مرضاة الله) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْراً عَظِيماً) The fāʾ connects the apodosis; (سوف) is a particle of futurity; (نؤتيه) is an imperfect verb and its first mafʿūl bihi; (أجرا) is the second mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «نحن»; (عظيما) is an adjective. The clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis), and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من».

dervis-irab:115-115.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المشاقّة): contention and opposition.
(نُوَلِّهِ ما تَوَلَّى): We make him an adherent of the misguidance he turned to, i.e. what he chose.

* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ يُشاقِقِ الرَّسُولَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ الْهُدى) A resumptive statement brought to comment on the story of Ṭuʿma the apostate; what is intended is the generality of the ruling and its covering all people. (من) is a conditional jussive noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يشاقق) is an imperfect verb, the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis), and (الرسول) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من بعد) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يشاقق); (ما) is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and together with (تبين) it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by annexation; (له) is attached to (تبين), and (الهدى) is the fāʿil (agent). (وَيَتَّبِعْ غَيْرَ سَبِيلِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) is conjoined to (يشاقق), and (غير سبيل المؤمنين) is a mafʿūl bihi. (نُوَلِّهِ ما تَوَلَّى) (نوله) is the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis); the hāʾ is its first object and (ما), a relative noun, its second object; the clause (تولى) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the clause of the protasis and its apodosis is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «من». (وَنُصْلِهِ جَهَنَّمَ وَساءَتْ مَصِيراً) is conjoined to (نوله); (جهنم) is the second mafʿūl bihi of (نصله); (مصيرا) is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and the specifically blamed (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e.: Hell.

* Benefits:
It is reported that Imam al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about a verse in the Book of Allah the Exalted indicating that consensus (al-ijmāʿ) is a proof; he read the Qur'an three hundred times until he found it in this verse: «ومن يشاقق الرسول..» to the end. The establishment of the inference is that following other than the way of the believers is forbidden, so following the way of the believers must be obligatory. The explanation of the first premise is that the Exalted attached the threat to whoever opposes the Messenger and follows other than the way of the believers; opposing the Messenger alone necessitates this threat, so if following other than the way of the believers did not necessitate it, that would be joining something that has no effect on the threat to something that independently entails that threat — and that is not permissible. So it is established that following other than the way of the believers is forbidden. When this is established, it follows that not-following their way is [forbidden, and following it] obligatory [Translator's note: the source reads "that not following their way is obligatory", which contradicts the argument; the intended sense is evidently as bracketed], because not following the way of the believers is truly describable as following other than the way of the believers. So if following the way of other than the believers is [forbidden] [Translator's note: the word "forbidden" is missing in the source], it follows that not following the way of the believers is forbidden; and if not following them is forbidden, then following their way is obligatory. The scholars of legal theory (uṣūl) have long discussions, with questions and answers, concerning the soundness of the inference from this verse; one may refer to them in their proper places.

dervis-irab:116-117.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَرِيداً): al-marīd and al-mārid is one who has reached the extreme in evil and corruption. One says marada, of the patterns naṣara and ẓarufa, when he became insolent and tyrannical; so he is mārid and marīd. He [Allah] made the idols feminine because they were so in their usage; the most famous of them were al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā and Manāt.
