From al-Ḥasan: there was no tribe among the tribes of the Arabs but had an idol which they worshipped and called "the female of the Banū so-and-so". Further detail about these idols will come where they are mentioned by name.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ) A resumptive statement brought to stress that associating partners with Allah (al-shirk) is not forgiven. (إن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يغفر) is its khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from (أن) and what falls within its scope is the object of (يغفر), and (به) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يشرك). (وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ) The wāw is a conjunction; (يغفر) is an imperfect verb and the fāʿil (agent) is "huwa"; (ما) is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (دون ذلك) is an adverb attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (لمن يشاء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يغفر), and the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يشرك) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يشرك). (فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلالًا بَعِيداً) The fāʾ is connective, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis); (ضلالا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and (بعيدا) an adjective; the clause of the condition and the apodosis is the khabar of «من». (إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا إِناثاً) The clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) and has no grammatical position; (إن) is negating; (يدعون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; (من دونه) is attached to (يدعون); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (إناثا) is a mafʿūl bihi, or an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl bihi, i.e.: feminine idols, because of the feminine form of their names, such as al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā and Manāt. It is also said: because they used to dress them in kinds of ornaments and adorn them in the guise of women. (وَإِنْ يَدْعُونَ إِلَّا شَيْطاناً مَرِيداً) The wāw is a conjunction and (إن) negating; (يدعون) is a verb and its fāʿil; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (شيطانا) is a mafʿūl bihi, and (مريدا) an adjective.

dervis-irab:22-23.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الربائب): plural of ربيبة, which is the wife's daughter by another [husband].
(الحجور): plural of حجر, with fatḥa or kasra on the ḥāʾ: the front of the garment. What is meant by it here is what being in the laps entails, which is being under their upbringing.
(الحلائل): plural of حليلة, which is the wife. Al-Farazdaq said:
وذات حليل أنكحتها رماحنا ... حلال لمن يبني بها لم تطلّق
(Many a woman with a husband our spears have given in marriage — lawful to whoever takes her as wife, though she was not divorced.)

* I'rab:
(وَلا تَنْكِحُوا ما نَكَحَ آباؤُكُمْ مِنَ النِّساءِ): resumptive speech introduced to begin explaining which women are forbidden in marriage and which are not. The واو is resumptive; لا is prohibitive; تنكحوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; ما is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it applies to the kind, like the one in His words: «ما طاب لكم من من النساء» [Translator's note: «من» is repeated in the source], i.e. do not marry the kind that your fathers married. Some said: ما is maṣdar-forming, the implied form being "do not marry with the marriage of your fathers", i.e. like the corrupt marriage of your fathers; so it, together with what it governs, is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and there is no harm in that. نكح آباؤكم is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); من النساء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (إِلَّا ما قَدْ سَلَفَ إِنَّهُ كانَ فاحِشَةً وَمَقْتاً وَساءَ سَبِيلًا): إلا is a particle of exception and ما is a disjoined (munqaṭiʿ) excepted, because the past is not excepted from the future; it may also be joined (muttaṣil). More about it will come in the section of Rhetoric. The clause قد سلف is the ṣila (relative clause); إن and its noun; the clause كان فاحشة is the khabar (predicate) of إن; the clause إنه is causal, with no grammatical position; مقتا is conjoined to فاحشة; ساء is a past verb for expressing blame, its fāʿil being vague and latent (mustatir), explained by the tamyīz (specification), which is «سبيلا»; the clause is either resumptive or conjoined to the khabar of كان, reported by an implied verb of saying. (حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهاتُكُمْ): حرم is a past verb in the passive, the تاء being the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حرمت; أمهاتكم is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَبَناتُكُمْ وَأَخَواتُكُمْ وَعَمَّاتُكُمْ وَخالاتُكُمْ وَبَناتُ الْأَخِ وَبَناتُ الْأُخْتِ): conjoined to أمهاتكم, so they fall within the scope of the prohibition. (وَأُمَّهاتُكُمُ اللَّاتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ): also conjoined. (وَأَخَواتُكُمْ مِنَ الرَّضاعَةِ): also conjoined, and the preposition with its genitive noun is accusative as a ḥāl from أخواتكم. (وَأُمَّهاتُ نِسائِكُمْ وَرَبائِبُكُمُ اللَّاتِي فِي حُجُورِكُمْ مِنْ نِسائِكُمُ): also conjoined; في حجوركم is attached to an omitted ṣila; من نسائكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl from ربائبكم. (اللَّاتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ): the relative noun is a naʿt (adjective) of نسائكم; the clause دخلتم بهن is the ṣila; the باء is for transitivity, i.e. you entered into privacy with them. (فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ): the فاء is resumptive; لم تكونوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause دخلتم بهن is the khabar of كان; the فاء is linking; لا is the lā of generic negation, جناح its noun, and عليكم a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar. (وَحَلائِلُ أَبْنائِكُمُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ أَصْلابِكُمْ): conjoined to what preceded; الذين is an adjective of أبنائكم; من أصلابكم: the preposition and its genitive noun are the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَأَنْ تَجْمَعُوا بَيْنَ الْأُخْتَيْنِ إِلَّا ما قَدْ سَلَفَ): the first maṣdar [Translator's note: so in the source («المصدر الاول»), evidently for «المصدر المؤول», the interpreted maṣdar] is also conjoined; بين is an adverb attached to تجمعوا; الأختين is muḍāf ilayhi; إلا is a particle of exception and ما is a disjoined or joined excepted; its i'rab has been given before. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً): إن and its noun; كان with its noun and its two khabars; the clause is the khabar of إن; the clause إن الله is resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse there is the device of mubālagha (hyperbole) in His words: «إلا ما قد سلف». That is because what is forbidden — marrying the women whom the fathers married — is a matter disapproved by most people, and it had reached such a degree of hideousness and repugnance that it was detested before the Law came concerning it; it deserves that the prohibition of it be obeyed.
2- Kināya (metonymy) in His words: «دخلتم بهن», which is a metonymy for intercourse, as mentioned before, or for privacy.
3- Beauty of arrangement in the order of the conjunction, which is evident.

* Benefits:
1- (الأمهات) is the plural of أم; the هاء is added in the plural to distinguish between rational beings and others: for rational beings one says أمهات and for others أمات; and they sometimes exchange [uses].
2- أخت and بنت: their origins are أخو and بنو; their واو was dropped and the تاء substituted for it.

dervis-irab:24-24.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمُحْصَناتُ): those who are protected (أحصنّ), their husbands having protected them by marriage. It is with fatḥa on the ṣād, as in the reading of the majority, except al-Kisāʾī, who read it with kasra. So it is a passive participle on the reading of the majority, and an active participle in the reading of al-Kisāʾī throughout the Qur'an; but in this verse al-Kisāʾī followed the majority.
(مُسافِحِينَ): plural of مسافح, which is the fornicator; from السفح, i.e. the pouring out of semen. The profligate man used to say to the profligate woman: سافحيني وماذيني (from المذي, pre-seminal fluid).

* I'rab:
(وَالْمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ النِّساءِ إِلَّا ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ): conjoined to the forbidden women mentioned before; من النساء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); إلا is a particle of exception and ما is a joined (muttaṣil) excepted. It has been said: disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), considering that what is excepted from is marrying wives, while the excepted is having intercourse with married women, so there is a flavour of disjunction in it; but there is no need for this forced interpretation. The clause ملكت أيمانكم is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, i.e. those who were taken captive while having husbands in the land of unbelief; they are lawful to the warriors, even if they are married women. It is reported from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent his army on the day of Ḥunayn to Awṭās, and they captured women who had husbands among the polytheists; they disliked approaching them, so Allah revealed this verse. Our poets have been captivated by this meaning; al-Farazdaq said:
وذات حليل أنكحتها رماحنا ... حلال لمن يبني بها لم تطلق
(Many a woman with a husband our spears have given in marriage — lawful to whoever takes her as wife, though she was not divorced.)
(كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ): كتاب is an emphatic maṣdar [mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], i.e. Allah has prescribed that for you as a prescription and ordained it as an ordinance. عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the maṣdar. A fuller treatment of that will come in the section of Benefits. (وَأُحِلَّ لَكُمْ ما وَراءَ ذلِكُمْ): the واو is conjunctive; أحلّ is a past verb in the passive — it has also been read in the active — and it is conjoined to the verb that put the maṣdar in the accusative; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أحل; ما is a relative noun, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وراء is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun, and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi. (أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا بِأَمْوالِكُمْ مُحْصِنِينَ غَيْرَ مُسافِحِينَ): the interpreted maṣdar from أن and what falls within its scope is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. intending that you seek women; the mafʿūl bihi is omitted because it is known. محصنين is a first ḥāl and غير مسافحين a second ḥāl. (فَمَا اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً): the فاء is resumptive; ما is a relative noun or a jussivising conditional noun, and it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) in either case; استمتعتم is the ṣila if ما is relative, and the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) if it is conditional; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استمتعتم; منهن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. فآتوهن: the فاء is linking in either case; آتوهن: the clause is the khabar (predicate) of relative ما, or in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the protasis and its apodosis then being the khabar of conditional ما. أجورهن is the second mafʿūl bihi, the first mafʿūl bihi being the هاء in آتوهن. فريضة is a ḥāl from أجورهن, or an emphatic noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar), as some said; but there is no need for that. (وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيما تَراضَيْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْفَرِيضَةِ): the واو is conjunctive or resumptive; لا is the lā of generic negation; جناح is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of لا; فيما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause تراضيتم has no grammatical position, being the ṣila; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تراضيتم; من بعد الفريضة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً): the clause gives the reason for the rulings that have come; the parallels of the rest of the i'rab have been given before.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «مسافحين» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya) for much fornication, likening it to the pouring of water into rivers and springs with gushing and speed.
2- In His words «فآتوهن أجورهن» there is also an explicit metaphor: He borrowed the word الأجور (wages) for the dowry; الأجور is the plural of أجر, which is what a person receives for work.

* Benefits:
Al-Kisāʾī parsed «كتاب الله عليكم» as accusative by incitement (ighrāʾ), as though He said: عليكم كتاب الله (keep to the Book of Allah); so the mafʿūl bihi was put before the verbal noun (ism al-fiʿl), which is عليكم. Then he said: that is permissible, and both hearing [from the Arabs] and analogy support it. As for hearing, it is the saying of the rajaz poet:
أيها المائح دلوي دونكا ... إني رأيت الناس يحمدونكا
(O you who draw water, here is my bucket for you; I have seen people praising you.)
What is meant is دونك دلوي, i.e. take it. As for analogy, the adverbial phrase, i.e. عليكم, stands in for the verb, its implied form being: keep to the Book of Allah; and if the verb appeared, putting its governed word before it would be permitted, and so likewise its governed word [Translator's note: so in the source]. The correct view is what we have held, but we have pointed to it for the spark of brilliance shining from it; there is no room here to refute it.

dervis-irab:25-25.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الطول), with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ: bounty, surplus, capability and attainment. One says: طلته, i.e. I attained it. Al-Farazdaq said:
إن الفرزدق صخرة عادية ... طالت فليس تنالها الأوعالا
(Al-Farazdaq is an ancient rock that has risen above the mountain goats, so they cannot reach it.)
i.e. it rose above the mountain goats, so «الأوعالا» is the object of طالت. And أمر طائل means [a matter] to be reckoned with. [The poet] said:
لقد زادني حبا لنفسي أنني ... بغيض إلى كل امرئ متطاول
(It has increased my love for myself that I am hateful to every overbearing man.)
From it is الطّول in the body, with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ (height), because it is an increase in it. And الطِّوَل, with kasra on the ṭāʾ and fatḥa on the wāw, is a rope with which the legs of an animal are tied. Ṭarafa said:
لعمرك إن الموت ما أخطأ الفتى ... لكالطّول المرخى وثنياه في اليد
(By your life, death, as long as it misses the young man, is like a slackened tether whose two ends are in the hand.)
(الأخدان): secret intimate companions; plural of خدن, with kasra on the khāʾ. Abū Zayd said: الأخدان are companions in lewdness; the singular is خدن and خدين.
(الْعَنَتَ): hardship, originally; its first origin is the breaking of a bone after it has been set; then it was borrowed for every hardship. What is meant by it here is fornication.

* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنْكُمْ طَوْلًا أَنْ يَنْكِحَ الْمُحْصَناتِ الْمُؤْمِناتِ): resumptive speech introduced to complete these legislated rulings. The parsings and the judgements of the exegetes and parsers on this verse are many, and we shall choose what is nearest to logic among them. من is a jussivising conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); لم يستطع is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); طولا is the object of يستطع; and the interpreted maṣdar from أن and ينكح is the object of طولا, because it is a maṣdar. The meaning is: whoever is unable to have a surplus of wealth by which he can attain marriage to a free woman, let him marry a slave-woman. The interpreted maṣdar may also be parsed as accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. means [enough] to marry the protected women. This is the most acceptable, as we see it, of the parsings in which the grammarians and parsers have floundered. (فَمِنْ ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ مِنْ فَتَياتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِناتِ): the فاء links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); مما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, i.e. let him marry a slave-woman from what your right hands possess; the clause ملكت أيمانكم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; من فتياتكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from the implied pronoun in «ما ملكت», and the referent is ما; and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of relative من [Translator's note: so in the source; من was parsed above as conditional, and the sentence here is somewhat garbled]; المؤمنات is a naʿt (adjective) of فتيات. (وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمانِكُمْ): the واو is parenthetical; الله is a mubtadaʾ and أعلم a khabar; بإيمانكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعلم; the clause has no grammatical position because it is parenthetical. (بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ): بعضكم is a mubtadaʾ and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive, introduced to put you and them on a par in religion, and this is one of the most splendid expressions of equality. (فَانْكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ): the فاء is al-faṣīḥa (the disclosing fāʾ), because it discloses an implied condition, i.e. if you know the straight course worthy of being followed, then marry them; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivising condition; بإذن أهلهن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): conjoined to فانكحوهن; بالمعروف is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آتوهن أجورهن, and its meaning is without delay and harm. آتى puts two objects in the accusative, and they are the هاء and أجورهن. (مُحْصَناتٍ غَيْرَ مُسافِحاتٍ وَلا مُتَّخِذاتِ أَخْدانٍ): محصنات is a ḥāl from the mafʿūl bihi in His words «فانكحوهن»; «غير مسافحات» is a second ḥāl; ولا متخذات أخدان is conjoined to مسافحات. (فَإِذا أُحْصِنَّ فَإِنْ أَتَيْنَ بِفاحِشَةٍ فَعَلَيْهِنَّ نِصْفُ ما عَلَى الْمُحْصَناتِ مِنَ الْعَذابِ): the فاء is resumptive; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; أحصن is a past verb in the passive, the nūn being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. فإن: the فاء links the apodosis of إذا, and إن is conditional; أتين is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis, and the nūn is the fāʿil (agent); بفاحشة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أتين. فعليهن: the فاء links the apodosis; عليهن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; نصف is the postponed mubtadaʾ; ما is a relative noun in the position of genitive by annexation; على المحصنات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun; من العذاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. The clause فإن أتين has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivising condition, and the clause فعليهن نصف is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the jussivising condition, which is إن. (ذلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ الْعَنَتَ مِنْكُمْ): ذلك is a demonstrative, a mubtadaʾ; لمن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; the clause خشي has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; العنت is a mafʿūl bihi; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. (وَأَنْ تَصْبِرُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ): the واو is resumptive; أن and what falls within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar, a mubtadaʾ; خير is the khabar of the interpreted maṣdar; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خير. (وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the واو is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ, غفور a first khabar and رحيم a second khabar.

* Benefits:
In the i'rab we chose what we saw as nearest to logic and closest to correctness, but for added benefit we cite what some scholars said in parsing this verse. They permitted making «أن ينكح» a badal (substitute) of «طولا», a substitution of a thing for the [same] thing, the two referring to one thing, because الطول is ability, and marriage is ability. They permitted the interpreted maṣdar to be the object of يستطع; and they said regarding the accusative of «طولا» that it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with an annexed noun omitted, i.e. whoever of you is unable to marry the protected women for lack of means; or that it may be accusative as a maṣdar [mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], governed by [the notion of] ability, the implied form being: whoever of you is unable with an ability to marry. So ponder, and protection is with Allah alone.

dervis-irab:118-121.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تبتيك الآذان) [Translator's note: the source heading reads تبكيت, evidently a misprint for تبتيك, from فليبتكن]: cutting or slitting them. They used to slit the ear of a she-camel when she had borne five litters and the fifth was a male, and they forbade themselves to benefit from her. That was one of their customs. Likewise they used to alter the creation of Allah: they would put out the eyes of livestock to exempt them from being ridden, or castrate them. Among altering the creation of Allah is tattooing; in the ḥadīth: "Allah has cursed al-wāshirāt (those who file their teeth), al-muraqqiqāt asnānahunna (those who thin their teeth), al-mutanaḍḍāt and al-mutanaffishāt, i.e. those who pluck their hair." [Translator's note: the ḥadīth wording appears corrupted in the source; the well-known wording curses tattooing women (al-wāshimāt), those who pluck facial hair (al-mutanammiṣāt) and those who file their teeth (al-mutafallijāt).]
(مَحِيصاً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) of ḥāṣa ʿanhu, when he turned aside and swerved. It has several maṣdars, among them also ḥayūṣan, maḥāṣan and ḥayaṣānan, with fatḥa on the yāʾ.

* I'rab:
(لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ وَقالَ: لَأَتَّخِذَنَّ مِنْ عِبادِكَ نَصِيباً مَفْرُوضاً) The clause has no grammatical position because it is a supplication (duʿāʾiyya) or resumptive. Some made it an adjective of «شيطانا» in the preceding verse, but I see in that something far-fetched and forced. (لعنه الله) is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil (agent). (وقال): the wāw is resumptive, or circumstantial with "qad" understood; the oath clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying). The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (أتخذن) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the clause (أتخذن) has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an omitted oath. (من عبادك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أتخذن); (نصيبا) is a mafʿūl bihi and (مفروضا) an adjective. (وَلَأُضِلَّنَّهُمْ وَلَأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمْ وَلَآمُرَنَّهُمْ) The three clauses are conjoined to (أتخذن); so these are Satan's five statements. (فَلَيُبَتِّكُنَّ آذانَ الْأَنْعامِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction [Translator's note: the source has the misprint عاصفة for عاطفة], and (آذان الأنعام) is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَلَآمُرَنَّهُمْ فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ اللَّهِ) Likewise conjoined. The origin of (يغيرن) is (يغيروننّ); the nūn was dropped for the jussive by the lām of command, and the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters [Translator's note: so in the source; the lām here is that of the oath-answer, and the nūn of the five verbs is usually said to be dropped to avoid a succession of nūns, not for a jussive]. (خلق الله) is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَمَنْ يَتَّخِذِ الشَّيْطانَ وَلِيًّا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يتخذ) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis); (الشيطان) is the first mafʿūl bihi and (وليا) the second; (من دون الله) is attached to an omitted adjective of «وليا». (فَقَدْ خَسِرَ خُسْراناً مُبِيناً) The fāʾ is connective; (قد) is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (خسرانا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and (مبينا) an adjective. The clause is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis), and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of «من». (يَعِدُهُمْ وَيُمَنِّيهِمْ وَما يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ إِلَّا غُرُوراً) The clause is resumptive, brought to show the reality of Satan's lying promises. The objects of (يعدهم) and (يمنيهم) are omitted because they are known. (وما): the wāw is circumstantial and (ما) negating; (يعدهم الشيطان) is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi and its fāʿil; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (غرورا) may be a second object of «يمنيهم» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb immediately governing it is يعدهم], or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e.: [a promise] of delusion; and these are equally preferable. (أُولئِكَ مَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ) The clause is resumptive; (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ, (مأواهم) a second mubtadaʾ, and (جهنم) the khabar of (مأواهم); the nominal clause is the khabar of (أولئك). (وَلا يَجِدُونَ عَنْها مَحِيصاً) The wāw is a conjunction and (لا) negating; (يجدون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; (محيصا) is a mafʿūl bihi; (عنها) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because the maṣdar does not govern what precedes it.

dervis-irab:122-122.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قِيلًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) like al-qawl and al-qāl. Ibn al-Sikkīt said: al-qāl and al-qīl are two nouns, not maṣdars.

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ) The wāw is resumptive; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (آمنوا) is a ṣila (relative clause); and (عملوا الصالحات) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً) (سندخلهم) is an imperfect verb and its first object; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu"; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the relative noun. (جنات) is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa), or accusative by removal of the preposition, as already stated. The clause (تجري ...) etc. is an adjective of (جنات); (خالدين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خالدين), and (أبدا) is an adverb also attached to (خالدين). (وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا)
(وعد الله) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and (حقا) is also a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb. It has also been said that it is accusative as a ḥāl, but I have some reservation about it. (وَمَنْ أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ قِيلًا) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and (أصدق) a khabar; (من الله) is attached to (أصدق), and (قيلا) is a tamyīz (specification).

dervis-irab:123-124.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النقير): its origin is the small spot on the back of the date-stone, as already stated, and it is a metonymy for paucity. The nūn with the qāf, when they are the fāʾ and ʿayn (first and second radicals) of the verb, has a unique meaning that is almost consistent, namely making an impression and leaving a trace behind it. Naqaba al-ḥāʾiṭ (he bored through the wall) is well known; naqaba al-bayṭār (the farrier pierced) the navel of the animal with the borer and drew out yellow fluid; naqqaḥa al-kalām wa-l-shiʿr (he revised the speech and the poetry); naqqaḥathu al-sinūn (the years took their toll on him); naqadahu al-thaman (he paid him the price in cash); naqada al-dirham, i.e. he distinguished its good from its bad — and he is one of the critics (naqada, nuqqād) of poetry; naqara al-ṭāʾir al-ḥabba (the bird pecked the grain) with its beak; naqara al-ʿūd wa-l-daff (he struck the lute and the tambourine): he produced from them a sound of far-reaching effect. This is among the rare marvels of this language and its wonders.

* I'rab:
(لَيْسَ بِأَمانِيِّكُمْ وَلا أَمانِيِّ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ) A resumptive statement brought to show that preference is only by righteous deeds and fruitful output, and that faith is what has settled in the heart and been supported by action. (ليس) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its noun is disputed among the grammarians and parsers: it has been said that it is the promise, because it is not dependent on wishes; and it has been said that it is the faith understood from His saying: «والذين آمنوا». All of that is admissible and good, and the reference is one. The bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (أمانيكم) is genitive in wording and accusative in position because it is the khabar (predicate) of (ليس); (ولا أماني أهل الكتاب) is conjoined to (أمانيكم). (مَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءاً يُجْزَ بِهِ) The clause is resumptive or explicative, and in either case has no grammatical position. (من) is a conditional jussive noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يعمل) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis), and (سوءا) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يجز) is the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يجز»; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (وَلا يَجِدْ لَهُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلِيًّا وَلا نَصِيراً) is conjoined to «يجز» and is jussive like it. (له) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of «وليا» and was placed before it. (من دون الله) is attached to (يجد), serving as the first object, and (وليا) is the second object; (نصيرا) is conjoined to «وليا». (وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحاتِ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; (من) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ; (يعمل) is the protasis; (من الصالحات) is attached to (يعمل), and the meaning of «من» is partition (tabʿīḍ), because encompassing all righteous deeds is not possible for those under obligation. Strange is al-Ṭabarī's saying that it is redundant; it amounts to nothing.
(من ذكر) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it removes the vagueness from «من»; (أو أنثى) is conjoined. The wāw is circumstantial; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (مؤمن) a khabar, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (فَأُولئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ وَلا يُظْلَمُونَ نَقِيراً) The fāʾ connects the apodosis; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (يدخلون الجنة) is a khabar; (ولا يظلمون) is conjoined to (يدخلون); (نقيرا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and its discussion has already been given. The clause (أولئك يدخلون) is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «من».

dervis-irab:26-28.t:
* I'rab:
(يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ سُنَنَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ): resumptive speech introduced to complete the explanation of the preceding rulings. يريد الله is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ليبين: the lām is redundant (zāʾida), but it has been given the status of the causal lām; the addition of the lām conveys emphasis on the will to explain. The meaning is: Allah wills to make clear to you what is hidden from you of your interests, and to guide you to the ways of those who were before you, so as to follow what in them is good for you and in harmony with your reality. يهديكم is conjoined to يبين; the كاف is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and سنن the second mafʿūl bihi; الذين is muḍāf ilayhi; من قبلكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. «سنن» may also be accusative by removal of the preposition. The discussion of هدى was given in al-Fātiḥa. (وَيَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ): conjoined to «يبين»; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتوب. (وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): the واو is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), عليم a first khabar (predicate) and حكيم a second khabar. (وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ): the واو is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يريد is the khabar; أن يتوب is an interpreted maṣdar, a mafʿūl bihi; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتوب. (وَيُرِيدُ الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الشَّهَواتِ): conjoined to the preceding يريد; الذين is the fāʿil; the clause يتبعون is the ṣila of the relative noun; الشهوات is a mafʿūl bihi, the sign of its accusative being the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. (أَنْ تَمِيلُوا مَيْلًا عَظِيماً): أن and what follows it is an interpreted maṣdar, the object of يريد; ميلا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and عظيما a naʿt (adjective). (يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُخَفِّفَ عَنْكُمْ): an emphasis of what preceded, to expand the statement; the clause is resumptive, and its i'rab has been given before. (وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسانُ ضَعِيفاً): the clause is resumptive, serving as the reason for the lightening. خلق is a past verb in the passive; الإنسان is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ضعيفا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الإنسان, an emphatic ḥāl, i.e. he is not strong enough to struggle against desires and to resist the soul that commands to evil.

* Benefits:
This is a construction that has occupied the parsers, and the views of the exegetes on it have conflicted. In the section of I'rab we cited what we held, and what al-Zamakhsharī held before, which is the view of the Kufans. But Sībawayh and the Basrans hold that the object of يريد is omitted, its implied form being: Allah wills this, i.e. the making lawful of what He made lawful, the forbidding of what He forbade and the legislating of what has been mentioned, so that the causal meaning is sound. But we see in it a forced interpretation that does not accord with the easy style of the Qur'an. There are two views worth recording:

1- The view of al-Farrāʾ:
Al-Farrāʾ holds that the lām here is the lām of kay, which alternates with «أن». He said: the Arabs alternate between the lām of kay and «أن», bringing the lām in the sense of «كي» in the place of «أن» with أردت and أمرت; so you say: أردت أن تفعل and أردت لتفعل. From it are the words of the Exalted: «يريدون ليطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم», «وأمرت لأعدل بينكم», «وأمرنا لنسلم لرب العالمين»; and from it is the saying:
أريد لأنسى ذكرها فكأنما ... تمثّل لي ليلى بكل سبيل
(I want to forget the thought of her, yet it is as though Laylā appears before me on every path.)

2- The view of al-Zajjāj:
Al-Zajjāj reported this view and said: if the lām were in the sense of «أن», another lām could enter upon it, just as you say: جئت كي تكرمني, and then say: جئت لكي تكرمني; and he recited:
أردت لكيما يعلم الناس أنها ... سراويل قيس والوفود شهود
(I wanted the people to know that they were the trousers of Qays, while the delegations were witnesses.)

dervis-irab:29-30.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْباطِلِ): resumptive speech introduced to begin explaining some of the prohibitions relating to property and lives. The i'rab of the vocative has been given many times. لا is prohibitive; تأكلوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; the واو is the fāʿil (agent); أموالكم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بينكم is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) تأكلوا; بالباطل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). What is meant by الباطل here is what the Law has not permitted. (إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجارَةً عَنْ تَراضٍ مِنْكُمْ): إلا is a particle of exception, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of accusative by disjoined (munqaṭiʿ) exception, because trade is not of the genus of wealth consumed wrongfully, and because the exception falls upon being (الكون), and being is a notion, not a substance. Trade was singled out because most of the means of livelihood are connected with it. تجارة is the khabar (predicate) of تكون, and its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: unless the trade is a trade. عن تراض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective), i.e. a trade proceeding from mutual consent. [Mutual consent is well known in the books of jurisprudence; according to al-Shāfiʿī it is their separating from the session of the contract while mutually consenting.] منكم is a preposition and transactions; according to Abū Ḥanīfa it is the consent of the buyer and seller at the time of offer and acceptance, and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of تجارة. [Translator's note: the source text is jumbled here — a sentence about Abū Ḥanīfa's definition of mutual consent has been spliced into «ومنكم جار ومجرور متعلقان بمحذوف صفة لتجارة»; it is translated as it stands.] (وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ): conjoined to what preceded; لا is prohibitive; تقتلوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by it; أنفسكم is a mafʿūl bihi. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيماً): the clause gives the reason for the prohibition, with no grammatical position; إن and its noun; the clause of كان with its noun and khabar is the khabar of إن. (وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ عُدْواناً وَظُلْماً): the واو is resumptive; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); يفعل is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ذلك is a demonstrative, a mafʿūl bihi, the reference being to the preceding prohibited things; and it has been said: to the killing of lives specifically. عدوانا and ظلما are two maṣdars in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (فَسَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِ ناراً): the فاء links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); سوف is a particle of the future; نصليه is an imperfect verb, the هاء being the first mafʿūl bihi and نارا the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause joined with the فاء is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of conditional من. (وَكانَ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيراً): the واو is resumptive; كان and its noun, and يسيرا its khabar; على الله is attached to يسير or to an omitted adjective of it.

dervis-irab:31-32.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبائِرَ ما تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ): resumptive speech introduced to call to avoiding the major sins and adhering to acts of obedience. إن is conditional; تجتنبوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the واو is the fāʿil (agent); كبائر is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ما is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause تنهون عنه has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); تنهون is an imperfect verb in the passive, the واو being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); عنه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) تنهون. (نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ): نكفر is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); عنكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نكفر; سيئاتكم is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَنُدْخِلْكُمْ مُدْخَلًا كَرِيماً): ندخلكم is conjoined to نكفر, the كاف being a mafʿūl bihi; مدخلا is a noun of place or a mīmī maṣdar, so it is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa) or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); it has also been said: an adverb of place, and that is not far-fetched. كريما is a naʿt (adjective). (وَلا تَتَمَنَّوْا ما فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ): resumptive speech introduced to forbid wishful coveting, because in it is attachment of the mind to this world and forgetfulness of the Hereafter. The واو is resumptive; لا is prohibitive; تتمنوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; the واو is the fāʿil; ما is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi; the clause فضل الله is the ṣila; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فضل; بعضكم is a mafʿūl bihi; على بعض is also attached to فضل. In this prohibition is a call to avoid envy. (لِلرِّجالِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا اكْتَسَبُوا): the clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive; it may also be explicative of what the prohibition was brought for. للرجال is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); نصيب is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); مما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of نصيب; the clause اكتسبوا is the ṣila. (وَلِلنِّساءِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا اكْتَسَبْنَ): conjoined to the preceding clause. (وَسْئَلُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): conjoined to the prohibition. اسألوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the Name of Majesty is the first object and the second is omitted; من فضله is attached to an omitted adjective of the omitted second object, i.e. something of His bounty. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيماً): إن and its noun; the clause of كان with its noun and khabar is the khabar of إن; the clause is causal, with no grammatical position; بكل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «عليما».

dervis-irab:125-126.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ دِيناً مِمَّنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أحسن) its khabar (predicate); (دينا) is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the mubtadaʾ; (ممن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أحسن); the clause (أسلم وجهه) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; (لله) is attached to «أسلم». The wāw is circumstantial; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (محسن) a khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «أسلم». (وَاتَّبَعَ مِلَّةَ إِبْراهِيمَ حَنِيفاً) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause (اتبع) is conjoined to the clause (أسلم), falling within the scope of the ṣila; (ملة إبراهيم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (حنيفا) is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of (اتبع) or from (إبراهيم), i.e.: inclining to the upright religion. (وَاتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ إِبْراهِيمَ خَلِيلًا) The wāw is the wāw of parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ), and the clause (اتخذ الله إبراهيم) is parenthetical; its benefit is emphasising the nearness of Ibrāhīm and his distinction in that Allah took him as an intimate friend. (خليلا) is the second mafʿūl bihi of (اتخذ). (وَلِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) The wāw is resumptive; (لله) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (ما) is a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ; (في السموات) is attached to the omitted ṣila of the relative noun; and (ما في الأرض) is conjoined to (ما في السموات). (وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُحِيطاً) The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; (كان) and its noun, (محيطا) its khabar, and (بكل شيء) is attached to «محيطا».

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of the Exalted (وَاتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ إِبْراهِيمَ خَلِيلًا) there is iʿtirāḍ (parenthesis). Parenthesis is a clause or more that intervenes in the course of speech or between two connected statements and conveys an addition to the meaning of the speaker's purpose other than removing ambiguity. It was discussed before at His saying in al-Baqara «ولن تفعلوا». We add to that that it serves multiple purposes: it may be for drawing attention and clarification. The poet said:
واعلم فعلم المرء ينفعه ... ان سوف يأتي كل ما قدرا
(And know — for a man's knowledge benefits him — that everything decreed will come.)
His saying «فعلم المرء ينفعه» is a parenthesis for drawing attention and clarification. Similar is what is related: al-Rāḍī bi-llāh wrote an apology to his brother al-Muqtafī while they were both at school. Al-Muqtafī had wronged al-Rāḍī, and al-Rāḍī was the elder of the two; so al-Rāḍī wrote to him:
يا ذا الذي يغضب من غير شي ... اعتب فعتباك حبيب إليّ
أنت على انك لي ظالم ... أعز خلق الله كلّا عليّ
(O you who grow angry for no reason, reproach me, for your reproach is dear to me. You — despite your wronging me — are the dearest of all Allah's creation to me.)
His saying «على انك لي ظالم» is a parenthesis for drawing attention. As for the verse above, it conveys emphasis on the obligation to follow the religion of Ibrāhīm, because one whose rank and nearness with Allah reached the point that He took him as an intimate friend (khalīl), who agrees with Him in qualities (khilāl), is worthy to have his religion followed.
It is said, concerning the reason Ibrāhīm was named the Khalīl (intimate friend) of Allah, that Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, sent to a friend (khalīl) of his in Egypt, during a crisis that afflicted the people, to obtain provisions from him. His friend said:
"If Ibrāhīm were seeking provisions for himself I would do it, but he wants them for the guests." His servants then passed by a valley of soft sand and filled the sacks (al-gharāʾir, i.e. al-ʿudūl) from it, out of shame before the people. When they told Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, the news grieved him and his eyes filled [Translator's note: the source reads حملته عيناه, likely for هملت عيناه, "his eyes overflowed"]. His wife went to one of the sacks and brought out the finest white flour (ḥuwwārā, i.e. flour) and baked bread. Ibrāhīm smelled the bread and said: "Where did you get it?" His wife said: "From your Egyptian friend." He said: "Rather, it is from my Friend, Allah, Mighty and Majestic." So Allah named him Khalīl.

dervis-irab:127-127.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَسْتَفْتُونَكَ): they seek a legal opinion (fatwā) from you. Al-fatwā with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and al-futyā with ḍamma; the plural is al-fatāwī with kasra on the wāw, and al-fatāwā with fatḥa is permissible for lightness.

* I'rab:
(وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ فِي النِّساءِ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ) The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to return to mentioning women and the rest of the rulings concerning them. (يستفتونك) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (في النساء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) it. (قل) is an imperative verb and its fāʿil is "anta"; this clause is also resumptive. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يفتيكم) is an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a khabar (predicate); the clause (الله يفتيكم) is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying); (فيهن) is attached to (يفتيكم). (وَما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتابِ فِي يَتامَى النِّساءِ) You may make the wāw a conjunction, so that the relative noun is conjoined to (الله), i.e.: Allah gives you a ruling, and so does what is recited in His Book.
You may also make it parenthetical, so that the clause is parenthetical with no grammatical position, and «ما» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: "gives you a ruling". (عليكم) is attached to (يتلى); (في الكتاب) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (في يتامى النساء) is attached to an omitted badal (substitute) from «فيهن». The annexation of «يتامى» to «النساء» is a case of annexing the adjective to the noun it describes. (اللَّاتِي لا تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ ما كُتِبَ لَهُنَّ) (اللاتي) is a relative noun, an adjective of (النساء); the clause (لا تؤتونهن) is a ṣila (relative clause); (ما) is a relative noun, the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause (كتب) is a ṣila, and (لهن) is attached to (كتب). (وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ) is conjoined to (تؤتونهن). (أن تنكحوهن) is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, which is «في», i.e.:
"[you desire] to marry them" for their beauty and their wealth; or «عن», i.e.: you are averse to marrying them because of their homeliness and poverty. So it is an instance of double-edged speech (al-kalām al-muwajjah), as will come in the section of Rhetoric. (وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْوِلْدانِ)
is conjoined to (يتامى النساء), and (من الولدان) is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَأَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلْيَتامى بِالْقِسْطِ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the interpreted maṣdar is genitive by being conjoined to (المستضعفين); or you may make the maṣdar accusative by removal of the preposition, so that the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element conjoined to what precedes, i.e.: "and He commands you to stand up". (لليتامى) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, and (بالقسط) is attached to (تقوموا). (وَما تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِهِ عَلِيماً) The wāw is resumptive; (ما) is a conditional jussive noun, a mubtadaʾ; (تفعلوا) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; (من خير) is attached to (تفعلوا). The fāʾ is connective, and the clause (إن الله) is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis); the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «ما». The clause (كان) is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «إن», and (عليما) is the khabar of (كان); (به), the preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to «عليما».

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is al-kalām al-muwajjah (double-edged speech), which is speech that admits two opposite meanings; it has been alluded to before. That is in His saying: «وترغبون أن تنكحوهن», for they are either beautiful or homely according to the preposition supplied. It is reported that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, when the guardian of an orphan girl came to him, would look: if she was beautiful he would say, "Marry her to someone other than you, and seek for her one better than you"; and if she was homely and had no wealth he would say, "Marry her yourself, for you have more right to her." Muslim narrated from ʿĀʾisha that she said: "This is the orphan girl who is in the care of her guardian; he desires her beauty and her wealth and wants to reduce her dowry. So they were forbidden to marry them unless they dealt justly with them in giving the full dowry, and they were commanded to marry others besides them." ʿĀʾisha said: "Then the people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a ruling, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: «ويستفتونك في النساء» up to His saying: «وترغبون أن تنكحوهن». So He made clear to them that when the orphan girl has beauty and wealth they desire to marry her and do not grant her what befits her in giving the full dowry; and when she is not desired because of little beauty, they leave her [Translator's note: the source repeats "they leave her" twice] and seek another."
Double-edged speech has been discussed before; it remains for us to say that among what admits two opposite meanings is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in other mosques, except al-Masjid al-Ḥarām.» From this ḥadīth two opposite meanings are drawn:
one is that al-Masjid al-Ḥarām is better than the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; the other is that the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is better than al-Masjid al-Ḥarām — rather, that it surpasses it by less [than a thousand] [Translator's note: the source wording بل تفضل ما دونها is obscure; the sense appears to be that a prayer in the Prophet's mosque exceeds one in al-Masjid al-Ḥarām by less than a thousandfold] — unlike the remaining mosques, for a thousand prayers in them fall short of a single prayer in it. Among this also is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to his wives: «The longest of you in hand will be the quickest of you to join me.» When he died — may the blessings of Allah be upon him — they began to measure their hands against one another to see which of them had the longest hand; then Zaynab was the quickest of them to join him, and she was much given to charity, so they knew then that he did not mean the bodily limb but meant charity. So this saying indicates the two meanings referred to. Among this also is what is reported from Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "I served the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for ten years, and he never said of anything I did, 'Why did you do it?', nor of anything I did not do, 'Why did you not do it?'" This saying admits two interpretations: one is describing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as patient with the character of whoever accompanied him; the other is that he described himself as perceptive and intelligent in the deeds he undertook, as though he perceived what was in the Messenger's mind and did it without needing to ask his permission. Among this also is what came in one of the prophetic supplications: he ﷺ prayed against a man of the polytheists, saying: «O Allah, cut off his trace (athar).» This admits three interpretations:
The first is that he prayed against him with chronic disability, for if he becomes crippled he cannot walk on the ground, and then his trace [footprint] is cut off. The second: that he prayed against him that he should have no offspring or descendants after him. The third: that he prayed against him that he should have no trace of any kind at all, i.e. that he should do no deed whose trace remains after him, whatever it may be — offspring, a building, a plantation or anything else.

The story of Khālid ibn al-Walīd and ʿAbd al-Masīḥ:
Among this also is what is related of ʿAbd al-Masīḥ ibn Buqayla when Khālid ibn al-Walīd descended upon them at al-Ḥīra. ʿAbd al-Masīḥ ibn Buqayla [the source here spells it بقلية] went out to him, and when he stood before him he said: "Good morning (anʿim ṣabāḥan), O king." Khālid said to him:
- "Allah has made us independent of this greeting of yours through 'Peace be upon you'." Then he said to him:
- "Where is the farthest point of your trace (whence do you come)?"
He said: "From my father's back."
He said: "Then from where did you come out?"
He said: "From my mother's belly."
He said: "Then upon what are you?"
He said: "Upon the earth."
He said: "Then in what are you?"
He said: "In my clothes."
He said: "Son of how many are you (how old are you)?"
He said: "Son of one man."
Khālid said: "I have never seen the like of today: I ask him about one thing and he heads towards another!" This is an excellent pattern of double-edged speech: it is fit to be an answer to Khālid about what he asked, and fit to be an answer to something else, namely what ʿAbd al-Masīḥ ibn Buqayla mentioned.

A delightful double meaning from Plato:
Among what runs along this path is what is related of Plato, that he said:
«Leaving medicine is medicine.» Some physicians held that he meant: if the constitution has become delicate and reached a point where it cannot bear medicine, then leaving it and refraining from it is medicine.
Others held that by "leaving" (al-tark) he meant "placing", i.e. placing the medicine upon the disease is medicine — pointing thereby to the physician's skill in the timing of his treatment.

Opposite double meaning in poetry:
If we return to poetry, we see [the source has the misprint وأينا for رأينا] al-Farazdaq following this manner of double meaning in his poetry, saying:
إذا جعفر مرّت على هضبة الحمى ... فقد أخزت الاحياء منها قبورها
(When [the tribe of] Jaʿfar pass by the hill of al-Ḥimā, its living have disgraced its graves [or: its graves have disgraced its living].)
This, as you see, indicates two opposite meanings: one is censure of the living, and the other censure of the dead. As for the censure of the living, it is that they abandoned the dead — he means that they met another people in battle and the living fled from them and surrendered them, or that the dead called on them for help and they did not help them. As for the censure of the dead, it is that they have disgraces and scandals that bring shame and ignominy, and with them they shame the living and attach them to them.
A verse of Abū Tammām:
In this vein came the saying of Abū Tammām:
بالشعر طول إذا اصطكّت قصائده ... في معشر وبه عن معشر قصر
(Poetry has length [/ pride] when its odes clash among one company, and it falls short regarding another company.)
This verse admits two opposite interpretations: one is that poetry's scope widens in praising you and narrows in praising others — meaning that his noble deeds are many and the noble deeds of others are few. The other is that poetry has pride and distinction in praising you, and obscurity and dullness in praising others. For the word al-ṭūl is understood as the opposite of shortness, and is also understood as pride, from our saying:
ṭāla fulān ʿalā fulān, i.e. he vaunted himself over him.

A verse of Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī:
Among what is strung on this thread is the saying of Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī:
عجبت لسعي الدهر بيني وبينها ... فلما انقضى ما بيننا سكن الدهر
(I marvelled at Time's running between me and her; when what was between us ended, Time grew still.)
This admits two interpretations: one is that by Time's running he meant the swift passing of the hours during the period of union, and when the union ended, Time returned to its state of stillness and slowness. The other is that by Time's running he meant the running about of the people of the time with slander and tale-bearing, and when the union between them ended they grew still and gave up their slandering. This is a case of putting the muḍāf ilayhi in place of the muḍāf, as in His saying: «واسأل القرية», i.e. the people of the town.
A verse of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
Of subtle meaning in this regard is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī in praise of ʿAḍud al-Dawla:
لو فطنت خيله لنائله ... لم يرضها أن تراه يرضاها
(Had his horses perceived his bounty, it would not please them to see him content with them.)
From this two opposite meanings are drawn: one is that his horses, had they known the measure of his precious gifts, would not have been content for themselves to be among his gifts, because his gifts are more precious than they. The other is that his horses, had they known that he gives them away among his gifts, would not have been content with that, since they dislike leaving his ownership.

Between the literal and the figurative:
All of this does not go beyond the literal. When it admits both the literal and the figurative and they pull at it from both sides, it reaches the highest degrees of inimitability; this will come in its places. But out of concern to complete the discussion we cite one example from poetry in which we see both meanings figurative, such as the saying of Abū Tammām:
قد بلونا أبا سعيد حديثا ... وبلونا أبا سعيد قديما
ووردناه ساحلا وقليبا ... ورعيناه بارضا وجميما
فعلمنا أن ليس إلّا بشق ... النفس صار الكريم يدعى كريما
(We have tried Abū Saʿīd lately, and tried Abū Saʿīd of old; we came to him for water as a seashore and as a well, and grazed him as young sprouts and as thick growth; so we learned that only through hardship of soul does the generous man come to be called generous.)
From "the shore" and "the well" two figurative interpretations are drawn: one is that he meant by them much and little, in relation to the shore and the well; the other is that he meant by them [needing] a means and not [needing] a means, for coming to the shore for water needs no means [rope], while coming to the well needs a means. Both of these meanings are figurative, since the literal shore and well are other than them. The right view is the second, because it better indicates the eloquence of the speaker and the praise of the one spoken of. As for the eloquence of the speaker, it lies in being free from the blemish of repetition, and in the contrast between the first half of the line and its second half indicating little and much — because al-bāriḍ is the first growth of plants when it appears, and when it increases and thickens it is called jamīm — as though he said:
"We took from him by his own volunteering and by asking, little and much." As for the praise of the one spoken of, it lies in enumerating his four states: in his volunteering and being asked, his giving much and giving little, and the hardships involved in enduring these states. Discussion of this is long, but like beauty it is never tiresome.

* Benefits:
1- Omitting the preposition before anna and an is regular (qiyāsī), on condition that confusion is avoided. His saying, Exalted: «وترغبون أن تنكحوهن» poses a difficulty for this, for the preposition was omitted here although confusion exists — as evidenced by the exegetes' disagreement about what is meant: some supplied «في» and some supplied «عن», and each argued for what he held. Two answers were given to it:
a- that the preposition was omitted relying on the contextual indication (qarīna) that removes the confusion;
b- that it was omitted with the intention of vagueness, so that thereby both whoever desires them for their beauty and wealth and whoever is averse to them for their homeliness and poverty might be deterred.
So the disagreement, then, is about the contextual indication.
2- They allowed other views regarding (في يتامى النساء), which we cite as an exercise for the mind. Among them: that the two [the preposition and its genitive noun] are a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from His saying (في الكتاب), and a muḍāf must be supplied, i.e.: "concerning the ruling on the orphan women" — and there is no doubt that the Book includes mention of the rulings on them. Among them: that the two are attached to (يتلى), and the attachment of two prepositions of the same wording [to one verb] is allowed because their meanings differ; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: as you say, "I came to you on (fī) Friday about (fī) the matter of Zayd". And among them: that the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e.: "being concerning the ruling on the orphan women".

dervis-irab:33-34.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النشوز): the origin of النشوز is rising up towards evils [Translator's note: so in the source («الارتفاع إلى الشرور»)]. The نشوز of a woman is her hatred of her husband and her raising herself above him in arrogance. One says: علوت نشزا من الأرض (I climbed a rise of ground), and نشزا with sukūn or fatḥa on the shīn. نشز الشيء عن مكانه: it rose from its place; نشزت إليّ النفس: the soul surged with alarm; and امرأة ناشز (a rebellious woman). Among the curious features of nūn and shīn is that they do not occur as the first and second radicals of a word without indicating this meaning or something close to it: rising above a thing, departing from its origin and not being in harmony with its reality. From it is نشأ الإنسان, i.e. he rose and appeared; «وأنشأناهنّ إنشاء»; «ومن أين نشأت؟» (where did you grow up?); الجواري المنشآت: the ships cleaving the waves of the sea; نشب العظم في الحلق: the bone stuck in the throat and rose up in it; تراموا بالنّشاب (they shot arrows at one another); نشبت الحرب (war broke out); نشج الباكي نشجا, which is the rising of weeping and its reverberation in the chest; and أنشد الشعر إنشادا حسنا (he recited poetry well), because the reciter raises his voice — to the end of what this root contains. This is among the wonders by which our noble language is distinguished.

* I'rab:
(وَلِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنا مَوالِيَ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوالِدانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ): the speech is resumptive, introduced to complete the rulings of inheritance. The parsers and exegetes have spoken a great deal about this verse, have been lengthy in discussion and turned the speech over in all its aspects, yet none of them arrived at anything substantial that quenches the thirst; it is inimitable speech. The nearest of what we have seen on it is the following: the واو is resumptive; لكل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); the tanwīn in كل is a substitute for a word, i.e. for every people. The clause جعلنا is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم; the first object of جعلنا is omitted, i.e. We made them; موالي is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); مما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of the omitted postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. a share; the clause ترك is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; الوالدان is the fāʿil (agent) and الأقربون is conjoined to it. The meaning is: and for each of these whom We made heirs (موالي) there is a share of the inheritance left. This is the best of the aspects with respect to meaning, but, as you have seen, it requires many implied elements. Next to it in quality is that «لكل» be a fronted object of جعلنا, موالي a second mafʿūl bihi, and what «كل» is annexed to be wealth, i.e. for every [piece of] wealth We have made heirs; and مما ترك is an adjective; and this has its problems. Some of what the leading scholars said will come in the section of Benefits. (وَالَّذِينَ عَقَدَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ فَآتُوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ): the واو is resumptive; الذين is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ; the clause عقدت أيمانكم is the ṣila; the فاء is linking because of the flavour of condition in the relative noun; the clause آتوهم is the khabar of الذين; the هاء is the first mafʿūl bihi and نصيبهم the second mafʿūl bihi. The واو may also be conjunctive, with الذين nominative, conjoined to الوالدان and الأقربون. الذين may also be accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), i.e. the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, as in: زيدا فاضربه. Some parsed it as conjoined to موالي, and Abū al-Baqāʾ chose this. There are many other views which we have passed over. The object of عقدت is omitted, i.e. عقدتهم (made a pact with them), and the attribution is figurative, as will come in the section of Rhetoric. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيداً): إن and its noun; the clause كان is the khabar of إن; على كل شيء is attached to «شهيدا»; شهيدا is the khabar of the defective كان. (الرِّجالُ قَوَّامُونَ عَلَى النِّساءِ بِما فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بَعْضَهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ): resumptive speech introduced to explain the reason for men being entitled to more in inheritance, for which one may refer to the well-known sources. الرجال is a mubtadaʾ and قوامون its khabar; على النساء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قوامون, i.e. they undertake the management of their affairs and the earning of their livelihoods, so that the mother is enabled to turn to the affairs of her house, or to practise the work that is in harmony with her nature; and everyone is facilitated for that for which he was created, as has come in the ḥadīth. بما فضل is also attached to قوامون; the باء is causal and a preposition; ما is maṣdar-forming or relative, and the clause after it has no grammatical position on both suppositions. الله is the fāʿil, بعضهم the object, and على بعض is attached to فضل. (وَبِما أَنْفَقُوا مِنْ أَمْوالِهِمْ): conjoined to what preceded. (فَالصَّالِحاتُ قانِتاتٌ حافِظاتٌ لِلْغَيْبِ): the فاء is resumptive, serving as a ramification of what preceded; الصالحات is a mubtadaʾ, قانتات a first khabar and حافظات a second khabar; للغيب is attached to حافظات. (بِما حَفِظَ اللَّهُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to حافظات; ما is maṣdar-forming, i.e. because of Allah's guarding of them, since He protected them and enabled them to guard [what is due] in their husbands' absence. ما may also be made relative in the sense of الذي, with the referential pronoun omitted, i.e. by what Allah has secured for them of their husbands' dowries and maintenance; the clause after «ما» has no grammatical position. (وَاللَّاتِي تَخافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ): the واو is resumptive; اللاتي is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ; the clause تخافون نشوزهن is the ṣila; نشوزهن is a mafʿūl bihi. (فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَاهْجُرُوهُنَّ فِي الْمَضاجِعِ وَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ): the فاء is linking because of the flavour of condition in the relative noun; عظوهن is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object, and the clause is the khabar of the relative noun; اهجروهن is conjoined to عظوهن; في المضاجع is attached to اهجروهن; اضربوهن is also conjoined. (فَإِنْ أَطَعْنَكُمْ فَلا تَبْغُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ سَبِيلًا): the فاء is resumptive; إن is conditional; أطعنكم is a past verb, the nūn being the fāʿil and the كاف a mafʿūl bihi, and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the فاء links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); لا is prohibitive; تبغوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; عليهن is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of «سبيلا» and was put before it; سبيلا is a mafʿūl bihi. It is possible that «تبغوا» is from البغي, i.e. wrongdoing, the meaning being: do not wrong them; then «عليهن» is attached to an omitted ḥāl [Translator's note: so in the source], and the accusative of «سبيلا» on this view is by dropping of the preposition. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيًّا كَبِيراً): إن and its noun, and the clause كان عليا كبيرا is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz mursal (metonymic trope) in His words: «عقدت أيمانكم», whether by الأيمان is meant the hand as a limb or the oath; the relation is causality.
2- Kināya (metonymy) in His words «في المضاجع»: by it He alluded to intercourse. The discussion of kināya has been given in full before. The Arabs have many ways of alluding to intercourse, out of scruple about mentioning it, as in the words of the Exalted: «هن لباس لكم وأنتم لباس لهن», and in poetry the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وصرنا إلى الحسنى ورقّ كلامنا ... ورضت فذلّت صعبة أي إذلال
(We came to what is best, our speech grew tender, and I tamed a refractory one, and she became submissive — what submission!)
So the taming of the woman, her submission, and the softening of her speech from breathlessness and excess of desire is a metonymy for that, of the utmost beauty and chastity. Among the curious metonymies relating to beds is what is related of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ: he married his son ʿAbd Allāh [to a woman], and the woman stayed with him three nights without his coming near her, as he was devoted only to his prayer. ʿAmr went in to her after three [nights] and said: "How do you find your husband?" She said: "An excellent husband, except that he has not searched a side of ours nor approached a bed of ours" — a metonymy whose like is rare.

An example between excellence and failure:
Among the badly used metonymies for intercourse is the saying of al-Mutanabbī:
إني على شغفي بما في خمرها ... لأعفّ عمّا في سراويلاتها
(For all my passion for what lies beneath her veil, I am chaste regarding what lies in her trousers.)
He wanted to allude to integrity and chastity, but fell into what is considered worse than lewdness, namely his words «عما في سراويلاتها». Al-Sharīf al-Raḍī took this meaning and brought it out in the most beautiful form and the chastest and noblest wording, where he said:
أحن إلى ما تضمر الخمر والحلا ... وأصدف عما في ضمان المآزر
(I yearn for what veils and ornaments conceal, and turn away from what the waist-wrappers hold in trust.)

And al-Sharīf fell into error:
Yet al-Sharīf al-Raḍī did not escape error either. He composed an ode consoling Abū Saʿd ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Khalaf on the death of his brother, namely:
إن لم تكن نصلا فغمد نصال ... غالته أحداث الزمان بغول
(If you were not a blade, you were the sheath of blades, which the events of time have destroyed with a calamity.)
In this there is a badness of metonymy that is not hidden, for the imagination races to what is ugly to mention. The fact is that al-Sharīf al-Raḍī wanted to glance at the sky of al-Farazdaq in three verses he said when a slave-girl of his died while pregnant, namely:
وجفن سلاح قد رزئت فلم أنح ... عليه ولم أبعث إليه البواكيا
وفي جوفه من دارم ذو حفيظة ... لو أن المنايا أمهلته لياليا
ولكن رأيت الدهر يعثر بالفتى ... ولا يستطيع ردّ ما كان جائيا
(Many a sheath of a weapon have I been bereaved of, yet I did not wail over it nor send the weeping women to it; and in its belly was one of Dārim, jealous of honour, had the fates granted him respite for some nights. But I have seen that time stumbles upon the young man, and he cannot repel what was to come.)
This is fine in meaning and beautiful in composition; and al-Sharīf came, for all the loftiness of his taste and the delicacy of his sensibility, and fell into this lapse in taking over his metonymy.

* Benefits:
We find it useful to cite [several] aspects, among them what Abū Ḥayyān cited in his exegesis al-Baḥr. Among these aspects is that «لكل» is attached to جعلنا, and the pronoun in «ترك» refers to «كل», which is annexed to [an implied] "human being", the implied form being: and He made for every human being an inheritance from what he left. So «مما» is attached to the verbal sense in the meaning of «موالي», or to an implied verb explained by the meaning, the implied form being: they inherit from what he left; the clause is complete at His words «مما ترك», and «الوالدان» is nominative, as though it were said: "And who is the heir?" and it was said: "They are the parents and the nearest relatives"; so the speech is two clauses. Among those aspects is that the implied form is: and We made for every human being heirs (موالي), i.e. inheritors; then a verb was implied, i.e. the heirs inherit from what the parents left; so the agent of «ترك» is «الوالدان». It is as though, since He was vague in His words "and We made for every human being heirs", however that human being for whom heirs were made is the parents and the nearest relatives [Translator's note: so in the source («بيد أن»), probably for «بيّن أن», "He made clear that"]; so those heirs inherit from what their parents and nearest relatives left, and the parents and nearest relatives are the ones inherited from. On these two aspects there is no implied omitted element in «جعلنا»; the object of «جعلنا» is the word «موالي», and the speech is two clauses. Perhaps unravelling talismans is easier than these intertwined aspects; the speech is inimitable, and the rules came following the language, so however far they extend and broaden, they do not cover or comprehend all its constructions.

A sound opinion of al-Shawkānī:
After writing the above, I came upon a sound opinion of al-Shawkānī, and I wished to conclude the discussion of this wondrous verse with it. He said: «That is: We made for every human being heirs, kinsmen (موالي) who take charge of his inheritance; «لكل» is a second object put before the verb to emphasise comprehensiveness. This clause confirms the content of what preceded it, i.e. so that everyone follows what Allah has apportioned to him of inheritance and does not covet what Allah has favoured others with over him.»
But it is truncated and evidently patched together, as though he became exasperated after hovering around the preserve without falling into it. The speech of Allah is too vast to be bounded by limits, or for minds to fathom its folds; so reflect.

dervis-irab:128-130.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النشوز): turning away from her and estrangement from her; withholding from her his person, his trust and his love, while his eyes aspire to one more beautiful than her.
(الإعراض): that he reduce his conversation with her, his companionship with her and his sharing her bed.
(المعلقة): she who is neither with a husband nor divorced. A woman poet said:
هل هي إلا حظة أو تطليق ... أو صلف أو بين ذاك تعليق
(Is it anything but favour, or divorce, or disfavour, or — between these — being left hanging?)
This is a delightful verse: the poetess decries the state of the wife with her husband and describes it as nothing but a small favour (ḥiẓẓa), when the husband favours her, or divorcing her, or ṣalaf, i.e. not being favoured by the husband — one says nisāʾ ṣalāʾif and ṣālifāt: women whom the husband does not favour — or being left hanging between those states mentioned.
Al-ḥaẓẓ is share and fortune, and perhaps al-ḥiẓẓa is the singular of al-ḥaẓẓ. Ṣalifat al-marʾa ṣalafan: when she was not favoured by her husband and he disliked her.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِها نُشُوزاً أَوْ إِعْراضاً) The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, to establish one of the most important rulings and to treat a most serious social issue. (إن) [the source prints وأن] is conditional; (امرأة) is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it. It is not permissible to put it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), because the condition demands a verb. The clause (خافت من بعلها) is explicative (mufassira) and has no grammatical position. (من بعلها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خافت), or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of «نشوزا», and when it was placed before it, it was parsed as a ḥāl. (نشوزا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (إعراضا) is conjoined to «نشوزا». (فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِما أَنْ يُصْلِحا بَيْنَهُما صُلْحاً) The fāʾ is connective; (لا) is the lā of generic negation and (جناح) its noun; (عليهما) is attached to its omitted khabar (predicate). (أن يصلحا بينهما) is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: in that they reconcile; the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (جناح) or to an omitted adjective of it. (بينهما) is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was an adjective of «صلحا», then the adjective was placed before the noun described and so was parsed as a ḥāl. (صلحا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The details of reconciliation are treated at length in the books of jurisprudence. (وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ) The wāw is parenthetical, and the clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar is parenthetical with no grammatical position. (وَأُحْضِرَتِ الْأَنْفُسُ الشُّحَّ) The wāw is also parenthetical; (أحضرت) is a passive past verb, (الأنفس) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and (الشح) is the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is also parenthetical. (وَإِنْ تُحْسِنُوا وَتَتَّقُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيراً) The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; (إن) is conditional, (تحسنوا) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ (protasis), and (تتقوا) is conjoined to it. The jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis) is omitted because it is known, i.e.: then doing good and being mindful [of Allah] is better. The fāʾ is causal (taʿlīliyya); (إن) and its noun, and the clause (كان) is its khabar; (بما تعملون) is attached to «خبيرا»; the clause (تعملون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and (خبيرا) is the khabar of (كان). (وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّساءِ) The wāw is resumptive; (لن) is a particle of negation, subjunctive and futurity; (تستطيعوا) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by (لن), the sign of its subjunctive being the dropping of the nūn; (أن تعدلوا) is an interpreted maṣdar, a mafʿūl bihi of (تستطيعوا); and (بين النساء) is an adverb attached to (تعدلوا). (وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ) The wāw is circumstantial — some call it the connective wāw (waṣliyya); (لو) is conditional, and (حرصتم) is a verb and its fāʿil. (فَلا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ فَتَذَرُوها كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ) The fāʾ is al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e.: if you know that, then do not incline; so the clause has no grammatical position. (لا) is prohibitive, and (تميلوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا); (كل الميل) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq. (فتذروها): the fāʾ is that of causation (al-sababiyya), so (تذروها) is in the subjunctive by an implied (muḍmara) an after it, because it occurs in the answer to a prohibition. It is also permissible for the fāʾ to be a conjunction, so that «تذروها» is jussive by being conjoined to (تميلوا). (كالمعلقة): the kāf is a noun meaning "like", so it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in (تذروها); or it is a preposition, so that the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, as stated before, i.e.:
resembling the one left hanging. (وَإِنْ تُصْلِحُوا وَتَتَّقُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً) The i'rab of its like was given shortly before. (وَإِنْ يَتَفَرَّقا يُغْنِ اللَّهُ كُلًّا مِنْ سَعَتِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (يتفرقا) is the protasis, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil; (يغن) is the apodosis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; (الله) is the fāʿil, (كلّا) a mafʿūl bihi, and (من سعته) is attached to «يغن». (وَكانَ اللَّهُ واسِعاً حَكِيماً) Its i'rab has been given many times.

* Benefits:
1- When what is the agent in meaning occurs after a particle that is specific to verbs, it is parsed as the fāʿil of an omitted verb explained by the verb mentioned after it, because the specificity of these particles to the verb requires that — otherwise a contradiction would occur. That is like the conditional particles.
