The Kufans and some Basrans allowed parsing it as a mubtadaʾ, the beginning with it being permissible when it is indefinite and the conditional particle precedes it. As for when the particle wavers between the verb and the noun, as in «أبشر يهدوننا» (Shall human beings guide us?), it is permissible to parse «بشر» as a mubtadaʾ — and this is preferable — with the clause (يهدوننا) as its khabar; and it is permissible to parse it as the fāʿil of an omitted verb explained by the verb mentioned after it, namely «يهدوننا», because the interrogative hamza alternates between both the noun and the verb.
2- It is permissible to omit a known protasis when the particle is «إن» or «من» while it is joined with the negating «لا», as in the saying of al-Aḥwaṣ:
فطلّقها فلست لها بكفء ... وإلا يعل مفرقك الحسام
(So divorce her, for you are no match for her; and if not, the sword will come down on the parting of your hair.)
i.e.: and if you do not divorce her, the sword will come down on the parting of your hair. One of the two — «إن» and the joining with lā — may be absent, and both may be absent together. The first is what Ibn al-Anbārī related in al-Inṣāf from the Arabs: "Whoever greets you, greet him; and whoever not, then pay him no heed", i.e.: and whoever does not greet you, pay him no heed. The second is like: «وإن امرأة خافت من بعلها نشوزا», where the protasis was omitted while the joining with «لا» is absent, i.e.: "and if a woman feared — feared ...".
The third is like his saying:
متى تؤخذوا قسرا بظنّة عامر ... ولم ينج إلا في الصفاد أسير
(Whenever you are taken by force on the suspicion of ʿĀmir, and no captive escapes except in fetters.)
i.e.: whenever you are caught, you are taken; so the protasis was omitted with both matters absent.

dervis-irab:41-42.t:
* I'rab:
(فَكَيْفَ إِذا جِئْنا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ): The فاء is resumptive, and كيف is an interrogative noun. In a construction like this it admits of two analyses and no third: first, that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "how is their state?"; second, that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of an omitted element, i.e. "how will they act?". إذا is an adverb of time attached to this omitted element, and the clause جئنا is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct). من كل is attached to an omitted element functioning as ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of شهيد that was then placed before it; بشهيد is attached to جئنا. There is also a third analysis, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported from Makkī, namely that «كيف» is governed by جئنا. (وَجِئْنا بِكَ عَلى هؤُلاءِ شَهِيداً): The واو is a conjunction; جئنا is a verb and agent, and the two are conjoined to the first جئنا; بك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جئنا; على هؤلاء is attached to «شهيدا»; and شهيدا is a ḥāl. (يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): The adverb is attached to يودّ. إذ is an adverb annexed to the adverb, and the adverb and the tanwīn are a compensation for a clause. [Translator's note: the source reads "annexed to the adverb"; the sense is that it is annexed to the omitted clause, for which the tanwīn compensates.] The implied sense is: "on the day when We bring a witness from every nation and bring you as a witness against these, those who disbelieved will wish". The clause يود is resumptive, and the clause كفروا is a ṣila (relative clause). (وَعَصَوُا الرَّسُولَ لَوْ تُسَوَّى بِهِمُ الْأَرْضُ): The واو is a conjunction; عصوا الرسول is conjoined to كفروا. لو is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya) after a verb of wishing, and together with what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar functioning as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يود, i.e. "they wish that the earth be levelled over them so that they are buried in it"; and الأرض is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of تسوّى. (وَلا يَكْتُمُونَ اللَّهَ حَدِيثاً): It is conjoined to «يود», and it may also be resumptive. يكتمون is an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marking being the retention of the nūn; and الله is accusative by removal of the preposition, and حديثا is a mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "they do not conceal from Allah any statement". Some scholars permitted that the name of Majesty (الله) be a mafʿūl bihi of يكتمون, because in their view it takes two objects.

* Benefits:
The tanwīn attached to annexed adverbs such as يومئذ, حينئذ and عندئذ is called the nūn of compensation (nūn al-taʿwīḍ), because it is a compensation for a clause, as you saw in the section on i'rab. Then two quiescent letters meet, the dhāl of «إذ» and the tanwīn, so the dhāl is given a kasra according to the basic rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters. This kasra is not a kasra of i'rab, because «إذ» is permanently indeclinable. Nor is the annexation in «يومئذ» and the like an annexation of one synonym to another; rather it is the annexation of the more general to the more specific, as in "shajar arāk" (the tree of arāk).

dervis-irab:43-43.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جُنُباً): well known. The masculine and feminine, the singular, dual and plural are alike in it, because it is a noun that has taken on the role of the verbal noun, which is al-ijnāb. This is the well-known and eloquent usage in the language, and the Qur'an came with it. They have also formed a sound plural of it with wāw and nūn in the nominative and yāʾ and nūn in the accusative and genitive, saying "qawm junubūn"; and a broken plural, saying "qawm ajnāb"; and as for the dual, they said "junubān".
(الْغائِطِ): originally the wide, low-lying hollow of land. When a man wished to relieve himself, he would go to a hollow (ghāʾiṭ) of the ground, so everyone who had an occurrence of ritual impurity came to be described as "taghawwaṭa", out of modesty about mentioning the impurity.
(الصعيد): earth. Tayammum with ṣaʿīd is originally "deliberate intent"; one says "tayammamtuka", "taʾammamtuka" and "amamtuka". Then they used this word so often that tayammum came to mean wiping the face and hands with earth. The basis of all this is the surface of the ground, free of plants, trees and buildings, and level. From it comes the saying of Dhū l-Rumma:
كأنه بالضحى ترمي الصعيد به ... دبابة في عظام الرأس خرطوم
(As if, in the forenoon, a she-camel with a long nose, in the bones of the head, were casting the ground with it.) He means: casting it onto the surface of the earth.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the i'rab of its like has already been given. (لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكارى): A resumptive statement, introduced to forbid prayer in a state of drunkenness. لا is prohibitive; تقربوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, and the واو is the agent; الصلاة is a mafʿūl bihi; the واو in وأنتم is the wāw of ḥāl; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and سكارى is its khabar. (حَتَّى تَعْلَمُوا ما تَقُولُونَ): حتى is a particle of limit and of genitive; تعلموا is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after حتى; ما is a relative noun and mafʿūl bihi, though ما may also be maṣdar-forming, in which case the interpreted maṣdar is the mafʿūl bihi. أن and what follows it are in the interpretation of a maṣdar governed in the genitive by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تقربوا. (وَلا جُنُباً إِلَّا عابِرِي سَبِيلٍ حَتَّى تَغْتَسِلُوا): It is conjoined to His words وأنتم سكارى, for that is a clause whose position is accusative as ḥāl from the agent of تقربوا, as if it had been said: "do not approach the prayer drunk, nor in a state of major impurity". إلا is a particle of restriction; عابري سبيل is an exception from all the states of those addressed, so it is accusative as ḥāl. The two ḥāls are combined to show that there are two states, as if it had been said: "do not approach the prayer in a state of major impurity unless there is with you another state in which you are excused, namely travel"; and "crossing a way" is an expression for travelling. «حتى تغتسلوا» is like «حتى تعلموا», and it is attached to the verb of prohibition. (وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضى أَوْ عَلى سَفَرٍ): The واو is a conjunction, and إن is conditional; كنتم: كان is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the تاء is its ism; مرضى is its khabar; أو is a conjunction; and the preposition and its genitive noun على سفر are in the position of accusative, conjoined to مرضى. (أَوْ جاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِنَ الْغائِطِ): أو is a conjunction; جاء is conjoined to what preceded; أحد is the agent; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element functioning as naʿt of أحد; and من الغائط is attached to جاء. (أَوْ لامَسْتُمُ النِّساءَ): Conjoined as well. So those who fall under the ruling of the condition are four, and more explanation of these rulings will come in Sūrat al-Māʾida; they are the sick, travellers, those who have had a minor impurity, and those in a state of major impurity. (فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا ماءً): The فاء is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to كنتم. (فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيداً طَيِّباً): The فاء links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); تيمموا is an imperative verb and the واو is the agent; صعيدا is a mafʿūl bihi and طيبا a naʿt; and the clause فتيمموا is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (فَامْسَحُوا بِوُجُوهِكُمْ وَأَيْدِيكُمْ): The فاء is a conjunction; امسحوا is conjoined to تيمموا; بوجوهكم is attached to امسحوا. Sībawayh reported: "masaḥtu raʾsahu" and "masaḥtu biraʾsihi". And أيديكم is conjoined to وجوهكم. Some grammarians said the باء denotes partitiveness (tabʿīḍ), and counted among such cases His words «عينا يشرب بها عباد الله», and the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
فلثمت فاها آخذا بقرونها ... شرب النزيف ببرد ماء الحشرج
(I kissed her mouth, taking hold of her locks, drinking like one dazed from the coolness of the water of al-Ḥashraj.)
Others said it denotes instrumentality (istiʿāna). All of that is acceptable. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَفُوًّا غَفُوراً): إن and its ism; and كان with its ism and khabar are the khabar of إنّ.

* Rhetoric:
1- Euphemism (kināya) in His words: من الغائط, for He used a euphemism for what is distasteful to mention; and "touching" (mulāmasa) for sexual intercourse, according to one of the two views. This will come in detail in al-Māʾida.
2- Iltifāt (shift of person) in His words: «أو جاء أحد», for He shifted from the second person to the third, because it is a euphemism for what one is ashamed to mention, so He did not address them with it. This is among the finer points of speech.

dervis-irab:176-176.t:
* I'rab:
(يَسْتَفْتُونَكَ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِي الْكَلالَةِ) A resumptive speech, introduced to mention the inheritance of full brothers and sisters, or of paternal ones. يستفتونك is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), with its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object). قل is an imperative verb, its fāʿil being "you" (أنت). والله is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ويفتيكم is an imperfect verb with its object, its fāʿil being "he" (هو), and the sentence is the khabar (predicate). The sentence الله يفتيكم is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). في الكلالة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يستفتونك, on the view that the first verb governs (iʿmāl al-awwal), or to يفتيكم, on the view that the second verb governs.
(إِنِ امْرُؤٌ هَلَكَ لَيْسَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَلَهُ أُخْتٌ) A resumptive speech, to set out the ruling in detail. إن is conditional. امرؤ is the fāʿil of an omitted verb that the following verb explains, and the sentence هلك is explicative, with no grammatical position. وليس is a defective past verb (kāna and its sisters); وله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted advanced predicate; ولد is its postponed subject (ism), and the sentence is a naʿt (adjective) of امرؤ. له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted advanced predicate, and أخت is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the sentence is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause because it occurs after the wāw of ḥāl.
(فَلَها نِصْفُ ما تَرَكَ) The fāʾ is the one that links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ولها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted advanced predicate; نصف is a postponed mubtadaʾ; ما is a relative noun, in the genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi; the sentence ترك is the ṣila (relative clause). The sentence joined by the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive (jazm) as the apodosis.
(وَهُوَ يَرِثُها إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَها وَلَدٌ) The wāw is resumptive; هو is a mubtadaʾ and the sentence يرثها is its khabar. إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussion; ويكن is a defective imperfect verb, jussive because of لم, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ولها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted advanced khabar of يكن; ولد is its postponed subject. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, that is: فهو يرثها ("so he inherits from her").
(فَإِنْ كانَتَا اثْنَتَيْنِ) The fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; وكانتا is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, the alif in «كانتا» being its subject (ism), and اثنتين its khabar.
(فَلَهُمَا الثُّلُثانِ مِمَّا تَرَكَ) The fāʾ is the linking one; ولهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted advanced predicate; والثلثان is a postponed mubtadaʾ; ومما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the sentence ترك is a ṣila; and the sentence joined by the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. The fāʿil of ترك is latent (mustatir), referring back to "the brother" (الأخ).
(وَإِنْ كانُوا إِخْوَةً رِجالًا وَنِساءً فَلِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; وكانوا is the protasis, the wāw being its subject and إخوة its khabar. ورجالا is a badal (substitute) from «إخوة», and ونساء is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to «رجالا». The fāʾ links the apodosis; وللذكر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted advanced predicate; ومثل حظ الأنثيين is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the sentence is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis.
(يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ) The sentence is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and you may also take it as a resumptive explanatory one. يبين الله is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; ولكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يبين. أن تضلوا is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with an omitted muḍāf, that is: "out of dislike that you go astray" (كراهية أن تضلوا). The object of يبين is omitted, and it is general. والله: the wāw is resumptive; والله is a mubtadaʾ; بكل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to his word «عليم», and عليم is the khabar of «الله».

* Benefits:
Sūrat al-Nisāʾ was closed with the mention of wealth and the rulings on inheritance, just as it was opened with it, so that there would be a correspondence (mushākala) between beginning and end. [Translator's note: the source reads «صورة النساء» ("the form/image of al-Nisāʾ"), apparently a misprint for «سورة النساء» ("Sūrat al-Nisāʾ"); translated as the latter.] The verses on inheritance in the sūra come down to three:
1- The first, on the inheritance of ascendants and descendants.
2- The second, on the inheritance of spouses and of maternal brothers and sisters.
3- The third, which is this verse, on the inheritance of full brothers and sisters, or paternal ones.
As for the blood relatives (ulū al-arḥām), their ruling will come in Sūrat al-Anfāl. The one who asked for a ruling on the kalāla was Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allah, when the Prophet ﷺ visited him in his illness and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a kalāla, so what should I do with my wealth?" Then this verse was revealed.

A selection of the sayings of the philologists on the kalāla:
It was said: the original sense of kalāla in the language is whatever is not of lineage by direct attachment (laḥḥ), that is, attached without an intermediary. It was said: it is whatever kin there is apart from the father and the child. It was said: whatever is apart from the child only. It was said: maternal brothers. In Lisān al-ʿArab, when mentioning the word as it is used, he said: It was said: the kalāla, of the agnatic relatives, is the one with whom the brothers inherit; and this word is applied to the deceased whom a male relative inherits; and it was said: rather, to the heirs other than those mentioned; and it was said: to each of the two. What decides is the contextual indication. The majority hold that the kalāla, among those who are inherited from, is the one who has neither child nor father. This much, then; the rulings on the kalāla are set out at length in the large works, and there is no room for them here.

The last verse revealed:
Al-Bukhārī and Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and others reported on the authority of al-Barāʾ, who said: The last sūra revealed in full was Sūrat Barāʾa, that is, al-Tawba, and the last verse revealed was the closing verse of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: «يستفتونك قل الله يفتيكم في الكلالة», that is, one of the verses on the obligatory shares. There is therefore no contradiction with what al-Bukhārī reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The last verse revealed was the verse on usury. Moreover, there is no way to be certain of the last verse of the Qur'an revealed; we say only that this verse is certainly among the last revealed, and it is possible that it was the very last of all. And Allah knows best.

dervis-irab:142-143.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُذَبْذَبِينَ): al-mudhabdhab is the one who is driven away (yadhubbu) from both sides, that is, he is repelled and pushed away, so he settles on neither one side. In dhabdhaba there is a repetition that is not in dhabba, as though the repetition of the letters signals a repetition of the meaning: they are swayed back and forth, tossed about in a flood of bewilderment; whenever desire inclines them to one side they are pushed to the other.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ يُخادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَهُوَ خادِعُهُمْ)
A resumptive statement, offered to explain another pattern of their ugly deeds. إنّ and its noun; the clause يخادعون الله is its khabar (predicate). The wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial); هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and خادعهم its khabar, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (وَإِذا قامُوا إِلَى الصَّلاةِ قامُوا كُسالى)
The wāw is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the clause قاموا is in the position of a genitive as the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); إلى الصلاة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قاموا; the second clause قاموا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; كسالى is a ḥāl. (يُراؤُنَ النَّاسَ وَلا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا)
The clause is a ḥāl clause. The matter was confused for Abū al-Baqāʾ, so he parsed it as a badal (substitute) for «كسالى»; yet it is neither the whole of it, nor part of it, nor is it contained in it. The original of يراءون is يرائيون, to which the well-known weakening (iʿlāl) was applied. الناس is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ولا يذكرون الله is conjoined to يراءون الناس; إلا is a particle of restriction; قليلا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), that is, "a little remembrance", or an adverbial, that is, "a little time". (مُذَبْذَبِينَ بَيْنَ ذلِكَ) مذبذبين is a ḥāl, because it is a derived noun; بين is an adverb attached to مذبذبين; ذلك is a muḍāf ilayhi; the pointing refers to disbelief and belief. (لا إِلى هؤُلاءِ وَلا إِلى هؤُلاءِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "not ascribed to these nor to those". (وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ سَبِيلًا) The wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; يضلل الله is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is the connective, and the clause لن تجد له سبيلا is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar of «من».

* Rhetoric:
1- Mushākala (correspondence of expression) in His saying: «وهو خادعهم». It has already come up, so renew your acquaintance with it. Here the punishment and recompense is named by the name of the offence.
2- Jinās al-taḥrīf (paronomasia by alteration): this is where the two elements of the pair are alike in wording but one differs from the other in form, and that is in His saying: «مذبذبين بين ذلك». Among its examples in poetry is the saying of Ṣafī al-Dīn al-Ḥillī: شديد البأس في أمر مطاع ... مضارب كل أقوام مطاعن (Mighty in valour in a command that is obeyed … a striker [with the sword] against every people, a thruster [with the spear]).

dervis-irab:144-146.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الدرك): with sukūn on the rā' or with fatḥa: the furthest depth of a thing; one says "the diver reached the bottom (darak) of the sea". Al-Ḥarīrī said in Durrat al-Ghawwāṣ: they say of that which one descends in by steps, darak, and of that which one ascends by, daraj. In the ḥadīth: «Paradise has levels (darajāt) and the Fire has depths (darakāt).» Some have objected to him, saying that the matter in this is easy, because what is descended by can also be ascended by.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) The i'rab of this vocative has already been given, so renew your acquaintance with it. (لا تَتَّخِذُوا الْكافِرِينَ أَوْلِياءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) A resumptive statement, offered to forbid taking disbelievers as allies and intimate friends. لا is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); الكافرين is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and أولياء the second mafʿūl bihi; من دون المؤمنين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of أولياء. (أَتُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ سُلْطاناً مُبِيناً) A resumptive statement, offered as a rebuke to them for their inclination to establish a proof against themselves with their own hands. The hamza is for rebuking interrogation; تريدون is an imperfect verb with its agent; أن تجعلوا: the interpreted maṣdar from أن and what is within its scope is the object of تريدون; لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجعلوا, serving as the first object; عليكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl; سلطانا is the second mafʿūl bihi of تجعلوا; مبينا is an adjective. (إِنَّ الْمُنافِقِينَ فِي الدَّرْكِ الْأَسْفَلِ مِنَ النَّارِ) The clause is resumptive, to explain the destination of the hypocrites, which is the lowest depth of the Fire.
إنّ and its noun; في الدرك is attached to an omitted khabar of إن; الأسفل is an adjective of الدرك; من النار is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُمْ نَصِيراً) The wāw is a conjunction; لن is a particle of negation, accusative and future; تجد is an imperfect verb accusative by لن; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «نصيرا»; نصيرا is the object of تجد. (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا) إلا is a particle of exception; الذين is the excepted; the clause of exception is a ḥāl clause; the clause تابوا has no position as the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (وَأَصْلَحُوا وَاعْتَصَمُوا بِاللَّهِ وَأَخْلَصُوا دِينَهُمْ لِلَّهِ) Conjoined to تابوا; دينهم is the object of أخلصوا; لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخلصوا. (فَأُولئِكَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; مع is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar of أولئك; المؤمنين is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the yāʾ. (وَسَوْفَ يُؤْتِ اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَجْراً عَظِيماً) The wāw is resumptive; سوف is a particle of futurity; يؤتي الله is a verb and agent; المؤمنين is the first mafʿūl bihi and أجرا the second; عظيما is an adjective.

dervis-irab:147-147.t:
* I'rab:
(ما يَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ بِعَذابِكُمْ) A resumptive statement, offered to establish that Allah, glory be to Him, draws no benefit to Himself by punishing you, nor does He ward off any harm from Himself by it. So what need has He of your punishment? ما is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يفعل; يفعل الله is an imperfect verb and agent; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يفعل; the interrogative here has the meaning of negation, and the clause is resumptive, offered to add to the rebuke of them. (إِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ وَآمَنْتُمْ) إن is conditional; شكرتم is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then you have avoided the punishment", and the clause is also resumptive; آمنتم is conjoined to شكرتم. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ شاكِراً عَلِيماً) The wāw is resumptive; كان with its noun and its two khabars.

* Benefits:
Gratitude (shukr) on the part of Allah is being pleased with the little of His servants' deeds and multiplying the reward for this little. Gratitude on the part of servants is obedience.

A glimpse of the hypocrites:
The scholars agreed that the hypocrite is one who displays belief and conceals disbelief.
They agreed that the hypocrite is more severely punished than the disbeliever, because he equals him in disbelief and adds to his disbelief the mocking of Islam and its people, the befriending of the disbelievers, and the extending of hands of submission to them, a clear proof of hypocrisy. From him, peace be upon him: Three things, whoever has them is a hypocrite, even if he prays and fasts: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays. Ḥudhayfa was asked: Who is the hypocrite? He said: The one who describes Islam but does not act by it.

dervis-irab:148-149.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْجَهْرَ): raising the voice in speech and other things. Also: jahara al-arḍ: he traversed it without knowing it; jahara al-shayʾ: he uncovered it and estimated it; jahara al-amr: the matter became public and spread.

* I'rab:
(لا يُحِبُّ اللَّهُ الْجَهْرَ بِالسُّوءِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ) A resumptive statement, offered to alert the sensible person to busy himself with himself and to speak openly of his own faults before searching for the faults of people. لا is a negative particle; يحب الله الجهر is an imperfect verb, agent and object; بالسوء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to الجهر; من القول is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from السوء. (إِلَّا مَنْ ظُلِمَ) إلا is a particle of exception and من is the excepted, a discontinuous exception (munqaṭiʿ), because the open speech of the wronged person is not counted among those who speak openly of evil speech. It is also permissible that it be continuous (muttaṣil) on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, that is, "except the open speech of one who was wronged", or that it be in the position of a nominative as a badal (substitute) for the agent of the maṣdar, which is al-jahr. The meaning: He does not love that anyone speak openly of evil, except one who was wronged, so he speaks openly, that is, he calls upon Allah to remove the evil that befell him. ظلم is passive, that is, Allah does not hold him to account for speaking openly of it by informing of the wrong of his wrongdoer and invoking against him. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعاً عَلِيماً) The wāw is resumptive; كان with its noun; سميعا is its first khabar and عليما its second khabar. (إِنْ تُبْدُوا خَيْراً أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ أَوْ تَعْفُوا عَنْ سُوءٍ) The clause is resumptive; إن is conditional; تبدوا is the protasis and the wāw is the agent; خيرا is the mafʿūl bihi; أو is a conjunction; تعفوا is conjoined to تبدوا; عن سوء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تعفوا. (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَفُوًّا قَدِيراً) The fāʾ is the connective; إن and its noun; the clause of كان with its latent noun and its two khabars is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of إن; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis. It is a justification for the omitted apodosis, that is: "pardoning is better, and it is closer [to piety]".

dervis-irab:150-151.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ) The clause is resumptive, offered to show that the way is clear, with no obscurity. إن and its noun; the clause يكفرون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; بالله is attached to يكفرون; ورسله is conjoined to الله. (وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُفَرِّقُوا بَيْنَ اللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ) Conjoined to يكفرون; أن and what follows it are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بين is an adverb attached to يفرقوا, and the exalted name is a muḍāf ilayhi; ورسله is conjoined to the exalted name. (وَيَقُولُونَ: نُؤْمِنُ بِبَعْضٍ وَنَكْفُرُ بِبَعْضٍ) Conjoined to what precedes; the clause نؤمن ببعض etc. is the quoted speech; ببعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نؤمن, and the second is attached to نكفر. (وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا بَيْنَ ذلِكَ سَبِيلًا) Conjoined to the first يريدون; أن and what follows it are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, the first mafʿūl bihi; the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl, and the pointing refers to disbelief and belief; سبيلا is the second mafʿūl bihi. (أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْكافِرُونَ حَقًّا) The demonstrative is the first mubtadaʾ; هم is the second mubtadaʾ; الكافرون is the khabar of «هم»; the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative; the clause of the demonstrative and what follows it is the khabar of إن; حقا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) to confirm the content of the sentence, the implied form being "that is truly true". Al-Wāḥidī's objection that disbelief can never be "true" in any respect is not valid, because "true" here does not mean the opposite of false; what is meant is that it is certainly so. (وَأَعْتَدْنا لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذاباً مُهِيناً) The wāw is resumptive; أعتدنا is a verb and agent; للكافرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعتدنا; عذابا is a mafʿūl bihi and مهينا an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «للكافرين» is the art of using the overt noun in place of the pronoun, to censure them and to give concrete form to their disbelief, as though it were something seen with the eye.

dervis-irab:152-152.t:
* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ) The wāw is resumptive; الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila; بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنوا; ورسله is conjoined to الله. (وَلَمْ يُفَرِّقُوا بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction and the clause is conjoined to آمنوا, falling within the scope of the ṣila; بين is an adverb attached to يفرقوا. بين entered upon أحد although an adverb of this kind requires a plural, because أحد is general in that it occurs in a negative context; the meaning is "they did not differentiate between two of them or between a group of them"; منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of أحد. (أُولئِكَ سَوْفَ يُؤْتِيهِمْ أُجُورَهُمْ) The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; the clause سوف يؤتيهم is its khabar, and the nominal clause is the khabar of the relative «الذين». (وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً) Its i'rab has already been given.

dervis-irab:71-72.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الحذر) with kasra on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the dhāl, or with fatḥa on both: vigilance and guarding against a feared thing.
(ثُباتٍ) with ḍamma on the thāʾ: a group of horsemen; one also says ثبوت. Its original pattern is فعلة like حطمة; its lām was dropped and the tāʾ marbūṭa of feminine marking was given in exchange for it. Whether that dropped letter is a wāw or a yāʾ is disputed (two views). In the lexicons: الثبات is the plural of ثبة, a group of men of more than ten, and it was said: of more than two. The sariyya (raiding party) is at least one hundred and at most four hundred; next comes the minsar, from four hundred to eight hundred; then the jaysh (army), from eight hundred to four thousand; then the jaḥfal, which is anything beyond that. Zuhayr said, describing a noble company and praising them:
وقد أغدو على ثبة كرام ... نشاوى واجدين لما نشاء
لهم راح وراووق ومسك ... تعلّ به جلودهم وماء
أمشي بين قتلى قد أصيبت ... نفوسهم ولم تقطر دماء
يجرّون البرود وقد تمشّت ... حميّا الكأس فيهم والغناء
(I go out in the morning among a noble company, merry, finding whatever we wish. / They have wine, a strainer, musk, and water with which their skins are perfumed over and over. / I walk among slain men whose souls were taken, though no blood has dripped. / They trail their mantles while the heat of the cup and of song courses through them.)
(انفروا) an imperative from النفر, which is alarm and sudden rush; one says نفر إليه نفرا, of the pattern ضرب and قعد. al-Aʿmash read انفروا with ḍamma on the fāʾ in both places.
(يبطئن) with shadda on the ṭāʾ: increased heaviness, slowness and lagging behind from jihad. One says بطّأ (with shadda) and أبطأ.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا خُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ فَانْفِرُوا ثُباتٍ أَوِ انْفِرُوا جَمِيعاً) A resumptive speech, meant to warn the army of the Messenger ﷺ of the dangers to which they may be exposed if they do not take their precaution. The i'rab of the vocative has already been given. خذوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) with omission of the nūn because its imperfect is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); حذركم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is a conjunction; and انفروا is conjoined to خذوا, that is: hasten upon them before they hasten upon you, and do not be slack, lest you cast yourselves into destruction with your own hands. ثبات is a ḥāl (circumstantial), marked as accusative by the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; or: انفروا is conjoined to the first انفروا, and جميعا is a ḥāl. (وَإِنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَنْ لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ) The wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, meant to address the laggards and hypocrites who were heavy and stayed behind from jihad. إن is a particle resembling the verb; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted predicate, preposed, of لمن; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), whose benefit is emphasis; من is a relative noun in the position of the accusative, the postposed noun of إن; and ليبطئن: the lām is the answer to an omitted oath, the sense being: "and among you is one who swears he will certainly lag behind." The oath and its answer are the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. يبطئن here may be intransitive, and it may be transitive with an omitted object, i.e. ليبطئنّ غيره, meaning he holds him back and stirs cowardice and panic in his soul; and these are worse than the enemies. In making them "of you" there is a generalisation required by the outward appearance, while in fact they are an enemy to you. Note that the ṣila itself is the answer to the oath, and both have no grammatical position. (فَإِنْ أَصابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ قالَ: قَدْ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ) The fāʾ is resumptive, إن is conditional, أصابتكم is a past verb in the position of the jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); مصيبة is the fāʿil; the clause قال is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the clause قد أنعم الله علي is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl). (إِذْ لَمْ أَكُنْ مَعَهُمْ شَهِيداً) إذ is an adverb of past time attached to أنعم; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; أكن is a defective imperfect verb whose noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; معهم is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl; and شهيدا is the khabar of أكن.

* Rhetoric:
1- Antithesis (ṭibāq) between ثبات and جميعا. That is: rise against the enemy and confront him as successive raiding parties or as massed squadrons, for lagging is the habit of the hypocrites.
2- Figurative usage of the mujāz mursal type in خذوا حذركم, the relation being causality, because caution, although it does not ward off destiny, is the instrument by which a man protects himself and safeguards his life.
3- The denying-type report (khabar inkārī) in His saying: «وإن منكم لمن ليبطئنّ».
Emphasis came with إن, with the lām of emphasis which the grammarians call "the shifted lām", and with the heavy nūn of emphasis, and in the use of the doubled (intensive) verb; the increase of letters is an increase of meaning. In the sum of these emphatics lies a dreadful intimidation of whoever holds himself back or holds others back. These verses were revealed about the hypocrite ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, who discouraged the believers at the battle of Uḥud. The poets clung to the hems of these meanings; Abū Tammām said, praising steadfastness in war and being killed in jihad, in an elegy for Muḥammad ibn Ḥumayd al-Ṭūsī, from a unique poem:
وقد كان فوت الموت سهلا فردّه ... إليه الحفاظ المرّ والخلق الوعر
ونفس تعاف العار حتى كأنما ... هو الكفر يوم الرّوع أو دونه الكفر
فأثبت في مستنقع الموت رجله ... وقال لها: من تحت أخمصك الحشر
تردى ثياب الموت حمرا فما دجا ... لها الليل إلا وهي من سندس خضر
(Escaping death was easy, but bitter honour and a rugged nature turned him back to it. / A soul that loathes disgrace as though, on the day of terror, it were unbelief, or less than unbelief. / So he planted his foot in the pool of death and said to it: from beneath your sole is the Gathering. / He put on the garments of death, red; and night had not fallen darkly upon it before they were of green silk.)
and so on to the end of that wonderful poem.

dervis-irab:73-74.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَئِنْ أَصابَكُمْ فَضْلٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction on His saying «فإن أصابتكم مصيبة». The first conditional was put first only because its content is more fitting to their purpose, and because the effect of their hypocrisy is more visible and stronger in impact. The lām is the preparatory lām of the oath (lām muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); إن is conditional; أصابكم is a past verb in the position of the jussive, the protasis; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; فضل is the fāʿil; and من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa). (لَيَقُولَنَّ كَأَنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُ مَوَدَّةٌ) The lām is the answer to the oath; ليقولنّ is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the clause has no position because it is the answer to the oath, which came first. كأن is the lightened form of the heavy كأنّ (its ruling will come in the section on Benefits); its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and the clause لم تكن is its khabar. The clause "كأن and what is in its scope" is parenthetical between the saying and what is said. Abū al-Baqāʾ chose that it be a ḥāl clause, following the statement of al-Rāghib, who said: "That is ugly, for one does not separate part of a sentence from another part that belongs to a different sentence." This is very strange, because it overturns the statements of all the grammarians. al-Rāzī said about it: "It is a parenthesis of utmost beauty, because whoever loves a person rejoices at his joy and grieves at his grief; so if he reverses the matter, that is a display of enmity." بينكم is an adverb attached to an omitted khabar of تكن, preposed; بينهم is conjoined to it; and مودة is the postposed noun of تكن. (يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ مَعَهُمْ فَأَفُوزَ فَوْزاً عَظِيماً) The clause is the quoted speech of «ليقولن». يا is a particle of vocative and the one addressed is omitted, or it is merely for drawing attention; the first is preferable. ليت is a particle resembling the verb, the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ is its noun; the clause كنت is the khabar of ليت, with كان and its noun; معهم is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar of كنت; فأفوز: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causality, and أفوز is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ; فوزا is the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and عظيما is an adjective. (فَلْيُقاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ الَّذِينَ يَشْرُونَ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا بِالْآخِرَةِ) The fāʾ is the "eloquent fāʾ" (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), i.e. "if you know all this, then let them fight"; the lām is the lām of command, and يقاتل is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command; في سبيل الله is attached to يقاتل; الذين is a relative noun, the fāʿil of يقاتل; the clause يشرون الحياة الدنيا is the ṣila of the relative noun; بالآخرة is attached to يشرون; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition. (وَمَنْ يُقاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) The wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; يقاتل is the protasis; and في سبيل الله is attached to يقاتل. (فَيُقْتَلْ أَوْ يَغْلِبْ فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْراً عَظِيماً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; يقتل, passive, is conjoined to يقاتل, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; أو is a conjunction; يغلب, active, is likewise conjoined, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; فسوف: the fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis; نؤتيه is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi; أجرا is the second mafʿūl bihi; and عظيما is an adjective.
The clause is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis; and the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar of «من».

* Rhetoric:
"Buying the life of this world with the Hereafter" is a metaphor of the makniyya type (implied-vehicle metaphor), to which reference was made earlier in these very words. The verb شرى can mean buying and selling, so one should not ask how the باء entered upon «الآخرة».

* Benefits:
When «كأن», the particle resembling the verb, is lightened, its operation remains; its noun is the pronoun of the matter, obligatorily omitted, and its khabar is a clause. If the clause serving as the khabar is affirmative with a fully inflecting verb, it is separated from كأن by «قد», as in your saying:
لا يهولنك اصطلاء لظى الحرب فمحذورها كأن قد ألمّ
(Let not the burning of the flame of war terrify you, for what is feared of it is as though it has already come.) Or, if negated, it is separated by «لم», as in his saying:
كأن لم يكن بين الحجون إلى الصفا ... أنيس ولم يسمر بمكة سامر
(As if there had been no companion between al-Ḥajūn and al-Ṣafā, and no night-talker had conversed in Mecca.)
That is to distinguish it from the maṣdar أن with the kāf of comparison attached to it. If the clause is not of that kind, there is no need to separate with anything, and this is the well-known usage.

dervis-irab:75-76.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْقَرْيَةِ) with fatḥa or kasra on the qāf: a noun comprising diverse meanings; it is the estate, the great town, a gathering of people, and the city. The plural is قرى with ḍamma on the qāf, and it was also read with kasra on the qāf and the rāʾ; the relative adjective from it is قروي and قرييّ.
Every "town" mentioned in the Qur'an has wrongdoing attributed to it figuratively, and examples will come in their places. As for this town in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, wrongdoing is attributed to its people in the literal sense, because what is meant by it is Mecca, and it was honoured by being spared the attribution of wrongdoing to itself, in tribute to it.

* I'rab:
(وَما لَكُمْ لا تُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) The wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, meant to urge to jihad by way of a question. ما is an interrogative noun whose sense is command and disapproval, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of it; and the clause لا تقاتلون في سبيل الله is a ḥāl clause. (وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الرِّجالِ وَالنِّساءِ وَالْوِلْدانِ) It is conjoined to «الله», and an omitted muḍāf must be supplied, i.e.: "you do not fight for the sake of freeing the oppressed." من الرجال is attached to an omitted ḥāl; الولدان is the plural of وليد, the small boy; and the women and children are those whom the polytheists kept from emigrating, among them Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "I and my mother were among them." (الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ: رَبَّنا أَخْرِجْنا مِنْ هذِهِ الْقَرْيَةِ الظَّالِمِ أَهْلُها) الذين is a relative noun, an adjective, and the clause يقولون is the ṣila of the relative noun; ربنا is a vocative muḍāf from which the particle of vocative has been omitted; أخرجنا is a verb of supplication, and نا is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech; من هذه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخرجنا; القرية is a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative; الظالم is a naʿt sababī (adjective in relation to what follows it); and أهلها is the fāʿil of الظالم, because it is an active participle. (وَاجْعَلْ لَنا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ وَلِيًّا) It is conjoined to أخرجنا; لنا is in the position of the accusative, the mafʿūl of اجعل; من لدنك is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl; and وليا is the second mafʿūl bihi. (وَاجْعَلْ لَنا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ نَصِيراً) Conjoined to what precedes. (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) A resumptive speech, meant to encourage fighting; الذين is the mubtadaʾ, the clause آمنوا is the ṣila, the clause يقاتلون is its khabar, and في سبيل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يقاتلون. (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ الطَّاغُوتِ) Conjoined to the preceding clause, whose i'rab has already been given. (فَقاتِلُوا أَوْلِياءَ الشَّيْطانِ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; قاتلوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable with omission of the nūn because its imperfect is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is the fāʿil; أولياء الشيطان is the mafʿūl bihi. (إِنَّ كَيْدَ الشَّيْطانِ كانَ ضَعِيفاً) إن and its noun; the clause كان is its khabar; ضعيفا is the khabar of كان; and the clause "إن and what follows it" is explanatory of the reason and has no position.

* Benefits:
The naʿt (adjective) is of two kinds:
1- Real (ḥaqīqī): that which describes an attribute of what it qualifies, and it must agree with what it qualifies in case, singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine, definiteness and indefiniteness.
2- Relational (sababī): that which describes an attribute of something that has a connection and tie to what it qualifies, as in the verse. It agrees with the qualified noun only in case, definiteness and indefiniteness, while its feminine or masculine follows what comes after it, and it always remains singular. In the verse, «الظالم» agreed with «القرية» in the genitive and definiteness, the gender followed what comes after it, namely الأهل, and it stayed singular even though the meaning of الأهل is plural. Had it been made feminine outside the Qur'an, saying الظالمة أهلها, it would be permissible, not because of the feminine of the qualified noun but because الأهل can be masculine or feminine.

dervis-irab:44-46.t:
* Vocabulary:
(هادُوا): they returned; what is meant is the rabbis of the Jews.
(الكلم): plural of «كلمة» (word). Distorting the words (taḥrīf al-kalim) means turning them away from their places and removing them, for when they alter it and put in its place a word other than it, they have turned it aside from the places in which Allah put it.
(راعِنا): It was said that it is Arabic, meaning "wait for us and watch us"; and it was said that it is a word resembling Hebrew or Syriac with which they used to insult one another, namely "rāʿīnā". In this is the utmost baseness and vileness, that you should insult another in a tongue he does not know.
(لَيًّا): a twisting with their tongues and a turning of the speech from its original course to insult and abuse. The Jews used to say to their companions: "We only abuse him and he does not know it; if he were a prophet he would know that." So Allah the Exalted informed him of what they mumbled and of what betrayed their malice and evil intent.

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيباً مِنَ الْكِتابِ): A resumptive statement, introduced to warn the believers against befriending the Jews. The hamza is interrogative; لم is a particle of negation, reversal (of tense) and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb jussive by لم. The seeing here is either of the heart, meaning knowing (and it is made transitive by إلى, meaning "has your knowledge not reached them?"), or of the eye, meaning "have you not looked at them?", for they deserve that you observe them and count them among visible things. The clause أوتوا is a ṣila, and the واو is the nāʾib fāʿil; نصيبا is a second mafʿūl bihi; and من الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element functioning as naʿt of «نصيبا». (يَشْتَرُونَ الضَّلالَةَ وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا السَّبِيلَ): The clause يشترون is a mafʿūl bihi of «تر» if the verb is of the heart, and a ḥāl if it is of the eye; the واو is the agent and الضلالة is a mafʿūl bihi. The meaning of "buying error" is exchanging for it after the clear signs have become plain. The discussion of the purchase of error has already been given. ويريدون is conjoined to يشترون; أن and what is within its scope are an interpreted maṣdar functioning as mafʿūl bihi of يريدون; and السبيل is the object of تضلوا. (وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِأَعْدائِكُمْ): The واو is a wāw of ḥāl; الله is a mubtadaʾ and أعلم its khabar; بأعدائكم is attached to أعلم; and the clause is in the position of accusative as ḥāl. (وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ وَلِيًّا وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ نَصِيراً): The discussion of كفى and of the redundancy of the باء in its agent or its object has already been given; here it is redundant in the agent. وليا and نصيرا are two tamyīz (specifications) or two ḥāls. (مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ): A resumptive statement, introduced to bring a base picture of the Jews during their dialogue with the Prophet ﷺ. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element functioning as a fronted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, whose place its naʿt has taken, namely the clause «يحرفون الكلم»; the implied form is: "among those who are Jews are a people who distort the words". It was also said: «من الذين هادوا» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "they are of those who are Jews", and the clause يحرفون is a ḥāl from the pronoun of هادوا. And it was said that «من الذين» is a ḥāl from «أعدائكم», making it clear, and what lies between is parenthetical; but the first is preferable. A clear opinion of Ibn Hishām will follow. (عَنْ مَواضِعِهِ): attached to يحرفون. (وَيَقُولُونَ: سَمِعْنا وَعَصَيْنا): The clause يقولون is conjoined to يحرفون; the clause سمعنا is the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl); and the clause وعصينا is conjoined to the clause سمعنا. (وَاسْمَعْ غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍ): Conjoined to سمعنا, included within what they say; that is, they say this in the course of addressing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. And غير مسمع is a ḥāl from the one addressed. This expression is among the double-edged speech that will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَراعِنا لَيًّا بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ وَطَعْناً فِي الدِّينِ): Conjoined to اسمع; ليا بألسنتهم is accusative as ḥāl, or as mafʿūl li-ajlihi, or as mafʿūl muṭlaq; and طعنا is conjoined to «ليا»; and في الدين is attached to طعنا. (وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ قالُوا: سَمِعْنا وَأَطَعْنا): The واو is a wāw of ḥāl or resumptive, and the clause is a ḥāl clause or resumptive; لو is conditional; أن and what follows it is the agent of an omitted verb, i.e. "had their saying been established"; the clause قالوا is the khabar of أن; and the two clauses سمعنا and أطعنا are part of what they said. (وَاسْمَعْ وَانْظُرْنا): Conjoined to the quoted speech, included within it. The meaning of انظرنا is "look at us", in place of راعنا, which contains baseness as was stated in the section on vocabulary. (لَكانَ خَيْراً لَهُمْ وَأَقْوَمَ): The لام links the apodosis of لو; كان is a defective past verb and its ism is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; خيرا is its khabar; لهم is attached to خيرا; and أقوم is conjoined to «خيرا». (وَلكِنْ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَلا يُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): The واو is a wāw of ḥāl; لكن is a lightened particle of rectification (istidrāk) that does not govern; لعنهم الله is a verb, object and agent; the فاء is a conjunction; لا is negative; يؤمنون is an imperfect verb, nominative; إلا is a particle of restriction; and قليلا is a naʿt of a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "except a little belief". It is also permissible that it be "a few of them", in which case it is an excepted element from the واو in يؤمنون.

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains a unique art, which we call ibhām (ambiguity), or double-edged speech, or speech that admits of two opposite meanings: it is the bringing of speech that carries two opposing meanings such that one cannot be told apart from the other. It is His words: «واسمع غير مسمع», which has two aspects:
1- An aspect that may be censure: that is, "listen from us, being prayed against, 'may you not hear'", that is, "may Allah afflict you with deafness, death". Perhaps this is what is meant here because of the baseness they harbour.
2- An aspect that may be praise: that is, "listen, without being made to hear anything unpleasant". Of this speech, which is like a spell of magic, such that even an eloquent man cannot take or leave it, is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «إذا لم تستح فاصنع ما شئت» ("If you have no modesty, do as you wish"). It contains two opposite meanings. One is that praise is meant by it, i.e. "if you do not do an act of which one is ashamed, then do as you wish, for you are safe from its consequence". The other is that censure is meant by it, i.e. "if you have no modesty to restrain you from doing what one is ashamed of, then do as you wish, for you have reached the lowest depths of abasement". These are two opposite meanings, one praise and the other censure.

Double-edged speech in the poetry of Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
Here it is fitting for us to include a section of the marvels of Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī in his panegyrics to Kāfūr, for he deliberately used this kind of speech, as in his words from a poem on him that begins:
عدوّك مذموم بكلّ لسان ... ولو كان من أعدائك القمران
(Your enemy is censured by every tongue, even if the sun and the moon were among your enemies.)
ولله سرّ في علاك وإنما ... كلام العدا ضرب من الهذيان
(Allah has a secret in your exaltation, and the speech of enemies is but a kind of raving.)
Then he said after that:
فمالك تعنى بالأسنّة والقنا ... وجدّك طعّان بغير لسان؟
(What is it with you, that you toil with spearheads and lances, when your good fortune is a stabber without a tongue?)
This speech is closer to censure than to praise, for he is saying: "You did not reach what you reached by your effort and concern, but by luck and good fortune, and you have no merit in that; for if his luck is the cause of his advancement, what is his worth? What is his standing? How slight is his affair! How small his importance!" And because good fortune may come to the obscure and the ignorant and to one who does not deserve it. Abū l-Ṭayyib was inclined to use this kind of speech in his poems on Kāfūr.
Abū l-Fatḥ ibn Jinnī reported, saying: "I read his dīwān to Abū l-Ṭayyib until I reached his poem that begins «أغالب فيك الشوق والشوق أغلب» ('I struggle against longing for you, and longing prevails'), and I came in it to this verse:
وما طربي لما رأيتك بدعة ... لقد كنت أرجو أن أراك فأطرب
(My delight when I saw you is no novelty; I had long hoped to see you and be delighted.)
So I said to him: 'O Abū l-Ṭayyib, you have done no more than make him Abū Zinna!' — which is the kunya of the monkey — and he laughed."

Examples of ibhām:
Among the curious cases of ibhām is what is told that one of the poets congratulated al-Ḥasan ibn Sahl on the marriage of his daughter Būrān to al-Maʾmūn, along with the poets who congratulated him. He rewarded all the people and deprived him. So he wrote to him: "If you persist in depriving me, I shall compose about you a verse of which no one will know whether I praised you in it or satirised you." So he summoned him and said to him: "I shall not give you anything until you do it." So he said:
بارك الله للحسن ... ولبوران في الختن
(May Allah bless al-Ḥasan, and Būrān, in the son-in-law.)
يا إمام الهدى ظفر ... ت ولكن ببنت من؟
(O imam of guidance, you have won, but with the daughter of whom?)
No one knew whether by his words "the daughter of whom?" he meant in greatness or in lowliness. Al-Ḥasan approved of that from him and asked him whether he had invented it. He said: "No, I took it from the poetry of Bashshār ibn Burd. It happened that he had a qabāʾ (coat) cut at the shop of a one-eyed tailor named Zayd, and the tailor said to him, by way of teasing: 'I will bring it to you such that you will not know whether it is a qabāʾ or a jubba.' Bashshār said to him: 'If you do that, I shall compose about you a verse of which none who hears it will know whether I have prayed for you or against you.' When he had sewn it, Bashshār said:
خاط لي زيد قباء ... ليت عينيه سواء
(Zayd sewed me a coat; would that his two eyes were alike.)
No one knew whether the sound eye was to equal the blind one, or the reverse."
The discussion of ibhām is long, and more of it will come in this wonderful book.

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām cited in al-Mughnī a shāhid (evidence) for a parenthetical insertion of more than two clauses. After citing the two verses just mentioned, he said: If «الذين هادوا» is taken as a clarification of «الذين أوتوا» and a specification of them, when the word is general of the Jews, then the parenthetical material on this taking is two clauses; and on the first taking it is three clauses, namely: «والله أعلم», and «وكفى بالله», twice. As for «يشترون» and «يريدون», they are two clauses of explanation for an implied element, since the meaning is: "Have you not looked at the story of those who were given…". But if «من» is attached to «نصير», as in «ونصرناه من القوم», or to an omitted khabar, on the basis that «يحرفون» is a naʿt of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "a people who distort", as in their saying "minnā ẓaʿana wa-minnā aqāma" ("among us are those who departed and among us are those who stayed"), i.e. "among us is a group", then there is no parenthetical insertion at all.

dervis-irab:47-47.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَطْمِسَ وُجُوهاً): We wipe out the outlines of their features and forms.
(عَلى أَدْبارِها): that is, We make them like the napes, like a blurred, upright tablet, so that they are neither distinct nor clear to one who sees them.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ): its i'rab has already been given. (آمِنُوا بِما نَزَّلْنا مُصَدِّقاً لِما مَعَكُمْ): A resumptive statement, introduced to warn against what has been prepared for the Jews, after their distortion of the words, of disfigurement and deformation. آمنوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) with the dropping of the nūn because its imperfect is one of the five verbs; بما is attached to آمنوا; the clause نزلنا is the ṣila of the relative; مصدقا is a ḥāl; لما is attached to مصدقا; and معكم is an adverb attached to an omitted element functioning as ṣila of the relative, i.e. "confirming that which is with you". (مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَطْمِسَ وُجُوهاً فَنَرُدَّها عَلى أَدْبارِها): من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنوا; أن نطمس is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; وجوها is a mafʿūl bihi; فنردها: the فاء is a conjunction, and نردها is conjoined to نطمس and is accusative like it; the هاء is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; and على أدبارها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element in the position of the second mafʿūl of نردّها; it was also said, attached to an omitted element functioning as ḥāl. I see no need for that i'rab. (أَوْ نَلْعَنَهُمْ كَما لَعَنَّا أَصْحابَ السَّبْتِ): أو is a conjunction, and نلعنهم is conjoined to «نطمس وجوها» or to «نردها»; the pronoun is mentioned, and in the plural of rational beings, because it returns to the owners of the faces, as will come in the section on rhetoric. وكما لعنا is attached to an omitted element functioning as mafʿūl muṭlaq; its like has already been given. ما is maṣdar-forming and نا is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as agent of «لعن»; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq or ḥāl; and أصحاب السبت is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَكانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ مَفْعُولًا): The واو is resumptive or of ḥāl; كان with its ism and khabar; and the clause has no position, or is in the position of accusative as ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse there is a majāz mursal (a non-comparative figurative usage) by mentioning the faces and intending their owners, the relation being that of whole for part («al-kulliyya»). [Translator's note: the source says "the relation being al-kulliyya"; strictly, mentioning the faces for their owners is the part for the whole (al-juzʾiyya), but the translation follows the text as written.]
2- Ibhām (ambiguity) in the indefiniteness of الوجوه (faces), out of gentleness towards those addressed, and to make dreadful the great matter that stirs fear. They differed about the meaning of the threat and what is intended by it in the verse: is it literal, so that the face is made like the nape and the nose, brow, eye and ear vanish — "darknesses, one above another" — or is what is meant the stripping of them of divine success and depriving them of grace? Some took the former view, and others the latter; see the longer works.

dervis-irab:77-77.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهُمْ كُفُّوا أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ) A resumptive speech, meant to arouse wonder in the soul of the Messenger ﷺ at their holding back from fighting after showing a desire for it and having actually engaged in it, as is indicated by the command to restrain the hands after they had been stretched out against them.
The hamza is for an interrogative of wonder; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb jussive by لم; إلى الذين is attached to «تر»; the clause قيل is the ṣila of the relative noun; لهم is attached to قيل; the clause كفوا is the quoted speech; أيديكم is the object of كفوا; and أقيموا الصلاة and آتوا الزكاة are conjoined to the clause كفوا, i.e. "do not fight the disbelievers as long as they are in Mecca." (فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقِتالُ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and لما is a particle of existence for existence, as Sībawayh said, or an adverb meaning "when" containing the sense of a condition, as Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said. The clause كتب عليهم القتال has no grammatical position because it occurs after a particle-type relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī), or it is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). (إِذا فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ يَخْشَوْنَ النَّاسَ كَخَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ) إذا is, on the sounder view, a particle, which the grammarians call the "particle of surprise" (al-fujāʾiyya), contrary to whoever claimed it is an adverb of place or time; only a verb follows it [Translator's note: the source reads "لا يليها إلا الفعل" ("only a verb follows it"), which contradicts the next clause, that it is specific to the nominal sentence; translated as written]; it does not occur at the beginning of a speech; a nominal sentence after it can only be a ḥāl; and it is specific to the nominal sentence, or one made inna-governed, as in: خرجت فاذا إن المطر نازل ("I went out, and lo, the rain was falling"). A copious and delightful discussion of it, which none preceded us in, will come in the section on Benefits. فريق is a mubtadaʾ, for which it was permissible to begin with it although it is indefinite, because it was qualified by His saying «منهم»; the clause يخشون الناس is the khabar of فريق; الناس is the mafʿūl bihi; and in كخشية الله the kāf is a noun meaning "like" in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, or it is a preposition and it with its genitive noun is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl or as a mafʿūl muṭlaq; and the clause فريق منهم etc. is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; and the clause of surprise has no position because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition. (أَوْ أَشَدَّ خَشْيَةً) أو is a conjunction, and أشد خشية is conjoined to كخشية الله, so it is a ḥāl or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, and خشية is a tamyīz (specification). Some of the i'rab-writers preferred that it be parsed as a ḥāl from His saying «خشية», because it is an adjective of an indefinite noun that was put before it and so became accusative; but that is sheer affectation with no need for it, and an interesting discussion of this will come in the section on Benefits, to which we draw attention for its preciousness. (وَقالُوا رَبَّنا لِمَ كَتَبْتَ عَلَيْنَا الْقِتالَ) The wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; قالوا is a verb and fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive or conjoined to the clause يخشون; ربنا is a vocative muḍāf from which the particle of vocative has been omitted; لم: the lām is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun whose alif was dropped because it follows a preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to كتبت; القتال is the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech. (لَوْلا أَخَّرْتَنا إِلى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ) لولا is a particle of urging like هلّا; أخرتنا is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; and the clause is included in what they said. (قُلْ مَتاعُ الدُّنْيا قَلِيلٌ) قل is an imperative whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you", and the clause is resumptive; متاع الدنيا is a mubtadaʾ and قليل a khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech. (وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لِمَنِ اتَّقى) The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; الآخرة is a mubtadaʾ and خير a khabar, and the clause is resumed or a ḥāl; and in لمن اتقى the lām is a preposition, من is a relative noun made genitive by the lām, the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خير, and اتقى is a past verb with a latent fāʿil, the clause being the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَلا تُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا) The wāw is a conjunction, لا is negative, and تظلمون is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil; فتيلا is an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq which it has replaced.

* Benefits:
1- The grammarians differed over "the إذا of surprise". Some said it is an adverb of place or time, and the i'rab-writers and exegetes followed them, so they plunged into endless mazes and reached no result. Others, headed by al-Akhfash, said: it is always a particle, and this is supported by your saying «إن خرجت فإذا إن المطر نازل» with kasra on the hamza of «إن», because «إن» with kasra does not let what follows it act on what precedes it, whereas with fatḥa what follows acts on what precedes, since it does not have the right to the head of the sentence. As for making it an adverb of place or time, it requires entering into pointless strainings. We have preferred in our book not to commit to an opinion of our own unless we see that someone before us held it; we say this because some pedants wronged us and claimed that we had erred. This question became famous in grammar, and an amusing debate took place over it between Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī, which you will find in full in Mughnī al-Labīb; and these disputants overlooked that what follows it occurs as a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the nominative in the Qur'an, as Ibn Yaʿīsh and other grammarians did; so go back to the discussion of the إذا of surprise in the Mughnī and the longer works, and you will hear wonders upon wonders.
2- A parallel to this verse has passed in the i'rab, namely the saying of the Exalted: «فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا». Among the delightful discussions concerning the noun that occurs after the noun of preference (ism al-tafḍīl) is that both the accusative and the genitive are valid for it. You say: «زيد أكرم أبا» with accusative, in which case Zayd is among the sons and you are preferring his father; and you say: «زيد أكرم أب» with genitive, in which case Zayd is among the fathers and you are preferring him.
And you say: «زيد أفضل إخوته», which is a mistake, because an afʿal al-tafḍīl is annexed only to what it is included in, and Zayd is not included in his brothers, since if you were asked about him you would count them without him; so the example would be like: Zayd is the best of women, which is invalid. The correct form is to say: أفضل الإخوة, or: أفضل بني أبيه.

dervis-irab:153-153.t:
* I'rab:
(يَسْئَلُكَ أَهْلُ الْكِتابِ أَنْ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ كِتاباً مِنَ السَّماءِ) A resumptive statement, offered to relate the request of the rabbis of the Jews, who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to bring down upon them a book from heaven, as Moses brought it; their request was nothing but obstinacy and stubbornness. يسألك is a verb and first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أهل الكتاب is the fāʿil (agent); أن تنزل is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of an accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi; عليهم is attached to تنزّل; كتابا is a mafʿūl bihi; من السماء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of كتابا. (فَقَدْ سَأَلُوا مُوسى أَكْبَرَ مِنْ ذلِكَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ fuṣḥā (eloquent fāʾ), the one that falls as the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if you find what they said too great and are astounded at what they asked out of obstinacy and excess, then they had asked Moses before you"; موسى is the first mafʿūl bihi and أكبر the second mafʿūl bihi; it is also permissible to parse it as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); من ذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أكبر. (فَقالُوا أَرِنَا اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; قالوا is conjoined to سألوا; the clause أرنا الله is in the position of an accusative as the quoted speech; أر is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; «نا» is a mafʿūl bihi and الله the second mafʿūl bihi; جهرة, that is, "visibly", is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, because jahra is a kind of absolute seeing and so it meets its companion in the verb; it may also be parsed as a ḥāl, being a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, that is, "openly". (فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ بِظُلْمِهِمْ) Conjoined to what precedes; بظلمهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخذتهم, that is, "because of their wrongdoing". (ثُمَّ اتَّخَذُوا الْعِجْلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّناتُ) ثم is a conjunction of order in the telling, that is, "then it was part of their affair that they took the calf"; من بعد is attached to اتخذوا; ما is a maṣdar particle, interpreted with the verb as a maṣdar that is the muḍāf ilayhi of بعد, that is, "after the coming of the clear signs". (فَعَفَوْنا عَنْ ذلِكَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction to what precedes; عن ذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عفونا. (وَآتَيْنا مُوسى سُلْطاناً مُبِيناً) The wāw is a conjunction; آتينا is a verb and agent; موسى is the first mafʿūl bihi and سلطانا the second mafʿūl bihi; مبينا is an adjective.

dervis-irab:154-155.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الطُّورَ): the mountain.
(لا تَعْدُوا): do not transgress. Its original is تعدووا; the ḍamma was found heavy on the first wāw and was dropped; then two sukūns met and the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns.
(غُلْفٌ): plural of aghlaf, like ḥumr, plural of aḥmar. It is also sound for it to be the plural of ghilāf (sheath, covering), like kitāb, kutub, with sukūn for lightness.

* I'rab:
(وَرَفَعْنا فَوْقَهُمُ الطُّورَ بِمِيثاقِهِمْ) The wāw is a conjunction and رفعنا is conjoined to what precedes; فوقهم is an adverb attached to رفعنا, and likewise بميثاقهم is attached to it; الطور is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَقُلْنا لَهُمُ: ادْخُلُوا الْبابَ سُجَّداً) قلنا is conjoined to what precedes; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قلنا; the clause ادخلوا الباب is the quoted speech; سجدا is a ḥāl. (وَقُلْنا لَهُمْ: لا تَعْدُوا فِي السَّبْتِ) Also conjoined to what precedes; the clause لا تعدوا is in the position of an accusative as the quoted speech; في السبت is attached to تعدوا. (وَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُمْ مِيثاقاً غَلِيظاً) Also conjoined to what precedes; منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخذنا; غليظا is an adjective of ميثاقا. (فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثاقَهُمْ وَكُفْرِهِمْ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ) The fāʾ is resumptive; the bāʾ is a preposition; ما is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis; نقضهم is genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "We did to them what We did because of their breaking"; ميثاقهم is the mafʿūl bihi of the maṣdar, which is نقض; كفرهم is conjoined to نقضهم; بآيات الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كفرهم. (وَقَتْلِهِمُ الْأَنْبِياءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ) Conjoined to what precedes; الأنبياء is the mafʿūl bihi of the maṣdar, which is قتلهم; بغير حق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَقَوْلِهِمْ قُلُوبُنا غُلْفٌ) Also conjoined; the clause قلوبنا غلف, of mubtadaʾ and khabar, is the quoted speech. (بَلْ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْها بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَلا يُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا) بل is a particle of exclusion and conjunction, that is, "the matter is not as they said"; طبع الله is a verb and agent; عليها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to طبع, and بكفرهم is attached to طبع, that is, "because of their disbelief"; the fāʾ is a conjunction; لا is negative; يؤمنون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the agent; إلا is a particle of restriction; قليلا is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "except a little belief", and so is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, or an adjective of an omitted time, that is, "except for a little time", and so is an adverb of time attached to يؤمنون. It may also be accusative as an exception from the agent of يؤمنون, that is:
"except a few of them".

dervis-irab:156-158.t:
* I'rab:
(وَبِكُفْرِهِمْ وَقَوْلِهِمْ عَلى مَرْيَمَ بُهْتاناً عَظِيماً) There are two views on this conjunction. The first is that it is conjoined to what is in His saying «فبما نقضهم», so it is attached to what the first is attached to. The second is that it is conjoined to His saying «بكفرهم» which comes after «طبع». It is also permissible that the whole of this and what is conjoined to it be conjoined to the whole of what precedes, and that the repetition of mentioning disbelief be a notice of the repetition of their disbelief, for they disbelieved in Moses, then in Jesus, then in Muḥammad, the blessings of Allah be upon them all. It is as though it were said: "Because of their combining the breaking of the covenant, disbelief in the signs of Allah, the killing of the prophets and their saying 'our hearts are covered', and their combining their disbelief with their slandering of Mary and their boasting of killing Jesus, peace be upon him, We punished them"; or "rather Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief and their combining their disbelief with such and such". على مريم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قولهم. بهتانا is a maṣdar on which "saying" operates, because it is a kind of it, like their expression "he sat squatting" (qaʿada al-qurfuṣāʾ). Some said:
its implied form is "a slanderous saying", so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq in any case. It was also said that it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, that is, "slandering". It is not far-fetched to make it a mafʿūl bihi of قولهم, since it contains the sense of "speech", as in "I said a sermon and poetry". عظيما is an adjective. (وَقَوْلِهِمْ إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا الْمَسِيحَ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ)
وقولهم is conjoined to what precedes; إن and its noun; the clause قتلنا المسيح is its khabar; المسيح is a mafʿūl bihi; عيسى is a badal (substitute) of المسيح; ابن is a badal or an adjective; مريم is a muḍāf ilayhi. (رَسُولَ اللَّهِ) An adjective of عيسى, or a badal of it, or it is accusative as praise by an omitted verb; they said that in mockery. (وَما قَتَلُوهُ وَما صَلَبُوهُ وَلكِنْ شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ) The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāl); ما is negative; قتلوه is a verb, agent and object; وما صلبوه is conjoined to وما قتلوه, the wāw being a conjunction; لكن is the lightened form, for istidrāk (rectification) only; شبه is a passive past verb, attributed to the preposition and its genitive noun after it, which is لهم. It is also permissible to attribute it to the pronoun of the one killed, because their saying "we killed" indicates him, as though it were said: "but the one they killed was made to resemble him to them". It is not correct to make it attributed to the Messiah, because he is the one imitated and not the one made to resemble. (وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِنْهُ) The wāw is resumptive; إن and its noun; the clause اختلفوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; فيه is attached to اختلفوا; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); في شك is attached to an omitted khabar of «إن»; منه is attached to an omitted adjective of شك, that is, "in a doubt arising from the matter of his killing", so من is for the beginning of the limit. It is not permissible to attach them to شك, since one does not say "I doubted from him". (ما لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا اتِّباعَ الظَّنِّ وَما قَتَلُوهُ يَقِيناً) This negated clause is resumptive, and you may put it in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, or in the position of a genitive as a second adjective of شك, that is, "unknown". ما is negative; لهم is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; به is attached to «علم», or is a ḥāl from it, because it was an adjective and was fronted; من is a redundant preposition; علم is genitive in form, nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ; إلا اتباع الظن is a discontinuous exception (munqaṭiʿ), because the following of conjecture is not of the same kind as knowledge; the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; قتلوه is a verb, agent and object; يقينا is an emphatic ḥāl from the agent of قتلوه, or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "a certain killing". (بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزاً حَكِيماً) بل is a particle of conjunction and exclusion; رفعه is a verb with a fronted object; الله is the agent; إليه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to رفعه; the wāw is resumptive; كان with its noun and its two khabars.

dervis-irab:159-159.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ إِلَّا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ) The wāw is resumptive; إن is negative; من أهل الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is the oath clause answered by His saying «إلا ليؤمنن». The oath clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ only because it is the point of the benefit. إلا is a particle of restriction; the lām is the one that prepares for the oath; يؤمنن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis; به is attached to يؤمنن; قبل موته is an adverb of time attached to يؤمنن. (وَيَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيداً) The wāw is a conjunction; يوم القيامة is an adverb attached to شهيدا; شهيدا is the khabar of يكون, whose noun is omitted; عليهم is attached to شهيدا.

dervis-irab:160-161.t:
* I'rab:
(فَبِظُلْمٍ مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا حَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّباتٍ أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ) The fāʾ is resumptive and the statement is resumptive, offered to explain what was forbidden them of good things because of their wrongdoing. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to حرمنا; the bāʾ is causal and was fronted before its operator to draw attention to how ugly the cause of the prohibition was; من الذين is attached to an omitted adjective of ظلم; the clause هادوا is the ṣila of the relative noun; حرمنا is a verb and agent; عليهم, the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to حرمنا; طيبات is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause أحلت لهم is an adjective of طيبات.
