(وَبِصَدِّهِمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ كَثِيراً) وبصدهم is conjoined to His saying فبظلم; عن سبيل الله is attached to «صد»; كثيرا is accusative as a maṣdar, that is, "a great turning away", or a mafʿūl bihi in the sense of "a great multitude"; you may also parse it as an adverb, that is, "many times". Ṣadd is used both intransitively and transitively, and its meaning is prevention. That is, their own turning away from the path of Allah many times by their disobeying Moses, peace be upon him, and opposing him; or their turning people away from the path of Allah by bad example or by commanding the wrong and forbidding the right. (وَأَخْذِهِمُ الرِّبَوا وَقَدْ نُهُوا عَنْهُ) Conjoined to صدهم; الربا is a mafʿūl bihi of «أخذ», because it is a maṣdar; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāl); قد is a particle of certainty; نهوا is a passive past verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʾil (deputy agent); عنه is attached to نهوا; the clause قد نهوا is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl. (وَأَكْلِهِمْ أَمْوالَ النَّاسِ بِالْباطِلِ) Conjoined to what precedes; أموال الناس is the mafʿūl bihi of أكل; بالباطل, the preposition and its genitive noun, may be attached to أكلهم because the bāʾ is causal, or to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "being involved in falsehood", such as bribery, betrayal and the like. (وَأَعْتَدْنا لِلْكافِرِينَ مِنْهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً) Conjoined to حرمنا; أعتدنا is a verb and agent; للكافرين is attached to أعتدنا; منهم is attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "those who persist in disbelief, not those of them who believed and repented"; عذابا is a mafʿūl bihi and أليما an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
The vagueness (ibhām) in His saying «فبظلم», with tanwīn, is so that the reader or listener may know that any kind of wrongdoing may be a cause of punishment in this world before the next. Punishment is of two kinds: worldly and otherworldly. The first is of two kinds: positive (waḍʿī), like the burdensome religious obligations in the time of legislation and the penalty prescribed for wrongdoing, whether a fixed punishment (ḥadd) or a discretionary one (taʿzīr); and natural, which is what the way (sunna) of Allah the Exalted requires in the order of society, in that wrongdoing is a cause of the weakness of nations, the ruin of their civilisation and one nation's domination over another.

dervis-irab:162-162.t:
* I'rab:
(لكِنِ الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ مِنْهُمْ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ) A resumptive statement, offered to remove the false impression arising from the unqualified statement that explained the bad state of the Jews, their disbelief and their disobedience, for that gives the impression that what was mentioned of them is general and covers all their individuals. So the istidrāk (rectification) came after it to explain the state of their best, whose insight the blindness of imitation did not take away. لكن is a particle of rectification, inoperative because the nūn is lightened; it must occur between two opposites, as it occurs here between the disbelievers and the believers. الراسخون is a mubtadaʾ; في العلم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it, because it is an active participle; منهم is attached to an omitted ḥāl from the latent pronoun in الراسخون; والمؤمنون is conjoined to الراسخون. (يُؤْمِنُونَ بِما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَما أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ) The clause يؤمنون is the khabar of الراسخون, or a ḥāl from them if we regard the clause سنؤتيهم as the khabar; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤمنون; the clause أنزل إليك is the ṣila; وما أنزل من قبلك is conjoined to the ṣila, falling within its scope; من قبلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. More will be said on the i'rab of this verse in the section on benefits. (وَالْمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلاةَ) The wāw is parenthetical; المقيمين is accusative as praise (madḥ) by an implied verb, to show the excellence of prayer, according to what Sībawayh and others said; the implied form is "I mean" or "I single out" the establishers of prayer who perform it perfectly, for they are the most fitting of the believers to be firmly rooted in belief. The accusative of praise or concern does not occur in eloquent speech except for a point, and the point here is what we mentioned above about the distinction of prayer; moreover, changing the i'rab of a word among its like draws the mind to the need to reflect on it, and guides thought to bring out its distinction, and this is one of the pillars of rhetoric; further explanation of this will come. It was also read in the nominative, as conjoined to المؤمنون; الصلاة is a mafʿūl bihi of المقيمين. (وَالْمُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ) Conjoined to what precedes; الزكاة is a mafʿūl bihi of المؤتون because it is an active participle. (وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ) والمؤمنون is conjoined to what precedes; بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to المؤمنون; اليوم is conjoined to الله; الآخر is an adjective. (أُولئِكَ سَنُؤْتِيهِمْ أَجْراً عَظِيماً) The clause أولئك and what follows it is the khabar of الراسخون, or it is resumptive; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; the clause سنؤتيهم is the khabar; أجرا is the second mafʿūl bihi; عظيما is an adjective.

* Benefits:
1- Al-Rāzī was firm that His saying الراسخون is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is يؤمنون. He thereby interprets "those firmly rooted" as "those who reason from evidence", and justified this by saying that the imitator is such that if he is made to doubt he doubts, whereas the one who reasons from evidence never doubts at all. He gave two views on His saying والمؤمنون: one, that they are the believers among them; the other, that they are the believers among the Emigrants and the Helpers. The meaning is that those firmly rooted in knowledge among them and the believers among the Emigrants and the Helpers are alike in believing in what was sent down to Muḥammad ﷺ and what was sent down to the messengers before him, making no distinction between them.

Abū al-Suʿūd prefers the second:
Abū al-Suʿūd, though, to whose sharpness of mind we have alluded in earlier discussion, insisted that the khabar is His saying «أولئك سنؤتيهم». He said: "His saying أولئك points to them in respect of their being described with the fine qualities enumerated, and the sense of distance in it signals the loftiness of their rank and the remoteness of their standing in excellence. It is a mubtadaʾ, and His saying سنؤتيهم أجرا عظيما is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ which is الراسخون and what is conjoined to it. The sīn is to confirm the promise, and the indefiniteness of أجرا is to magnify it. This i'rab better suits the correspondence of the two sides, since the former were threatened with painful punishment and the latter promised a great reward. As for what the majority leaned toward, making His saying يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك etc. the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, it has complete soundness, except that it does not take into account the correspondence of the two sides." We have recorded Abū al-Suʿūd's words only for the mental agility in them [Translator's note: the source reads «توئب ذهني»; probably «توثب ذهني»], though the first is the better.
2- Changing the i'rab, as we said above, urges the mind to reflect on the reason for the change and to bring out the distinction hidden in it. Its counterpart in speech is that the speaker changes the ring of his voice and the manner of his delivery of the word to which he wishes to alert the addressee, such as raising or lowering the voice or lengthening it. Some ignorant people, and some who feign ignorance, have counted the like of this as a mistake in the soundest and most eloquent speech.
Al-Zamakhsharī's eloquent reply:
It is useful here to give what al-Zamakhsharī said on this matter. He said:
"It is a broad chapter which Sībawayh broke open with examples and attestations. No attention is paid to what they claimed of its being a solecism in the script of the muṣḥaf, though perhaps it is heeded by one who has not studied it in the Book (that is, Sībawayh's book), and does not know the ways of the Arabs and their variety in using the accusative of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ); and it escaped him that the foremost early Muslims were more zealous in their concern for Islam and in warding off attacks against it than to leave in the Book of Allah a breach for those after them to fill, or a tear for those who followed them to mend."

What Ibn Jarīr says:
As for Ibn Jarīr, he mentioned that in the muṣḥaf of Ibn Masʿūd it is «والمقيمون الصلاة». He said: the correct one is the reading of everyone, and he replied to whoever claimed that this was a scribes' mistake. Then he mentioned the people's differing and said: some of them said it is accusative as praise, as in His saying «والموفون بعهدهم إذا عاهدوا والصابرين في البأساء والضراء وحين البأس». He said: this is permissible in the speech of the Arabs, as the poet said:
لا يبعدن قومي الذين هم ... سم العداة وآفة الجزر
النازلين بكل معترك ... والطيبون معاقد الأزر
(May my people not perish, those who are the poison of enemies and the bane of the slaughter-camels; those who alight in every battlefield, and the pure ones at the knots of their loincloths.)
Others said: it is genitive, conjoined to His saying بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك.
The text of Sībawayh's wording:
As for Sībawayh's wording in his book, it is: "This is the chapter on what is made accusative for glorification", and among that is: والمقيمين الصلاة, and he recited:
وكل قوم أطاعوا أمر سيدهم ... إلا نميرا أطاعت أمر غاويها
الطاعنين ولما يطعنوا أحدا ... والقائلون: لمن دار تخلّيها
(Every tribe obeyed the command of its chief, except Numayr, who obeyed the command of its misleader; those who thrust [spears] though they have not yet thrust anyone, and those who say: "Whose is the abode we are leaving?")

dervis-irab:35-36.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الشقاق): disagreement. Disagreement was called shiqāq because the disagreeing party does what is hard (yashuqqu) on his companion, or because each of them has come to be on one side (shiqq), that is, one flank.
(الْجُنُبِ), with two ḍammas: the distant neighbour and the stranger; the masculine and feminine, singular, dual and plural are alike in it. He said:
لا يجتوينا مجاور أبدا ... ذو رحم أو مجاور جنب
(No neighbour, whether a kinsman or a distant neighbour, will ever find us loathsome.) (الصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنْبِ), with fatḥa on the jīm and sukūn on the nūn: the companion in some good affair, such as learning, trade, craft or travel, for he is your companion and is always at your side.
(ابْنِ السَّبِيلِ): the traveller and one cut off in his journey.
(المختال): the proud, arrogant one; the alif of its root is a yāʾ, and from it comes al-khayl (horses), because they strut in their gait with exuberance.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ شِقاقَ بَيْنِهِما) A resumptive clause, introduced to address those in authority about the disagreement between the spouses. إن is conditional; خفتم is a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis; شقاق is a direct object; and بينهما is a muḍāf ilayhi: shiqāq is annexed to the adverb by way of extension, and its original is "a disagreement between them", annexed on the pattern of His words «بل مكر الليل والنهار», whose original is "rather, plotting in the night and the day"; or on the basis that the "between" is made to be the one that causes disagreement, and the night and the day the ones that plot, on the pattern of their saying: "your day is going". The pronoun in بينهما refers to the two spouses even though they were not mentioned, since something that indicates them was mentioned, namely the men and the women. (فَابْعَثُوا حَكَماً مِنْ أَهْلِهِ وَحَكَماً مِنْ أَهْلِها) The fāʾ links the apodosis; ابعثوا is an imperative verb with an agent, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; حكما is a direct object; من أهله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective; and حكما من أهلها is conjoined to what precedes. (إِنْ يُرِيدا إِصْلاحاً يُوَفِّقِ اللَّهُ بَيْنَهُما) The clause is resumptive; إن is conditional; يريدا is the protasis, its jussive sign being the omission of the nūn, and the alif is the fāʿil; إصلاحا is a direct object; يوفق الله is the apodosis, and the clause has no position; and بينهما is an adverb attached to يوفق. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيماً خَبِيراً) إن and its ism; the clause of كان with its ism and its two khabars is the khabar of إن; the clause is a justification with no position. (وَاعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَلا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئاً) The wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, introduced to state the rights of parents, relatives, neighbours and the like. اعبدوا is an imperative verb and the wāw its agent; الله is its object; لا تشركوا is conjoined to what precedes; به is attached to تشركوا; and شيئا is a direct object, i.e. anything of things, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. anything of association. (وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً) The wāw is a conjunction; بالوالدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the verb of the omitted verbal noun; and إحسانا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "do good to them with a goodness". (وَبِذِي الْقُرْبى وَالْيَتامى وَالْمَساكِينِ وَالْجارِ ذِي الْقُرْبى وَالْجارِ الْجُنُبِ وَالصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنْبِ) All are conjoined, and بالجنب is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ) Likewise conjoined. (وَما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ) ما is a relative noun conjoined to what precedes, and the clause ملكت أيمانكم is the ṣila. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ مَنْ كانَ مُخْتالًا فَخُوراً) إن and its ism; the clause لا يحب is its khabar; من is a relative noun, a direct object; the clause كان is the ṣila, the ism of كان being latent; مختالا is the first khabar of كان and فخورا its second khabar.

* Benefits:
Nothing came in the Sharia indicating that the neighbour is one between whom and his neighbour there is a fixed measure, nor did anything occur in the language of the Arabs indicating that; rather, what is meant by al-jār in the language is the one adjacent, and it is applied to several meanings: among them the neighbour; the one you have protected from being wronged; the protector and the one seeking protection; the partner in trade; the husband of a woman, who is her jār; a woman's private part; what is near of dwellings; and the anus. It is related that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "I have settled in the quarter of a people, and the one nearest to me in neighbourhood is the one who harms me most." So the Prophet sent Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿAlī to cry out at the doors of the mosques:
"Verily, forty houses are neighbours, and he will not enter Paradise whose neighbour is not safe from his harms."
It was read والجار ذا القربى in the accusative as a specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), drawing attention to the greatness of his right.

dervis-irab:37-37.t:
* Vocabulary:
(البخل) is well known. It has four dialectal forms: fatḥa on the bāʾ and on the khāʾ; ḍamma on both; fatḥa on the bāʾ with sukūn on the khāʾ; and ḍamma on the bāʾ with sukūn on the khāʾ, which is the best known of them, and in it the majority of people read. It was also read in the three forms mentioned above.

* I'rab:
(الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ وَيَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبُخْلِ) A resumptive clause, introduced to prohibit miserliness and censure it. الذين is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "worthy of every censure and blame". You may also parse it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who".
It was said that it is a badal from «من كان», so that it falls within the scope of what precedes; and it was said that it is in the position of accusative as censure (ʿalā al-dhamm), so it is a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "I censure". The clause يبخلون is the ṣila of the relative; يأمرون الناس is conjoined to يبخلون; and بالبخل is attached to يأمرون. (وَيَكْتُمُونَ ما آتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; يكتمون is conjoined to يبخلون and the wāw is its agent; ما is its object; the clause آتاهم الله is a ṣila; and من فضله is attached to آتاهم. (وَأَعْتَدْنا لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذاباً مُهِيناً) The wāw is resumptive; أعتدنا is a verb and agent; وللكافرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعتدنا; عذابا is a direct object and مهينا an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «للكافرين» the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun, to proclaim that whoever has this as his habit is an ingrate toward the favour of Allah, and whoever is an ingrate toward His favour has a punishment that brands him with the brand with which the disbelievers are branded. Our poets alluded to this brand; Bashshār ibn Burd said:
وللبخيل على أمواله علل ... زرق العيون عليها أوجه سود
(The miser has, over his wealth, ailments: blue-eyed ones with black faces upon them.)
Al-Zamakhsharī has fine prose describing miserliness, from which we quote the following passages: «We have seen, among those afflicted with the disease of miserliness, one who, when it reaches his ear that someone has been generous to someone else, stares fixedly at him, undoes his cloak-wrapping and becomes agitated, his eyes rolling in his head as though his baggage had been plundered and his treasury broken open, out of vexation at that and regret that it exists.»

dervis-irab:38-38.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرئاء) and al-riyāʾ: spending for the sake of boasting and vying.

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوالَهُمْ رِئاءَ النَّاسِ) The wāw is a conjunction; الذين is conjoined to the preceding الذين; the clause ينفقون is the ṣila; أموالهم is a direct object; and رئاء الناس is an interpreted ḥāl, i.e. "showing off"; it may also be parsed as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. "so that it may be said: how generous they are!", and this is more apparent than the ḥāl, for the conditions for the accusative are fulfilled in it. (وَلا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَلا بِالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ) Conjoined to what precedes; the secret of the repetition of لا will come in the section on Rhetoric. (وَمَنْ يَكُنِ الشَّيْطانُ لَهُ قَرِيناً) The wāw is resumptive; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; يكن is the protasis; له is attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «قرينا»; and قرينا is the khabar of يكن. (فَساءَ قَرِيناً) The fāʾ links the apodosis, because ساء here is a defective past verb to express censure; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; قرينا is a tamyīz explaining the fāʿil; and the one specified for censure is omitted, its implied form being «هو», referring back to «الشيطان».
The clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من».

* Rhetoric:
In the repetition of the negative «لا» there is the art of repetition, and likewise of the bāʾ, to signal that each of the two is negated separately. If you say: لا أكرم زيدا وعمرا, the speech admits that generosity is negated of the pair together without it following that generosity is negated of each one of them, and it also admits that it is negated of both. But if you say: «ولا عمرا», the negation of generosity of both together is determined.

dervis-irab:39-40.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المثقال): what something is weighed against, whether heavy or much. The mithqāl of a thing is its weight or its balance; the plural is mathāqīl. By custom the mithqāl equals a dirham and a half, and it may sometimes exceed or fall short of that somewhat.

* I'rab:
(وَماذا عَلَيْهِمْ لَوْ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ) The wāw is resumptive; as for ماذا, it was said earlier that we have two ways of parsing it. One is that you make «ما» interrogative, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and «ذا» a relative here specifically, the khabar of «ما»; then «عليهم» is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative. The other
is that you make the whole of ماذا an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and عليهم attached to an omitted khabar. What is meant by the question here is rebuke, censure and denunciation. لو is conditional; آمنوا is the protasis, and the apodosis is omitted, the implication being "what harm would that do them?"
It is a common construction: you say to the avenger, "What would it harm you if you forgave?", and to the disobedient child, "What would it cost you if you were dutiful to your parents?", although it is known that there is neither harm nor loss in forgiveness and dutifulness; it is purely for rebuke and censure. It is also possible that «لو» is a maṣdar particle, and the interpreted maṣdar from «لو» and the verb is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "what is upon them in their believing". بالله is attached to آمنوا; اليوم is conjoined to the word of majesty; and الآخر is an adjective. (وَأَنْفَقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَهُمُ اللَّهُ) Conjoined to آمنوا; مما is attached to أنفقوا; and the clause رزقهم الله is the ṣila of the relative. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِهِمْ عَلِيماً) The wāw is resumptive; كان and its ism; بهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عليما; and عليما is the khabar of كان. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ) A resumptive clause, introduced as a preface to mentioning the recompense for good deeds and bad deeds. إن and its ism; the clause لا يظلم is its khabar; and مثقال ذرة is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, i.e. "a wrong the weight of an atom".
It was also said that «يظلم» is made to include the meaning of a verb that takes two objects, so «مثقال» is accusative as a second direct object, and the first is omitted, the implication being: "He does not diminish or defraud anyone of the weight of an atom". The first is easier and involves less strain. (وَإِنْ تَكُ حَسَنَةً يُضاعِفْها) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; تك is the protasis, its jussive sign being the sukūn implied on the nūn, which is omitted from the jussive imperfect of كان for lightness, a discussion of which has preceded. The ism of تك refers back to المثقال, and he made it feminine because it is annexed to ذرة, as has also been discussed. حسنة is the khabar of «تك»; يضاعفها is the apodosis and the hāʾ is a direct object. (وَيُؤْتِ مِنْ لَدُنْهُ أَجْراً عَظِيماً) يؤت is conjoined to يضاعفها; من لدنه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤت, or to an omitted ḥāl because it precedes the thing qualified; أجرا is a direct object and عظيما an adjective.

dervis-irab:78-78.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بُرُوجٍ): In the speech of the Arabs, البروج are fortresses and citadels.
(مُشَيَّدَةٍ): The scholars of Arabic differed over the meaning of المشيدة. Some of the Basrans said: المشيّدة is "tall"; he said: as for المشيد without shadda, it is "adorned" — this was said by Abū ʿUbayda in Majāz al-Qur'ān. Others of them said something like that, except that he said: المشيد without shadda is that which is worked with الشيد, and الشيد is gypsum plaster. Some of the Kufans said: المشيد and المشيّد are the same in origin, except that the shadda is put on one only for its own sake, and the verb of it is in a plural sense, like their saying:
هذه ثياب مصبغّة وغنم مذبّحة
("these are dyed garments and slaughtered sheep"); so it is doubled because it is a plural, in which the action is distributed. Likewise قصور مشيدة, since the palaces are many and the building was repeated in them; and for that reason it was said بروج مشيدة, and likewise His saying the Exalted «وغلقت الأبواب».

* I'rab:
(أَيْنَما تَكُونُوا يُدْرِكْكُمُ الْمَوْتُ) A resumptive speech, meant to address the Jews and the hypocrites and to explain that the world is worthless and has no permanence. أينما is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted khabar of تكونوا, preposed, if it is the defective كان; or attached to the apodosis if it is the complete (non-defective) كان; تكونوا is the protasis and the wāw is the fāʿil or the noun of تكونوا; and يدرككم الموت is the apodosis. (وَلَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُرُوجٍ مُشَيَّدَةٍ) The wāw is circumstantial and لو is conditional; كان and its noun; في بروج is attached to an omitted khabar of كنتم; مشيدة is an adjective of بروج; and the apodosis clause is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. (وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ حَسَنَةٌ يَقُولُوا هذِهِ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ) The wāw is resumptive and إن conditional; تصبهم is the protasis and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; حسنة is the fāʿil; يقولوا is the apodosis; هذه is a mubtadaʾ; من عند الله, the preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted khabar; and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech. (وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَقُولُوا هذِهِ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ) Conjoined to what precedes. (قُلْ كُلٌّ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ) The clause is resumptive, meant to censure their presumption; قل is an imperative; كل is a mubtadaʾ, for which it was permissible to begin with it because of the sense of generality in it; من عند الله is attached to an omitted khabar; and the nominal clause is the quoted speech. (فَمالِ هؤُلاءِ الْقَوْمِ لا يَكادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ حَدِيثاً) The fāʾ is resumptive and ما is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ; لهؤلاء is attached to an omitted khabar; القوم is a badal; the clause لا يكادون is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, the wāw being the noun of يكادون; the clause يفقهون is in the position of the accusative, the khabar of يكادون, the wāw being the fāʿil; and حديثا is the mafʿūl bihi.

* Benefits:
(أَيْنَما) أين is one of the nouns of place, vague, which falls upon the six directions and upon every place that is asked about, and it is transferred to the sense of requital (conditional), so one says: أين تكن أكن ("wherever you are, I will be").
Most often in its use the particle «ما» is joined to it, as in the verse, but that is not obligatory in it; rather you have a choice. Ibn Hammām al-Salūlī said:
أين تصرف بها العداة تجدنا ... نصرف العيس نحوها للتلاقي
(Wherever you turn the enemies with it, you will find us turning the pale camels toward them in order to meet.)

dervis-irab:79-79.t:
* I'rab:
(ما أَصابَكَ مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ) A resumptive speech, meant to give the answer to their words and refute them. The sense of combining the attribution of evil to the servant with the attribution of all things to Allah will come in the section on Rhetoric, in a way that quenches thirst. ما is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; أصابك is a past verb in the position of the jussive, the protasis; من حسنة is attached to an omitted ḥāl; the fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis; من الله, the preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. فهي من الله ("it is from Allah"); and the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar of من [Translator's note: the source says «خبر من», although the conditional noun here is «ما»; translated as written]. (وَما أَصابَكَ مِنْ سَيِّئَةٍ فَمِنْ نَفْسِكَ) Conjoined to what precedes. (وَأَرْسَلْناكَ لِلنَّاسِ رَسُولًا) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, meant to show the standing of the Messenger and to extol his great and lofty resolve; أرسلناك is a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; للناس is attached to أرسلناك or to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective and was put before; and رسولا is a ḥāl. (وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً) The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition and الله is the fāʿil of كفى in position, genitive in form by the bāʾ; and شهيدا is a tamyīz or a ḥāl, and the i'rab of that has already been given.

* Rhetoric:
The mujāz mursal in attributing the evil to the servant, the relation being causality, because it is the self that ruins its owner and entangles him in committing sins; and there is no contradiction between its being created and its being the one that entangles, so all of that is brought into order by His saying: «قل كل من عند الله». The Muʿtazila have lengthy speech on this matter, to which one should turn in the longer works, where the disagreement between Ahl al-Sunna and the Muʿtazila becomes bitter.

dervis-irab:80-81.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بيّت): بيّت الأمر means: he fabricated it, arranged it and decided it by night. التبييت is either from البيتوتة (spending the night), because it is deciding a matter and planning it at night — one says: هذا أمر بيّت بليل ("this is a matter plotted by night") — or from أبيات الشعر (verses of poetry), because the poet plans them and arranges them. The meaning in the verse is that they said and devised something other than the obedience they gave you; and every deed done at night has been "plotted"; from that comes بيّت للعدو, which is falling upon them by night. And from it is the saying of ʿUbayda ibn Hammām:
أتوني فلم أرض ما بيّتوا ... وكانوا أتوني بشيء نكر
لأنكح أيّمهم منذرا ... وهل ينكح العبد حرّ لحر
(They came to me, and I was not pleased with what they plotted, for they had come to me with something monstrous: that I should marry their widow to Mundhir. Does a free woman marry a slave, being freeborn herself?) He means by his saying "فلم أرض ما بيتوا" the night: that is, what they settled upon by night.
The meaning of his saying حر لحر is: a free man whom noble people bore, as you say: he is noble from noble people, and free from free people; the lām in it is of lineage, and "free" is traced to fathers and free people. This you will not find in a book, so memorise it.

* I'rab:
(مَنْ يُطِعِ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدْ أَطاعَ اللَّهَ) A resumptive speech, meant to explain that obedience to the Messenger is part of obedience to Allah and to explain the rulings of his message. من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ; يطع الرسول is the protasis; the fāʾ is connecting; قد is a particle of certainty; the clause فقد أطاع الله is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of من. (وَمَنْ تَوَلَّى فَما أَرْسَلْناكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَفِيظاً) The wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; تولى is a past verb in the position of the jussive, the protasis; the fāʾ is connecting for the answer; ما is negative; أرسلناك is a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «حفيظا»; حفيظا is a ḥāl; and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "so pay no heed to him"; the protasis and its omitted apodosis are in the position of the nominative, the khabar of «من»; and the clause ما أرسلناك is explanatory of the reason, with no position. (وَيَقُولُونَ طاعَةٌ) The wāw is resumptive; يقولون is an imperfect verb and fāʿil; طاعة is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "our command and our affair" [is obedience]; the clause is the quoted speech; and the clause يقولون is resumptive, meant to show their treatment of the Messenger after having shown the obligation of obeying him. (فَإِذا بَرَزُوا مِنْ عِنْدِكَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb of the future containing the sense of a condition; the clause برزوا is in the position of the genitive by annexation; and من عندك is attached to برزوا, i.e. "they went out from you". (بَيَّتَ طائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ غَيْرَ الَّذِي تَقُولُ) The clause بيت طائفة has no position because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition; منهم is attached to an omitted adjective of طائفة; غير is the mafʿūl bihi; الذي is the muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause تقول has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَاللَّهُ يَكْتُبُ ما يُبَيِّتُونَ) The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يكتب its khabar; ما is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi; and the clause يبيتون has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; أعرض is an imperative; عنهم is attached to أعرض; توكل is conjoined to أعرض; and على الله is attached to توكل. (وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا) The i'rab of its like has already been given.

* Benefits:
The verb is masculine in «بيت طائفة» because the feminine of الطائفة is not a real feminine, since it is in the sense of الفريق and الفوج (a company, a band), so it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) or a generic noun (ism jins).
The rulings on making the verb masculine or feminine with the fāʿil are set out at length in the books of grammar, so go back to them, and Allah is the Granter of success.

dervis-irab:48-50.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُزَكُّونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ): they describe themselves with the purity of deeds and obedience, and with abundance of worship and sincerity.
(فَتِيلًا): al-fatīl is the thread in the cleft of a date-stone, and the dirt that you roll between your fingers. One says "mā aghnā ʿanka fatīlan", that is, "nothing, to the measure of a fatīl". The Arabs coined a proverb for smallness from four things combined in the date-stone: the fatīl; the naqīr, which is the dimple in the back of the stone; the qiṭmīr, which is the thin husk over it; and these three occur in the Noble Qur'an. The fourth is the yaʿrūf, which is what lies between the stone and the calyx at the top of the fruit, like a link between them.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ): A resumptive statement, introduced to show that forgiveness is impossible without it. إن and its ism, and the clause لا يغفر is its khabar; أن and what is within its scope are an interpreted maṣdar in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of يغفر; and به is attached to يشرك. Al-Farrāʾ mentioned in his book Maʿānī al-Qur'an that it is accusative by removal of the preposition that would have governed it in the genitive had it been overt. In any case, the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يغفر. (وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ): The واو is a conjunction, and يغفر is conjoined to the negated verb, so it is affirmative; but it is better that it be resumptive, with يغفر resumptive and nominative, to avert confusion. ما is a relative noun and mafʿūl bihi; دون is an adverb of place attached to an omitted element functioning as ṣila of the relative; ذلك is muḍāf ilayhi, the demonstrative referring to the associating (ishrāk) understood from يشرك; لمن is attached to يغفر; and the clause يشاء has no position, because it is a ṣila of the relative. (وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدِ افْتَرى إِثْماً عَظِيماً): The واو is resumptive; من is conditional and a mubtadaʾ; يشرك is the protasis; بالله is attached to يشرك; the فاء in فقد links the apodosis; قد is a particle of emphasis; افترى is a past verb; إثما is a mafʿūl bihi; عظيما is a naʿt; and the clause joined with the فاء is in the position of jussive as apodosis; and the protasis with its apodosis are the khabar of من. (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ): A resumptive statement, introduced to express wonder at their claim to be pure before Allah despite the disbelief they are clothed in, since the Jews said: "We are the beloved ones of Allah." The hamza is for interrogation of wonder; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb jussive by لم; إلى الذين is attached to تر; and the clause يزكون أنفسهم is a ṣila of the relative. (بَلِ اللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَنْ يَشاءُ): بل is a particle of rejection (iḍrāb) and conjunction; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يزكي is its khabar; من is a relative noun and mafʿūl bihi; and the clause يشاء is a ṣila of the relative. (وَلا يُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا): The واو is a conjunction; لا is negative; يظلمون is an imperfect passive verb and the واو is the nāʾib fāʿil; it is conjoined to an omitted element, the implied form being "so they will be rewarded and will not be wronged"; and فتيلا is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "a wrong to the measure of a fatīl", like مثقال ذرة. It may also be parsed as a second mafʿūl, on the view that يظلمون implies the meaning of "they are diminished". This i'rab was given before under مثقال ذرة. (انْظُرْ كَيْفَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ): The clause is resumptive; انظر is an imperative verb; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as ḥāl or mafʿūl muṭlaq, and perhaps the second is preferable; يفترون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the واو is the agent; the interrogative clause is in the position of accusative as the object of انظر, because انظر is connected to the interrogative; على الله is attached to يفترون; and الكذب is a mafʿūl bihi or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, because it is synonymous with the governing verb يفترون, for lying and fabrication come from one valley. (وَكَفى بِهِ إِثْماً مُبِيناً): The واو is resumptive; كفى is a verb; به: the باء is a redundant preposition, and the هاء is the object of كفى in position; the agent is a latent pronoun explained by an indefinite noun, namely His words إثما; so إثما is a tamyīz, and مبينا a naʿt.

dervis-irab:51-54.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الجبت): the idol, and everything worshipped besides Allah.
(الطاغوت): the sorcerer. Many legends have been woven around the two, which you will find in the longer works.

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيباً مِنَ الْكِتابِ): A resumptive statement, introduced to speak of Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and others of the Jews when they came to Makka, saw the slain of Badr, and incited the polytheists to take revenge for them and to fight the Prophet ﷺ. The i'rab of its like was given just before. نصيبا is the second object of أوتوا, and من الكتاب is attached to an omitted element functioning as naʿt of نصيبا. (يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْجِبْتِ وَالطَّاغُوتِ): The clause يؤمنون is a ḥāl from «الذين» or from the واو in أوتوا; and if the seeing is of the heart, its position is accusative as second mafʿūl bihi of the «تر» of knowing. (وَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): The واو is a conjunction and يقولون is conjoined to يؤمنون; وللذين is attached to يقولون; and the clause كفروا is a ṣila of the relative. (هؤُلاءِ أَهْدى مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا سَبِيلًا): The clause is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech of their saying; هؤلاء is a demonstrative and mubtadaʾ; أهدى is its khabar; من الذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أهدى; the clause آمنوا is a ṣila of the relative; and سبيلا is a tamyīz. (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ): A resumptive clause to show their state and the reality of their affair. أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; الذين is the khabar of the demonstrative; and the clause لعنهم is a ṣila of the relative. (وَمَنْ يَلْعَنِ اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ نَصِيراً): The واو is resumptive; من is conditional and a fronted mafʿūl bihi of يلعن; يلعن is the protasis, jussive, and given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Al-Jalāl (may Allah have mercy on him) erred, for he implied an accusative pronoun, and it escaped him that the wording of the Qur'an may not be tampered with. الله is the agent; the فاء links the apodosis; لن is a particle of negation, accusation (naṣb) and futurity; تجد is an imperfect verb made accusative by لن; the clause joined with the فاء is in the position of jussive as apodosis; له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نصيرا; and نصيرا is the mafʿūl bihi of تجد. The protasis and apodosis are the khabar of «من».
(أَمْ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُلْكِ): أم is a disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) conjunction meaning بل; it is a conjunction of rejection and transition from censuring them for declaring themselves pure and the like, to censuring them for something else, namely their claim that they have a share of sovereignty. لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element functioning as fronted khabar; نصيب is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and من الملك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element functioning as naʿt of نصيب. (فَإِذاً لا يُؤْتُونَ النَّاسَ نَقِيراً): The فاء is the "eloquent" (faṣīḥa) فاء, because it discloses an implied condition, i.e. "if they were given a share of sovereignty, then…". إذن is a particle of response and consequence, and it has been made inoperative because it occurs after a conjunction, which is the more eloquent usage, as will come in the section on benefits. لا is negative; يؤتون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the واو is the agent; الناس is the first mafʿūl bihi and نقيرا the second. (أَمْ يَحْسُدُونَ النَّاسَ عَلى ما آتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): أم is a particle of conjunction and rejection meaning بل, and it is for beginning the second of their ugly traits; يحسدون is an imperfect verb, nominative; الناس is a mafʿūl bihi; على ما آتاهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يحسدون; the clause آتاهم is a ṣila; الله is the agent; and من فضله is attached to آتاهم. (فَقَدْ آتَيْنا آلَ إِبْراهِيمَ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ): The فاء is causal, as if giving the reason for the denial and the condemnation; قد is a particle of emphasis; آتينا is a verb and agent; آل ابراهيم is the first mafʿūl bihi; الكتاب the second; and الحكمة is conjoined to الكتاب. (وَآتَيْناهُمْ مُلْكاً عَظِيماً): conjoined to what preceded.

* Benefits:
(إذا) [Translator's note: the source prints إذا, but إذن is clearly meant throughout the discussion that follows.] is one of the particles that make the imperfect verb accusative by themselves, whereas the others do so through an implied أن accompanying them; they are: أن, لن, إذن, كي. As for إذن, it is a particle that governs the accusative because of its specificity and because it turns the verb to the future, and it is a particle of response and consequence. It has three cases:
1- That it enters the verb at the beginning of the response; here it must be operative, as in your saying "idhan akrimuka" ("then I will honour you"), in response to "I will visit you".
2- That what precedes it is a wāw or a fāʾ; here it is permissible to make it operative or inoperative, on two different considerations, as in your saying "Zayd yaqūmu wa-idhan yadhhabu" ("Zayd stands and then he goes"). Here both nominative and accusative are permissible on two different considerations. That is, if you conjoin «wa-idhan yadhhabu» to «yaqūmu», which is the khabar, you make «idhan» inoperative and it becomes like the khabar, because what is conjoined to something takes its place, as if you had said "Zayd idhan yadhhabu", and so what follows it depends on what precedes it, because it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. If you conjoin it to the first clause, the wāw is like a resumptive, and it is at the beginning of a speech, so for that reason it is made operative and the verb is accusative through it.
3- As for the third case, it is that it occurs in the middle, with what follows it depending on what precedes it, or the verb is a verb of present time, not future, in response to one who said: "I will visit you", "I, then, will honour you". Here the verb is nominative, because the verb after it depends on the mubtadaʾ, which is "anā". Likewise if you said: "In tukrimnī idhan akrimuka" ("If you honour me, then I will honour you"), the verb is jussive, because the verb after «idhan» depends on the particle of condition.
There are further details to which one returns in the books of grammar.

dervis-irab:55-56.t:
* I'rab:
(فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ آمَنَ بِهِ): The فاء is resumptive, for branching out; منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element functioning as a fronted khabar; من is a relative noun and a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause آمن is a ṣila of the relative; and به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمن. (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ صَدَّ عَنْهُ): conjoined to what preceded. (وَكَفى بِجَهَنَّمَ سَعِيراً): The واو is resumptive; كفى is a past verb; the باء is a redundant particle; جهنم is genitive by the باء in form and nominative in position as the agent of كفى; and سعيرا is a tamyīz or ḥāl. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِنا سَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِمْ ناراً): إن and its ism; the clause كفروا is a ṣila of the relative; بآياتنا is attached to كفروا; سوف is a particle of futurity; نصليهم is an imperfect verb, the هاء is its first object and نارا its second object; the clause سوف نصليهم نارا is the khabar of إن; and the clause of إن and what is within its scope is resumptive. (كُلَّما نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ بَدَّلْناهُمْ جُلُوداً غَيْرَها): The clause is a ḥāl from the accusative pronoun in «نصليهم», and you may make it a naʿt of «نارا»; in which case an omitted returning pronoun must be implied, i.e. "whenever their skins are well done in it". كلما is an adverb of time containing the meaning of condition, attached to بدلناهم; the clause نضجت جلودهم is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi if ما is taken as redundant, but if it is a particle-like relative (maṣdar-forming), it has no position; and the clause بدلناهم has no position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. بدلناهم is a verb, agent and first mafʿūl bihi; جلودا is a second mafʿūl bihi, or accusative by removal of the preposition; and غيرها is a naʿt of جلودا. (لِيَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ): The لام is for cause and genitive; يذوقوا is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the lām of cause, its accusative marking being the dropping of the nūn, and the واو is the agent; العذاب is its object; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to بدلناهم. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَزِيزاً حَكِيماً): إن and its ism, and the clause كان is its khabar; the ism of كان is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; عزيزا is the first khabar of كان and حكيما its second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The takhyīlī implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya takhyīliyya) in His words «ليذوقوا العذاب»: the thing compared (al-mushabbah) is omitted, and one of its concomitants is borrowed, namely tasting; and what is meant by tasting here is its perpetuity, together with the repugnance and indescribable pain that accompany it. There is no doubt that the continuation of the tasting of the punishment while the bodies remain alive and preserved in it contains what it contains of ruling out whatever might cross the mind of imagining that the punishment and its pain will cease. Not to mention the effect that the sense of taste has on the soul of one burned by fire.

dervis-irab:82-83.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَتَدَبَّرُونَ): they ponder. تدبر الشيء means to ponder it and to look into its consequences and what results from it and where it ends up.
(أَذاعُوا): It has the sense of the base verb «ذاع». One says ذاع الشيء يذيع, and one also says أذاع الشيء, and it takes an object the same way. It may be a case of taḍmīn (embedding a meaning), أذاع having been made to include the meaning of "he spoke of", so that it is transitive by itself and with the bāʾ. This word is, as it were, a correct expression for the broadcasting which broadcasts news at set times. الإذاعة is spreading abroad (الإشاعة). He said:
أذاع به في الناس حتى كأنه ... بعلياء نار أوقدت بثقوب
(He spread it abroad among the people until it was like a fire kindled on a height with a kindling stick.)
al-Zamakhsharī preferred that the meaning be "they performed the act of broadcasting with it", which is more eloquent than أذاعوه, so that the discipline is more forceful and the prohibition more comprehensive. In that is teaching and a warning of the obligation to keep secret the news of armies and their movements; and how great is the harm in people's chattering about every report and rumour that strikes their ears, particularly in our time, after the abandoned enemy invaded the Arab lands — may Allah purify them of his filth and protect them from his abomination.
(يَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ): they draw out its management by their sagacity and their complete knowledge of the affairs and stratagems of war. In origin it means drawing out water when the earth is first dug, and it was borrowed for what a man draws out of meanings by the excellence of his mind. In the coming together of the nūn and the bāʾ as the first and second radicals of the word there is a wondrous secret, for they indicate appearing and becoming clear: النبأ is the report that appears to people so that they pass it on and exchange it among themselves. سبيل نأبيء means a road that is evident and sudden. نبّ التيس نبيبا means the billy-goat bleated in rut, and in his bleating is an appearing of himself. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the delegation of the people of Kufa when they complained of Saʿd: "Some of you speak to me, but do not bleat before me the bleating of billy-goats."
From this word is derived الانبوب (tube), plural أنابيب. He said:
أو من مشعشعة ورهاء نشوتها ... أو من أنابيب تفاح ورمان
(Or from a diluted wine, a foolish one in its intoxication; or from the tubes of apple and pomegranate.)
And نبت: it appeared; one says: ظهر النبات والنبت في الأرض (the plant and the sprout appeared in the earth).
And نبس: he spoke; you say: كلمته فعبس وما نبس ("I spoke to him and he frowned and did not utter a word").
And نبش الأرض عما تحتها نبشا (he dug up the earth for what is under it). He said:
مهلا بني عمنا مهلا موالينا ... لا تنبشوا بيننا ما كان مدفونا
(Gently, sons of our uncle, gently, our allies; do not dig up between us what was buried.)
The discussion of النبط has preceded, and from it they derived الأنباط. Khālid ibn al-Walīd said to ʿAbd al-Masīḥ ibn Buqayla: "Are you Arabs or Nabateans?" He said: "Arabs who drew out (استنبطنا), and Nabateans who became Arabised (استعربنا)." And Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī said:
أين امرؤ القيس والعذارى ... إذ مال من تحته الغبيط
استنبط العرب في الموامي ... بعدك واستعرب النبيط
(Where is Imruʾ al-Qays and the maidens, when the camel-saddle tilted beneath him? The Arabs drew water in the deserts after you, and the Nabateans became Arabised.)
This is among the strange things of this noble language.

* I'rab:
(أَفَلا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ الْقُرْآنَ) The hamza is for a disapproving question and the fāʾ is a conjunction on an implied clause, i.e.: "Do they turn away from the Qur'an, so that they do not ponder it?" لا is negative; يتدبرون is an imperfect verb and fāʿil; and القرآن is its mafʿūl bihi [Translator's note: the source prints «مفعونه», evidently a misprint for «مفعوله»]. (وَلَوْ كانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ غَيْرِ اللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا فِيهِ اخْتِلافاً كَثِيراً) The wāw is circumstantial and لو is conditional; كان is the defective verb with a latent noun, i.e. the Qur'an; من عند غير الله is attached to an omitted khabar; the lām occurs in the answer to لو; وجدوا is a verb and fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition; فيه is attached to وجدوا; اختلافا is the mafʿūl bihi; and كثيرا is an adjective. (وَإِذا جاءَهُمْ أَمْرٌ مِنَ الْأَمْنِ أَوِ الْخَوْفِ أَذاعُوا بِهِ) A resumptive speech, meant to describe the hypocrites who broadcast rumours to discourage the people and to spread fear in their souls. إذا is an adverb of the future containing the sense of a condition; the clause جاءهم أمر is in the position of the genitive by annexation; من الأمن is attached to an omitted adjective of أمر; الخوف is conjoined to الأمن; and the clause أذاعوا به has no position because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition. (وَلَوْ رَدُّوهُ إِلَى الرَّسُولِ وَإِلى أُولِي الْأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ) The wāw is circumstantial and لو conditional; ردّوه is a verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; إلى الرسول is attached to ردّوه; إلى أولي الأمر is conjoined to «إلى الرسول»; and منهم is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (لَعَلِمَهُ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ مِنْهُمْ) The lām occurs in the answer to لو; علمه الذين: verb, mafʿūl bihi and fāʿil; the clause يستنبطونه has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; the clause لعلمه الذين has no position because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition; and منهم is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لَاتَّبَعْتُمُ الشَّيْطانَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا) The wāw is resumptive and لولا is a particle of prevention due to existence, containing the sense of a condition; فضل الله is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; عليكم is attached to فضل; رحمته is conjoined to فضل; the lām occurs in the answer to لولا; the clause اتبعتم has no position because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition; الشيطان is the mafʿūl bihi; إلا is a particle of exception; and قليلا is the excepted from the fāʿil of اتبعتم, i.e.: "except a few of you"; or from the fāʿil of أذاعوا به, i.e.: "they made that matter known, except a few of them." More of its meaning and i'rab will come in the section on Benefits.

* Benefits:
The exegetes and i'rab-writers expanded at length on this exception. Were we to seek exhaustiveness, the space would be too narrow for us, and the danger of expanding is increased by the bitter dispute between Ahl al-Sunna and Ahl al-Iʿtizāl (the Muʿtazila); and we do not like to pass over that without pointing to it. The gist of what they set out is that in His saying «إلا قليلا» there are several views; we have chosen what seemed to us closest to the meaning and nearest to logic, and there is no harm in citing some of what they said:
1- That it is excepted from the fāʿil of «اتبعتم», i.e.: a small group among you did not follow Satan; and by "bounty" would be meant the sending of Muḥammad ﷺ, like Quss ibn Sāʿida al-Iyādī, ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, Waraqa ibn Nawfal and others who believed before the sending of the Prophet ﷺ.
2- That what is meant is whoever the obligation had not reached, so the exception on this view is discontinuous (munqaṭiʿ).
3- That it is excepted from the fāʿil of أذاعوا, i.e.: they made that matter known, except a few of them.
4- That it is excepted from the fāʿil of «لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه».
5- That it is excepted from the fāʿil of «لوجدوا».
6- That it is excepted from the general, and by "the few" is meant the community of Muḥammad.

What Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī says:
Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī said: «The most correct of these views, in my opinion, is the view of whoever said: "What is meant is the exception of the few from the broadcasting."» And he said after a long discussion: «We said that this is more correct only because the matter cannot fall outside one of the views we have mentioned, and it is impermissible that it be from His saying "لاتبعتم الشيطان", because it is impermissible that someone upon whom Allah has bestowed His bounty and mercy be of the followers of Satan.
[Translator's note: the source quotation of al-Ṭabarī ends here, without a closing quotation mark and mid-discussion, as printed.]

dervis-irab:131-132.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) The wāw is resumptive; ولله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar, preposed; ما is a relative noun, postposed mubtadaʾ; في السموات is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun; and ما في الأرض is conjoined to ما في السموات. (وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ) The wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of certainty; وصينا is a verb and fāʿil; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause أوتوا الكتاب is the ṣila, and الكتاب is the second mafʿūl bihi of «أوتوا»; the clause قد وصينا has no position because it is the answer to the implied oath; من قبلكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl; and إياكم is conjoined to الذين, i.e. "and We have enjoined you" (أَنِ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ) أن is explicative (mufassira) meaning أي, because enjoining is in the sense of saying; or it is maṣdar-forming, in which case it and the verb after it are interpreted as a maṣdar accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. بأن اتقوا, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to وصينا. (وَإِنْ تَكْفُرُوا فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is a jussive conditional particle; تكفروا is the protasis and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "you will not harm Him at all"; the fāʾ is a conjunction; إن is a particle resembling the verb; لله is attached to an omitted khabar of إن, preposed; ما is a relative noun, the postposed noun of إنّ; في السموات is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun; and ما في الأرض is conjoined to ما في السموات. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَنِيًّا حَمِيداً) The wāw is a conjunction; كان with its noun and its two khabars. (وَلِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of «ما», preposed; ما is a relative noun, postposed mubtadaʾ; في السموات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun; and ما في الأرض is conjoined to ما في السموات. (وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا) The wāw is resumptive; كفى is a past verb; the bāʾ is a preposition added to the fāʿil, which is Allah; and وكيلا is a tamyīz.

dervis-irab:133-134.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ وَيَأْتِ بِآخَرِينَ) إن is conditional; يشأ is the protasis; يذهبكم is the apodosis; أيها الناس: its i'rab has already been given; يأت is conjoined to يذهبكم; and بآخرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأت. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلى ذلِكَ قَدِيراً) The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; كان and its noun; قديرا is its khabar; and على ذلك is attached to «قديرا». (مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوابَ الدُّنْيا) من is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; كان is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive, the protasis; its noun is latent, referring back to «من»; the clause يريد is its khabar; and ثواب الدنيا is the mafʿūl bihi. (فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ ثَوابُ الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ) The fāʾ is connecting for the answer; عند is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar, preposed; the word "Allah" is the muḍāf ilayhi; ثواب الدنيا والآخرة is a postposed mubtadaʾ; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (وَكانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعاً بَصِيراً) The wāw is resumptive; كان with its noun and its two khabars.

dervis-irab:57-57.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ظليل): an adjective of ظل (shade), derived from it to reinforce its content, as one says "laylun alīl" and "yawmun ayyam", that is, perpetual, which the sun does not remove; and "sajsaj", in which there is neither heat nor cold.

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ): The واو is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to «الذين كفروا» to establish the state of these and of those, as will come in the section on rhetoric. الذين is a relative noun and mubtadaʾ, and the clause آمنوا is a ṣila of the relative. (سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً): The clause «سندخلهم» is the khabar of الذين; the هاء is the first mafʿūl bihi and جنات the second mafʿūl bihi by broad usage (ʿalā l-saʿa), and its like has already been given, or it is accusative by removal of the preposition; the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is a naʿt of جنات; خالدين is a ḥāl; فيها is attached to خالدين; and أبدا is an adverb also attached to خالدين. (لَهُمْ فِيها أَزْواجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ): The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element functioning as fronted khabar; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element functioning as ḥāl; أزواج is a delayed mubtadaʾ and مطهرة a naʿt, that is, these spouses are purified of the impurities known in this world, such as menstruation and the like. The nominal clause is a second naʿt of جنات.
(وَنُدْخِلُهُمْ ظِلًّا ظَلِيلًا): The clause is conjoined; ظلا is a second mafʿūl bihi by broad usage, the first mafʿūl being the هاء; and ظليلا is a naʿt.

* Rhetoric:
In the conjoining of «الذين آمنوا» to «الذين كفروا» there is a confused laff and nashr (a scrambled "folding and unfolding" arrangement), to which reference was made earlier, along with the antithesis (muqābala) and parallelism in the speech.

dervis-irab:58-58.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَماناتِ إِلى أَهْلِها): A resumptive statement, introduced to affirm trusts after the earlier mention of the Jews' breach and violation of them. إن and its ism, and the clause يأمركم is its khabar; أن and what is within its scope are an interpreted maṣdar accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "to render (bi-an tuʾaddū)", the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to يأمركم, or else it is a second mafʿūl bihi of يأمركم; الأمانات is the mafʿūl bihi of تؤدوا, its accusative marking being the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; and إلى أهلها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تؤدوا. (وَإِذا حَكَمْتُمْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ أَنْ تَحْكُمُوا بِالْعَدْلِ): The واو is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb of the future containing the meaning of condition, attached to an omitted element, since what follows the maṣdar-forming أن does not act on what precedes it, and the implied form is "He commands you"; the clause حكمتم is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; بين الناس is an adverb attached to حكمتم; أن تحكموا is an interpreted maṣdar conjoined to أن تؤدوا, so that the adverb has come between the conjunction and the conjoined element; and بالعدل is attached to تحكموا, though you may attach it to an omitted element functioning as ḥāl from the agent of تحكموا, i.e. "being clothed in justice". (إِنَّ اللَّهَ نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ): The clause is resumptive, introduced to give the reason for the command. نعما originally is نعم and ما: نعم is a fixed past verb that forms praise, and ما is an indefinite complete noun, accusative as tamyīz, the agent being a latent pronoun specified by an indefinite noun; or «ما» is a relative and is the agent of نعم, and the clause يعظكم به is a naʿt of the thing praised (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ), which is omitted, the implied form being: "How excellent is the thing, a thing with which He admonishes you." The described noun is omitted in the manner of His words: «من الذين هادوا يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه», the meaning being "a people who distort the words"; this was stated just before, so renew your acquaintance with it. به is attached to يعظكم, and the clause نعما is the khabar of إن. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ سَمِيعاً بَصِيراً): إن and its ism, and the clause كان is its khabar; سميعا is the first khabar of كان and بصيرا its second.

* Benefits:
1- Al-amāna (trust) is an inclusive noun covering all rights, whether due to Allah or to a human being, and its details are recorded in the longer works. On the authority of Abū Hurayra, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Render the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you."
Al-Baghawī related with his chain of transmission from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never gave us a sermon without saying: «لا إيمان لمن لا أمانة له، ولا دين لمن لا عهد له» ('There is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness, and no religion for one who has no covenant')."
2- نعمّا: with a kasra on the nūn, following the kasra of the ʿayn.

dervis-irab:59-59.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَأُولِي الْأَمْرِ مِنْكُمْ): A resumptive statement addressed to all people, commanding obedience to the rulers. The i'rab of the vocative has been given many times. أطيعوا الله: an imperative verb, agent and object; أطيعوا الرسول is conjoined to أطيعوا الله; and أولي الأمر is conjoined as well. أولي is accusative, its accusative marking being the yāʾ because it is attached to the sound masculine plural; and منكم is attached to an omitted element functioning as ḥāl. (فَإِنْ تَنازَعْتُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ فَرُدُّوهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ): The فاء is resumptive and إن is conditional; تنازعتم is a past verb in the position of jussive as protasis; في شيء is attached to تنازعتم; فردوه: the فاء links the apodosis, and ردوه is an imperative verb, agent and object; إلى الله is attached to ردوه; الرسول is conjoined to الله; and the clause joined with the فاء is in the position of jussive as apodosis. (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ): إن is conditional; كنتم is the defective كان and its ism, the past verb being in the position of jussive as protasis; the clause تؤمنون is in the position of accusative as khabar of كنتم; بالله is attached to تؤمنون; اليوم is conjoined to الله and الآخر is a naʿt; the conditional clause is resumptive, and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then refer it". (ذلِكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلًا): The clause is resumptive; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and خير its khabar; أحسن is conjoined to خير; تأويلا is a tamyīz; and the demonstrative refers to the referral.

* Benefits:
In this verse there is an allusion to the four juristic proofs: His words «أطيعوا الله» point to the Book; His words «وأطيعوا الرسول» point to the Sunna; His words «وأولي الأمر» point to consensus (ijmāʿ); and His words «فإن تنازعتم» point to analogy (qiyās).

dervis-irab:60-60.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا بِما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ): A resumptive statement, introduced to show the occasion for wonder at the state of those who claimed for themselves that they had combined belief in what was sent down to the Messenger of Allah, namely the Qur'an, and in what was sent down to the prophets before him, and then came with what contradicts this claim and topples it from its foundation, namely their desire to seek judgment from the ṭāghūt; thus they combined the two contradictories and joined the two opposites. The hamza is for interrogation of wonder. لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb jussive by لم, its jussive marking being the dropping of the weak letter, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta", the one addressed being the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; إلى الذين is attached to تر; and the verb of seeing is suspended (ʿulliqa) if it is of the heart. The clause يزعمون is a ṣila of the relative; وأنهم: أن and its ism, and the clause آمنوا is its khabar; أن with its ism has taken the place of the two objects of يزعمون; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنوا; أنزل is a passive past verb and the clause is a ṣila; and إليك is attached to أنزل. (وَما أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): The واو is a conjunction, and ما is conjoined to the first ما; the clause أنزل is a ṣila; and من قبلك is attached to أنزل or to an omitted element functioning as ḥāl. (يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَتَحاكَمُوا إِلَى الطَّاغُوتِ): The clause يريدون is a ḥāl clause; أن and what is within its scope are an interpreted maṣdar functioning as mafʿūl bihi of يريدون; and إلى الطاغوت is attached to يتحاكموا. (وَقَدْ أُمِرُوا أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا بِهِ): The واو is a wāw of ḥāl; قد is a particle of emphasis; أمروا is a passive past verb and the واو is the nāʾib fāʿil; أن يكفروا is an interpreted maṣdar accusative by removal of the preposition; and به is attached to يكفروا. (وَيُرِيدُ الشَّيْطانُ أَنْ يُضِلَّهُمْ ضَلالًا بَعِيداً): The واو is a conjunction; يريد الشيطان is conjoined to يريدون; أن يضلهم is an interpreted maṣdar, the object of يريد; ضلالا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; and بعيدا is a naʿt.

dervis-irab:61-63.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعالَوْا إِلى ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ وَإِلَى الرَّسُولِ): A resumptive statement, introduced to complete the material of wonder at their state. The واو is resumptive; إذا is an adverb of the future containing the meaning of condition, attached to the apodosis, which is رأيت; the clause قيل is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; لهم is attached to قيل; the clause تعالوا is the quoted speech; وإلى ما أنزل الله is attached to تعالوا; the clause أنزل الله is a ṣila of the relative; and وإلى الرسول is conjoined to His words: إلى ما أنزل الله. (رَأَيْتَ الْمُنافِقِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْكَ صُدُوداً): رأيت is a verb and agent, and the clause has no position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; المنافقين is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause يصدون is a ḥāl if the seeing is of the eye, or a second mafʿūl bihi if the seeing is of the heart; عنك is attached to يصدون; and صدودا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq. (فَكَيْفَ إِذا أَصابَتْهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ): The فاء is resumptive; كيف is an interrogative noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as ḥāl, i.e. "how will they act?" or "how will you see them?"; it may also be a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "how is their doing, or their state?". إذا is an adverb of the future containing the meaning of condition, attached to the omitted apodosis; the clause أصابتهم is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; مصيبة is the agent; بما is attached to أصابتهم; ما may be maṣdar-forming or a relative; the clause قدمت أيديهم has no position; and أيديهم is the agent. (ثُمَّ جاؤُكَ يَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ إِنْ أَرَدْنا إِلَّا إِحْساناً وَتَوْفِيقاً): ثم جاءوك is conjoined to أصابتهم, and I see no justification for what some have done in conjoining it to the clause يصدون, as al-Bayḍāwī holds. The clause يحلفون بالله is a ḥāl clause; إن is negative; أردنا is a verb and agent; إلا is a particle of restriction; إحسانا is a mafʿūl bihi; and توفيقا is conjoined to إحسانا. (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ ما فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ): The clause is resumptive, introduced to add warning about their hypocrisy. أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and الذين is the khabar of the demonstrative; the clause يعلم الله is a ṣila of the relative; ما is a relative noun and mafʿūl bihi; and في قلوبهم is attached to an omitted element functioning as ṣila of the relative. (فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَعِظْهُمْ وَقُلْ لَهُمْ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ قَوْلًا بَلِيغاً): The فاء is the "eloquent" فاء, which discloses an implied condition, i.e. "if their state is thus, then turn away from them and accept no excuse from them". أعرض is an imperative verb whose agent is "anta"; عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعرض; and the clause has no position, because it is the apodosis of an omitted non-jussive condition. وعظهم is conjoined to أعرض; وقل لهم is conjoined to أعرض; لهم is attached to قل; and as for في أنفسهم, concerning what this preposition and its genitive noun are attached to there are three analyses, equal in soundness and quality:
1- That they are attached to بليغا, because his command to threaten them reaches the core of their hearts. The context of the threat in His words: «فكيف إذا أصابتهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم، ثم جاءوك» bears witness to it.
2- That they are attached to قل, and its meaning: "say to them, concerning their own vile selves and their hearts folded upon evil, a penetrating word". The context suits it, in His words: «أولئك الذين يعلم الله ما في قلوبهم», of the inner recesses of error and impulses of misguidance.
3- That they are attached to an omitted element functioning as ḥāl, i.e. the thing said being a secret that does not go beyond their selves and does not pass them. The conduct of the Prophet ﷺ bears witness to it, and it accords with the Prophet's eagerness for concealment and gentleness, in the hope that they would return to right guidance and settle on the right. قولا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq and بليغا a naʿt, or a ḥāl, the two of them being alone with them. And advice in private is more beneficial than in public.

dervis-irab:135-135.t:
* Vocabulary:
(القسط) justice. In al-Miṣbāḥ al-Munīr: قسط يقسط قسطا, of the pattern ضرب: he acted unjustly, and also he acted justly, so it is one of the contronyms (aḍdād), as Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ said. And أقسط with alif: he acted justly, and the noun is القسط with kasra.
(تَلْوُوا): you incline your tongues, turning away from the truth. One says: لواني الرجل حقي, and القوم يلوونني ديني, and that is when they put him off with delay (liyyan). So by اللي is meant procrastination. al-Aʿshā said:
يلوينني ديني النّهار وأقتضي ... ديني إذا وقذ النّعاس الراقدا
(They put off my debt by day, and I collect my debt when drowsiness has overpowered the sleeper.)
This verse is from a set of fine verses, the first of which is:
إن الغواني لا يواصلن امرأ ... فقد الشباب وقد يصلن الأمردا
(The fair maidens do not keep company with a man who has lost his youth, though they may keep company with the beardless youth.)

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) The i'rab of its like has already been given. (كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ) A resumptive speech, meant to establish justice with the rich and the poor alike. كونوا is a defective imperative verb and the wāw is its noun; قوامين is its khabar; and بالقسط is attached to قوامين. (شُهَداءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلى أَنْفُسِكُمْ) شهداء is a second khabar of كونوا; لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شهداء; the wāw is circumstantial; لو is conditional; and على أنفسكم is attached to an omitted khabar of the omitted كان and its noun after the conditional لو, i.e.: "even if the testimony be against yourselves"; and the answer to لو is omitted, i.e.: "so do not hold back from giving testimony." (أَوِ الْوالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ) Conjoined to أنفسكم. (إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيراً فَاللَّهُ أَوْلى بِهِما) إن is conditional; يكن is a defective imperfect verb, the protasis, and the noun of يكن is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "the one testified against"; غنيا is the khabar of يكن; أو is a conjunction; فقيرا is conjoined to «غنيا»; the fāʾ in فالله is connecting for the apodosis; الله is a mubtadaʾ and أولى a khabar; بهما is attached to أولى; and the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis. (فَلا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ and لا is prohibitive; تتبعوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, the wāw being the fāʿil; الهوى is the mafʿūl bihi; and أن with what is in its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, a mafʿūl li-ajlihi of «تعدلوا»: either from العدل (justice), in which case the implied form is "out of dislike that you act justly", or from العدول (deviating), in which case the implied form is "in order that you deviate" [Translator's note: the source reads «بغية أن أن تعدلوا» with a doubled «أن», evidently a typographical repetition; translated once]. (وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيراً) The wāw is a conjunction and إن conditional; تلووا is the protasis; أو تعرضوا is conjoined to it; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the connecting fāʾ, the implied form being "He will punish you"; إن and its noun; the clause كان is its khabar; بما تعملون is attached to «خبيرا»; the clause تعملون has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; خبيرا is the khabar of «كان»; and the whole clause is explanatory of the reason for what precedes, with no position.

* Benefits:
1- The grammarians differed over the antecedent of the pronoun in His saying «بهما». The rule is that when the conjunction is «أو», the ruling regarding the return of the pronoun, predication and the like belongs to one of the two things or things; so you say: زيد أو عمرو أكرمته, and you do not say أكرمتهما. On this basis the following objection arises: how is the pronoun dual in «بهما» when the conjunction is «أو»? The statement of the answer comes down to the following: a- The pronoun in «بهما» does not refer back to the rich man and the poor man mentioned, but to the genus of rich and poor, and the genus is one.
b- That «أو» is not for choice but for distribution (tafṣīl); this is what Abū al-Baqāʾ inclined to, and he said, in meaning: each one of the one testified for and the one testified against may be rich and may be poor, and they may both be rich and may both be poor; so since the divisions upon distribution were such and were not mentioned, «أو» was brought to indicate distribution. On this the pronoun in «بهما» refers back to the one testified for and the one testified against, in whatever state they are.

The wording of Ibn Jarīr:
As for Ibn Jarīr, he said: What is meant is: Allah is more entitled to the wealth of the rich and the poverty of the poor, because that is from Him and from none other, and for that reason He said «بهما» and did not say «به».
And others said: أو here has the meaning of the wāw.
2- The omission of «كان» and its noun is frequent after the conditional «إن» and «لو».
Because «إن» is the mother of the jussive particles and «لو» the mother of the non-jussive particles, just as «كان» is the mother of its chapter. They allow latitude with the mothers that they do not allow with others. Among the examples of omitting كان and its noun after إن in poetry is the saying of al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Mundhir:
قد قيل ما قيل إن صدقا وإن كذبا ... فما اعتذارك من قول إذا قيلا
(What has been said has been said, whether true or false; so what is your excuse for a saying once it has been said?)
That is: إن كان المقول صدقا وإن كان المقول كذبا ("if what was said was true and if what was said was false"). Among the examples of omitting it together with its noun after «لو» is the saying of another:
لا يأمن الدهر ذو بغي ولو ملكا ... جنوده ضاق عنها السهل والجبل
(No oppressor is safe from time, even a king whose troops are too many for the plain and the mountain.)
That is: ولو كان الباغي ملكا ("even if the oppressor were a king").

dervis-irab:136-136.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) Its i'rab has already been given. (آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتابِ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ عَلى رَسُولِهِ) A resumptive speech, meant to command steadfastness in faith.
آمنوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; بالله is attached to آمنوا; رسوله is conjoined to الله; الكتاب is also conjoined; الذي is an adjective of الكتاب; and the clause نزل على رسوله is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَالْكِتابِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ) والكتاب is also conjoined, i.e. the genus "book", for what is meant is the revealed books; الذي is an adjective and the clause أنزل is the ṣila of the relative noun; من is a preposition, and قبل is an adverb indeclinable on ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording, not in meaning; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنزل. (وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ) The wāw is resumptive and من is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; يكفر is the protasis; بالله is attached to يكفر; and what follows is conjoined to it. (فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلالًا بَعِيداً) The fāʾ in فقد is connecting for the apodosis, and قد is a particle of certainty; ضل is a past verb; ضلالا is the mafʿūl muṭlaq; and بعيدا is an adjective. The clause is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis, and the clause of the protasis with its apodosis is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of «من».

dervis-irab:137-137.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدادُوا كُفْراً) A resumptive speech, meant to describe the vacillation of the Jews and the hypocrites in the abysses of trials and unrest. إن and its noun; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila; the conjunction was repeated to make plain their end, their becoming and their wavering between disbelief and belief; and كفرا is a tamyīz. (لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا) The clause is the khabar of إنّ; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; يكن is a defective imperfect verb and الله is its noun; ليغفر: the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), and يغفر is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after it; the preposition and its genitive noun — the lām of denial and the interpreted maṣdar — are attached to an omitted khabar of يكن, i.e. "intending to forgive them"; the preposition and its genitive noun «لهم» are attached to يغفر; ولا ليهديهم is conjoined to what precedes; and سبيلا is the second mafʿūl bihi of ليهديهم, or it is accusative by removal of the preposition, with the preposition and its genitive noun attached to يهديهم.

dervis-irab:163-165.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الوحي): in the language it is applied to the sign and gesture, and from it comes His saying, the Exalted: «فأوحى إليهم أن سبّحوا بكرة وعشيّا»; and to inspiration that occurs in the soul, which is subtler than the gesture, and from it comes His saying, the Exalted: «وأوحينا إلى أم موسى». It appears that this is by the care of Allah, mighty and majestic.
