Some of it is permanently instinctive, and from it comes His saying, the Exalted: «وأوحى ربك إلى النحل»; and to informing in secret, which is that you inform a person of a matter you hide from others, and from it comes His saying, the Exalted: «شياطين الإنس والجن يوحي بعضهم إلى بعض». It was also applied to writing and to a message because of the particularity in them. The revelation of Allah to His prophets is what He casts to them of necessary knowledge that He conceals from others, after having prepared them to receive it, whether through an intermediary such as the angel or without an intermediary.

The view of Muḥammad ʿAbduh:
The teacher and imam Shaykh Muḥammad ʿAbduh defined it in Risālat al-Tawḥīd as «a knowledge that a person finds in himself with certainty that it is from Allah, whether through an intermediary or without one. The first presents itself to his hearing with a voice or without a voice. It is distinguished from inspiration in that inspiration is a perception the soul is certain of and is driven to what is asked, without awareness of where it came from, and it is more like the sensation of hunger, thirst, sorrow and joy.» Then the imam went on at length explaining how it is possible and how it occurs.
(الْأَسْباطِ): plural of sibṭ, which is applied to a grandchild. The tribes (asbāṭ) of the Children of Israel were twelve.
(الزبور): in the sense of «mazbūr» (written), like rukūb in the sense of markūb (ridden). Ḥamza and Khalaf read it with ḍamma on the zāy; it is then a plural of the same pattern as its singular, and it was said that it is a maṣdar.
In any case it means a book and something written. In al-Mukhtār: al-zabr with kasra, and the plural is zubūr, like qidr and qudūr.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّا أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ كَما أَوْحَيْنا إِلى نُوحٍ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ) A resumptive statement, offered to reassure the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by mentioning the prophets whom Allah sent to mankind before him. إن and its noun; the clause أوحينا is the khabar (predicate); إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوحينا; the kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "a revelation like Our revelation"; «ما» may be a maṣdar particle, in which case it is, with what follows it, an interpreted maṣdar in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, like "Our revelation"; or it may be a relative noun meaning "that which" with its returning pronoun omitted, that is, "like that which We revealed to Noah", and the clause أوحينا has no position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative. وإلى نوح is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوحينا; النبيين is conjoined to نوح; من بعده is attached to an omitted ḥāl. He began with the mention of Noah because he is the earliest sent prophet mentioned in the books of the people.
An argument stands as proof against people only when its premises are known to them. Then He singled out some of the prophets for mention and said: (وَأَوْحَيْنا إِلى إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَإِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْباطِ وَعِيسى وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُونُسَ وَهارُونَ وَسُلَيْمانَ) The wāw is a conjunction; أوحينا is a verb and agent; إلى إبراهيم is attached to أوحينا, and the names of the prophets after it are conjoined to it. (وَآتَيْنا داوُدَ زَبُوراً) آتينا is a verb and agent; داود is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); زبورا is the second mafʿūl bihi. (وَرُسُلًا قَدْ قَصَصْناهُمْ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ) رسلا is a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb conjoined to أوحينا, its implied form being "and We gave"; the clause قد قصصناهم is an adjective; عليك is attached to قصصنا; من قبل is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَرُسُلًا لَمْ نَقْصُصْهُمْ عَلَيْكَ) Conjoined to what precedes. (وَكَلَّمَ اللَّهُ مُوسى تَكْلِيماً) The wāw is a conjunction; كلّم الله is a verb and agent; موسى is a mafʿūl bihi; تكليما is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of emphasis, to remove the possibility of figurative sense. Al-Farrāʾ said: the Arabs call whatever reaches a person "speech" by whatever way it reaches him, as long as it is not emphasised with the maṣdar; if it is emphasised with it, it can only be literal. (رُسُلًا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ) رسلا is a badal (substitute) of the preceding «رسلا», or it is accusative as praise; مبشرين is an adjective; ومنذرين is conjoined to مبشرين. (لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى اللَّهِ حُجَّةٌ بَعْدَ الرُّسُلِ) This lām is the lām of «kay» (purpose) and is attached to منذرين or to مبشرين, so the matter is one of tanāzuʿ (competition between two operators), which will be mentioned in the section on benefits. It is also permissible that the lām be attached to an omitted element, that is, "We sent them for that". أن is a particle that puts the verb in the accusative; لا is negative; يكون is a defective imperfect verb, accusative by أن; للناس is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; على الله is attached to an omitted ḥāl; حجة is the postponed noun of يكون; بعد الرسل is an adverb of time attached to the sense of negation, that is:
"so that their argument and excuse after the sending of the messengers may be negated". (وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزاً حَكِيماً) Its i'rab has often been given.

* Benefits:
1- All the names of the prophets are diptotes (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), except six, which your saying «ṣun shamlahu» gathers: Ṣāliḥ, Nūḥ, Shuʿayb, Muḥammad, Lūṭ and Hūd. They are made diptote for being proper names and non-Arabic. By "non-Arabic" is meant what was transferred from the tongue of non-Arabs, in whatever language. The foreignness of a name is recognised in several ways:
1- The report of the leading authorities. 2- The name's departure from the patterns of Arabic nouns, like Ibrāhīm. 3- It being of four or five letters devoid of the dhalāqa letters; the dhalāqa letters are six: mīm, rāʾ, bāʾ, nūn, fāʾ and lām, gathered in (mur bi-nafl). 4- The combination in it of letters that do not combine in Arabic speech, such as jīm and qāf, with an intervening letter, as in:
jurmūq, and without an intervening letter, as in qaj and jaqqa; ṣād and jīm, as in al-ṣawlajān; kāf and jīm, as in al-sukurruja; rāʾ after nūn at the beginning of a word, as in narjis; zāy after dāl at the end of a word, as in muhandiz.
2- Tanāzuʿ (competition) in operation: this is when two inflected verbs, or two nouns resembling them in operation, or an inflected verb and a noun resembling it, come first, and an object comes after them, which is required by each of them in meaning. An example of two verbs:
«آتوني أفرغ عليه قطرا»; an example of two nouns is his saying:
عهدت مغيثا مغنيا من أجرته ... فلم أتخذ إلا فناءك موئلا
(I found you a helper, an enricher of the one you give protection; so I took as refuge nothing but your courtyard.)
and an example of different ones: «هاؤم اقرءوا كتابيه». When two operators compete, it is permissible to give effect to whichever you wish; the Basrans chose the last because of its nearness, and the Kufans chose the first because of its precedence. The detail of the discussion of tanāzuʿ is set out in the grammar books. The verse is a case of the second operating, because if it were a case of the first operating, a pronoun would have been placed in the second, and it would have been said: "bearers of good tidings and warners of it". It was not said so, which indicates the Basran school. It has parallels in the Qur'an.
3- By His saying: «ورسلا لم نقصصهم عليك» He meant the messengers sent to the nations whose knowledge and history are unknown to your people and to the People of the Book neighbouring your land, such as the nations of the East, the nations of the northern lands and the nations of the other part of the earth.
4- Theology (ʿilm al-kalām): Thaʿlab said: were it not for the emphasis with the maṣdar in His saying:
«وكلم الله موسى تكليما» it would be possible for you to say: "I spoke (kallamtu) to so-and-so for you", meaning I wrote him a note and sent him a messenger. But when He said «تكليما», it can only be speech heard from Allah the Exalted. From the question of speech (kalām), the science of the foundations of religion was named "ʿilm al-kalām", and it is a question investigated in its fundamentals.

dervis-irab:166-169.t:
* I'rab:
(لكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ بِما أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكَ) This clause of istidrāk (rectification) is resumptive, to explain an omitted clause that is necessary for this clause to be a rectification of it. The omitted clause is what is reported in the occasions of revelation: when the People of the Book asked for a book to be sent down from heaven and were as obstinate about it as they liked, He said: "but Allah bears witness", meaning that they do not bear witness, but Allah does. لكن is the lightened, inoperative form; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause يشهد is the khabar; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يشهد; the clause أنزل إليك is the ṣila. (أَنْزَلَهُ بِعِلْمِهِ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ يَشْهَدُونَ) The clause is explicative and has no position; أنزله is a verb and mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil (agent) being a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He"; بعلمه is attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "bearing His particular knowledge", or "being known to Allah the Exalted". والملائكة: the wāw is a conjunction and الملائكة is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause يشهدون. (وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً) The wāw is resumptive; كفى is a past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition and الله is the agent, genitive in form, nominative in position; شهيدا is a tamyīz (specification). (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) The clause is resumptive; إن and its noun; the clause كفروا is the ṣila; the clause صدوا is conjoined to it; عن سبيل الله is attached to صدوا. (قَدْ ضَلُّوا ضَلالًا بَعِيداً) The clause is the khabar of إن; ضلالا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; بعيدا is an adjective. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَظَلَمُوا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ طَرِيقاً) The clause is resumptive, to explain their destination. إن and its noun; the clause كفروا is the ṣila; the clause ظلموا is conjoined to the ṣila; the clause لم يكن الله is its khabar; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; يكن is a defective imperfect verb jussive by لم; الله is its noun; ليغفر: the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); يغفر is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the lām of denial.
The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of يكن, that is, "desiring to forgive them"; this has already been explained. ولا: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative; ليهديهم is conjoined to ليغفر; طريقا is the second mafʿūl bihi, or accusative by removal of the preposition. (إِلَّا طَرِيقَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً) إلا is a particle of exception; طريق is a continuous exception (mustathnā muttaṣil); جهنم is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, with fatḥa as its sign of genitive because it is a diptote for being a proper name and feminine; خالدين is a ḥāl from the object of يهديهم; أبدا is an adverb of time attached to خالدين, serving as emphasis, so that it not be taken to mean a long stay.
More discussion of it will come. (وَكانَ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيراً) The wāw is resumptive; كان with its noun; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يسيرا or to an omitted ḥāl; يسيرا is the khabar of كان.

* Benefits:
The meaning of khulūd in the language: the remaining of a thing for a long period in one state, with no change or corruption befalling it. For example, they call the hearth-stones (athāfī), that is, the stones of the fireplace:
khawālid (everlasting), and that is because of their long stay, not their permanent remaining. Abad is an expression for a stretch of extended time that is not divided as time is divided. Taʾabbada al-shayʾ: it remained for ever. It is used for anything that remains a long time. In Lisān al-ʿArab:
al-abad: time (al-dahr), and there is looseness in it. In the proverb: (ṭāla al-abad ʿalā lubad) it is said of everything old. They also said: abada bi-l-makān (of the pattern ḍaraba), ubūdan: he stayed in it and did not leave. They had nothing in their speech in the sense of "infinity".
In Lisān it explains khuld as permanence of remaining in an abode one does not leave. By permanent dwelling in common usage is meant the opposite of temporary, shifting dwelling, like dwelling in the desert. So those who have houses in cities in which they live are said, in the language, to be khālidūn (abiding) in them. He said in Lisān: khalada bi-l-makān yakhludu khulūdan (of the pattern naṣara) and akhlada: he stayed; and khalada like ḍaraba and naṣara, khaldan and khulūdan also: grey hair was slow to come to him. One who grew old without turning grey and without his teeth falling out is called al-mukhlad with kasra on the lām, and it was said: with fatḥa. Zuhayr said:
لمن الدّيار غشيتها بالفدفد ... كالوحي في حجر المسيل المخلد
(Whose are the abodes I visited on the high ground, like writing on the stones of the watercourse, long-lasting?)

dervis-irab:170-170.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ قَدْ جاءَكُمُ الرَّسُولُ بِالْحَقِّ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) A resumptive statement, offered to command those under obligation in general to believe, after the avenues of excuse had been closed to them. The address is general to all people, not to the people of Mecca alone, although the usual rule is that «يا أيها الناس» is an address to the people of Mecca and «يا أيها الذين آمنوا» an address to the people of Medina. قد is a particle of certainty; جاءكم الرسول is a verb, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and fāʿil (agent); بالحق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاءكم; من ربكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فَآمِنُوا خَيْراً لَكُمْ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ fuṣḥā (eloquent fāʾ); آمنوا is an imperative verb with its agent, that is: "if the matter is as you have come to know, then believe; belief will be better for you, because it purifies you and cleanses you of sensory and moral impurities and qualifies you for everlasting happiness." This is the implied form that comes first to mind, and it is the view of al-Kisāʾī, so it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted kāna with its noun. As for al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, they take the implied form to be: "and be guided by belief, better for you", that is, than what you are in.
Al-Farrāʾ said: "believe with a belief better for you", so its accusative is as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar. Al-Zamakhsharī said: its accusative is by an implied verb, because when He urged them to belief, it was known that He was urging them to a matter, so He said "better for you", that is: aim for or bring what is better for you than what you are in. لكم is attached to «خيرا». (وَإِنْ تَكْفُرُوا فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; تكفروا is an imperfect verb, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) [Translator's note: the source prints «وتفكروا», apparently a misprint for «وتكفروا»]; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being:
"your disbelief will not harm Him, because He is independent of you". He alerted to His independence by His saying: «فإن لله ما في السموات والأرض»; so the fāʾ is for justification; إن is a particle resembling the verb; لله is attached to an omitted fronted khabar of it; ما is a relative noun, its postponed noun; في السموات والأرض is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative. (وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً) Its i'rab has often been given.

dervis-irab:171-171.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لا تَغْلُوا): do not exceed the reasonable limit. The origin of ghuluww in everything is exceeding its limit. Ghalā bi-l-jāriya ʿaẓmuhā wa-laḥmuhā: when a girl hastens into youth and outstrips her peers, "it surges with her" (yaghlū bihā) ghuluwwan and ghalāʾan. From that is the saying of al-Ḥārith ibn Khālid al-Makhzūmī, in some fine verses in which he recalls his beloved and the days that passed of his days and hers:
إذ ودّها صاف ورؤيتها ... أمنية وكلاهما غنم
لفّاء مملوء مخلخلها ... عجزاء ليس لعظمها حجم
خمصانة قلق موشّحها ... رود الشباب غلا بها عظم
وكأن غالية تباشرها ... تحت الثياب إذا صفا النجم
(When her love was pure and seeing her was a wish, and both were a gain; full-thighed, her anklets filled, large-hipped, her bones without bulk; slender-waisted, her sash loose, tender with youth, her bones grown strong; and as though perfume touched her beneath her clothes when the star is clear.)

* I'rab:
(يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لا تَغْلُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ) A resumptive statement, offered to warn the People of the Book against exaggeration. يا is a particle of vocative and أهل الكتاب is the one addressed, a muḍāf; لا is prohibitive and تغلوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; في دينكم is attached to تغلوا. (وَلا تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْحَقَّ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive and تقولوا is a jussive imperfect verb; على الله is attached to تقولوا; إلا is a particle of restriction; الحق is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "except the true saying", or a mafʿūl bihi because it contains the sense of "saying", as in "I said a poem". (إِنَّمَا الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُ أَلْقاها إِلى مَرْيَمَ وَرُوحٌ مِنْهُ) A resumptive statement, offered to define the lord Messiah, peace be upon him. إنما is kāffa and makfūfa (a restraining particle and what is restrained); المسيح is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and عيسى a badal (substitute) of it; ابن مريم is also a badal or an adjective; رسول الله is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; كلمته is conjoined to رسول; the clause ألقاها is a ḥāl clause, and قد must be implied with it, the operator in the ḥāl being the sense of «كلمته», because the meaning of "word" is that he was brought into being by it without a father. وإلى مريم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ألقاها; وروح is conjoined to كلمته; منه is attached to an omitted adjective of روح, and من is for the beginning of the limit. (فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَلا تَقُولُوا ثَلاثَةٌ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ fuṣḥā, that is: "if the matter is thus, then believe in Allah with a belief fitting to Him, the Exalted"; بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنوا; ورسله is conjoined to the exalted name; the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تقولوا is an imperfect verb jussive by it; ثلاثة is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "do not say: our gods are three", and the clause آلهتنا ثلاثة is in the position of an accusative as the quoted speech. (انْتَهُوا خَيْراً لَكُمْ) The clause is resumptive; انتهوا is an imperative verb and agent; and خيرا — its i'rab was given a little earlier, so renew your acquaintance with it; لكم is attached to «خيرا». (إِنَّمَا اللَّهُ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ) A resumptive statement, offered to confirm oneness. إنما is kāffa and makfūfa; الله is a mubtadaʾ and إله the khabar; واحد is an adjective. (سُبْحانَهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ) سبحان is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, that is, "glorify Him with glorification"; أن and what is within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "from his having"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to سبحان; له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar of يكون; ولد is its postponed noun; the clause of declaring transcendence is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, that is, "transcendent". (لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) له is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ما is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ; في السموات is attached to an omitted ṣila; the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; وما في الأرض is conjoined to ما في السموات; the clause is resumptive, offered to justify the declaration of transcendence, that is: if He owns everything in them, how can one imagine His need of a child? (وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا) Its i'rab has often been given.

* Benefits:
One of the clever ones took issue with the i'rab of His saying, the Exalted: «ثلاثة» and said: "Among the difficulties also is His saying, the Exalted: «ثلاثة». They went, regarding the nominative of ثلاثة, to its being the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the meaning being: 'do not say: our gods are three'. That too is invalid, because the denial is directed only at the khabar. If we say 'do not say: our gods are three', we have negated the three and have not negated the gods, exalted is Allah above that.
The correct view is to say: 'three' is an adjective of the last mubtadaʾ, 'do not say: we have three gods'; then the khabar, which is «لنا», was omitted as «لنا» is omitted in your saying «لا إله إلا الله», leaving 'do not say: three gods', as one says 'no two gods', so the distinction is sound."
His words do not lack a rare cleverness, so reflect on that, and Allah protect you.

dervis-irab:172-173.t:
* Vocabulary:
[Translator's note: in the source text of this entry, the opening words of each quoted verse and of the vocabulary head are cut off, so fragments such as «َسْتَنْكِفَ)» appear instead of the full text. The translation follows what is printed.]
(...يَسْتَنْكِفَ)
Istinkāf: refraining from something out of disdain and shrinking from it. It was said that its origin is from nakafa al-damʿ, when one wipes the tear from his cheek with his finger so that it does not show; and nakafa from it: he disdained; and ankafahu ʿanhu: he cleared him of it. In al-Miṣbāḥ: nakaftu min al-shayʾ nakfan (of the pattern taʿiba), and nakaftu ankufu (of the pattern qatala) is a dialect form. And istankaftu: I refrained out of disdain and arrogance.

* I'rab:
(...لَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفَ الْمَسِيحُ أَنْ يَكُونَ عَبْداً لِلَّهِ)
A resumptive statement, offered to confirm the earlier declaration of transcendence. The meaning: the Messiah will not disdain, nor disown being a servant of Allah, nor is he one who holds himself above that, because he is among the most knowing of Allah's creation of the greatness of Allah, and of what is due to Him from the rational among His creatures of gratitude and servanthood, by which they excel one another. لن is a particle of negation, accusative and future; يستنكف is an imperfect verb accusative by it; المسيح is the fāʿil (agent); أن and what is within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, the implied form being: "from being ..."; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يستنكف; عبدا is the khabar of يكون; ولله is attached to an omitted adjective of «عبدا». (...وَلَا الْمَلائِكَةُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ)
The wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; الملائكة is conjoined to المسيح, or is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is, "and they disdain"; المقربون is an adjective of الملائكة. (...وَمَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفْ عَنْ عِبادَتِهِ وَيَسْتَكْبِرْ)
The wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; يستنكف is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); عن عبادته is attached to يستنكف. (...فَسَيَحْشُرُهُمْ إِلَيْهِ جَمِيعاً)
It is permissible that the fāʾ be the apodosis of the condition, the implied form being: "whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will punish him when He gathers him to Him, and whoever does not disdain and is not arrogant, He will reward him". It is also permissible that the apodosis be omitted, that is, "He will requite him", and then His saying «فسيحشرهم» is conjoined to it. The hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi; إليه is attached to يحشرهم; جميعا is a ḥāl from the hāʾ; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من». (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ فَيُوَفِّيهِمْ أُجُورَهُمْ وَيَزِيدُهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ) The fāʾ is for ramification, and the clause after it has no grammatical position because it stands as a resumption; أما is a particle of condition and detailing; الذين is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila; the clause عملوا الصالحات is conjoined to the ṣila; the fāʾ is the connective; يوفيهم is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He", the hāʾ being its first object and أجورهم its second; يزيدهم is conjoined to فيوفيهم; من فضله is attached to يزيدهم; the clause is the khabar of الذين. (وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اسْتَنْكَفُوا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا فَيُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً) The clause is conjoined to what precedes and its i'rab has already been given; عذابا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; أليما is an adjective. (وَلا يَجِدُونَ لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلِيًّا وَلا نَصِيراً) Conjoined to what precedes; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «وليا»; من دون الله is attached to an omitted ḥāl; وليا is a mafʿūl bihi; ولا نصيرا is conjoined to it.

* Benefits:
Those who hold the superiority of angels over prophets used this verse as evidence, and they are Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī and al-Ḥalīmī among the leaders of the Ashʿarites, and most of the Muʿtazila. Al-Zamakhsharī laid out the manner of the proof in a way that neither fattens nor relieves hunger, and al-Bayḍāwī and Ibn al-Munayyir went on at length in refuting him. The fair-minded person sees that ranking in excellence in this matter is a kind of stoning the unseen, since it cannot be known except by a text from the Lawgiver, and there is no text. The disagreement on this has no benefit or return in belief or action, but is merely a widening of the distance of division by disputation and argument.

dervis-irab:174-175.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ قَدْ جاءَكُمْ بُرْهانٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) A resumptive statement, to confirm where matters ended up in establishing overwhelming proofs against the opponents, and Allah the Exalted calling all people to follow His proof and be guided by the light He brought.
قد is a particle of certainty; جاءكم برهان is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a postponed fāʿil (agent); من ربكم is attached to an omitted adjective of برهان. (وَأَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكُمْ نُوراً مُبِيناً) The wāw is a conjunction; أنزلنا is a verb and agent; إليكم is attached to أنزلنا; نورا is a mafʿūl bihi; مبينا is an adjective. (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَاعْتَصَمُوا بِهِ) The fāʾ is for ramification and the clause has no position; أما is a particle of condition and detailing; الذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); بالله is attached to آمنوا; واعتصموا به is conjoined to آمنوا. (فَسَيُدْخِلُهُمْ فِي رَحْمَةٍ مِنْهُ وَفَضْلٍ) The fāʾ is the connective for the apodosis of «أما», and the clause يدخلهم is the khabar (predicate) of الذين; في رحمة is attached to يدخلهم, and منه is attached to an omitted adjective of رحمة; وفضل is conjoined to رحمة. (وَيَهْدِيهِمْ إِلَيْهِ صِراطاً مُسْتَقِيماً) Conjoined to يدخلهم; وإليه is attached to an omitted ḥāl from «صراطا», fronted before it; صراطا is the second mafʿūl bihi of يهديهم, or a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb indicated by «يهديهم»; مستقيما is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz mursal (transferred usage with a non-resemblance link) in His saying: «في رحمة منه», because a person does not dwell in mercy, since it is one of the abstract meanings; he dwells only in its place, which is Paradise.
So the use of "mercy" for its place is a figurative usage in which the occupant is mentioned and the place is meant; its relation is that of occupancy (ḥāliyya).

dervis-irab:64-64.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ رَسُولٍ): The واو is resumptive; ما is negative; أرسلنا is a verb and agent; من is a redundant preposition; and رسول is genitive in form and accusative in position as the mafʿūl bihi of أرسلنا. (إِلَّا لِيُطاعَ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): إلا is a particle of restriction; the لام is for cause; يطاع is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the lām; and the preposition and its genitive noun are an exception emptied (mufarragh) from the most general of causes, i.e. "We sent no messenger for any purpose of purposes except for obedience", so it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, but it does not fulfil the conditions for the accusative. As for بإذن الله, it is permissible that this preposition and its genitive noun be attached to an omitted element functioning as ḥāl; it was also said: to أرسلنا; and it was said: to يطاع. The three analyses are equal in preponderance. (وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ إِذْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ جاؤُكَ): The واو is resumptive; لو is conditional; أن with its ism and what is within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar, the agent of an omitted verb, i.e. "had their coming been established"; إذ is an adverb of past time attached to جاءوك; the clause ظلموا أنفسهم is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause جاءوك is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أن. (فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا اللَّهَ وَاسْتَغْفَرَ لَهُمُ الرَّسُولُ): The فاء is a conjunction, and the clause استغفروا is conjoined to جاءوك; the name of Majesty is a mafʿūl bihi; and استغفر لهم الرسول is conjoined to what preceded. (لَوَجَدُوا اللَّهَ تَوَّاباً رَحِيماً): The لام occurs in the apodosis of لو; وجدوا الله is a verb, agent and first mafʿūl bihi, and the clause has no position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; توابا is a second mafʿūl bihi, and رحيما is a naʿt of توابا or a badal from it.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is an iltifāt in His words «واستغفر لهم الرسول», for the flow of the speech required that He say "and you asked forgiveness for them", but He turned from that to exalt the Messenger, to point to him with an indication that moves their hearts, and because it includes the mention of a fitting attribute, namely asking forgiveness for those whose sins have grown great and whose offences are many.

dervis-irab:65-65.t:
* Vocabulary:
(شَجَرَ): it was mixed, varied, interwoven and entangled; from it the tree (shajar) is named because of the interweaving and entanglement of its branches. Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd said:
وهم الحكّام أرباب الهدى ... وسعاة الناس في الأمر الشّجر
(They are the judges, the lords of guidance, and the pursuers of the people's interests in the entangled affair.)
meaning the varied and entangled. From it comes "tashājur al-rimāḥ", that is, the lances' crossing one another.

* I'rab:
(فَلا وَرَبِّكَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): The فاء is resumptive; لا is added to emphasise the oath; the واو is a particle of oath and genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "uqsimu"; and «لا يؤمنون»: لا is negative and يؤمنون is an imperfect verb, nominative, with the واو as agent; and the clause لا يؤمنون has no position, because it is the answer to the oath. (حَتَّى يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيما شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ): حتى is a particle of limit and genitive; يحكموك is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after حتى, the واو is the agent and the كاف the mafʿūl bihi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يؤمنون; فيما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يحكّموك; the clause شجر is a ṣila of the relative; and بينهم is an adverb of place attached to شجر. (ثُمَّ لا يَجِدُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجاً مِمَّا قَضَيْتَ): ثم is a particle of conjunction denoting delay; لا is negative; يجدوا is conjoined to يحكموك; في أنفسهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يجدوا, serving as the second object; حرجا is the first mafʿūl bihi of يجدوا; مما is attached to an omitted element functioning as naʿt of حرجا; and the clause قضيت is a ṣila of the relative. (وَيُسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيماً): conjoined to يجدوا, and تسليما is a mafʿūl muṭlaq.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there are numerous intensifications that reach the highest ranks of eloquence. The aim of them is to increase the warning and the threat, at which the muscles shudder and the hearts tremble. We shall point to them in detail:
1- First, He, glorified be He, swore by Himself, reinforcing this oath with the particle of negation, that they do not believe. Faith is the capital of the righteous among Allah's servants, until there comes to them one of the noblest of goals, namely recourse to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and making him the judge in what has broken out between them of dispute.
2- Then He, glorified be He, was not content with that, but said: «ثم لا يجدوا في أنفسهم حرجا مما قضيت», adding to the seeking of judgment another matter, namely finding no constraint at all in their breasts; so mere seeking of judgment and submission is not sufficient, but it must spring from their breasts, issuing from contentment, reassurance and goodness of soul. This is the finest depiction of the relationship that must be rooted between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers, and between a leader and those he leads, and the trust that takes root in the hearts of the people towards their leader and the one in authority over them, so long as he is well guided and walks in the way of sound uprightness.
3- Then He, glorified be He, was not content with all of this, but added to it His words: ويسلموا, that is, submit with complete submission and yield outwardly and inwardly, not a blind yielding, but the yielding of one who is confident and reassured of the soundness of the position of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
4- And to «يسلموا» He added the confirming maṣdar, saying «تسليما». Thus faith is not established for a servant until this seeking of judgment takes place from him, and he finds no constraint in his breast at what has been decreed against him, and submits to the ruling of Allah and His law with a submission mixed with no rejection and tainted by no blemish. Glorified be the One who said these words! And listen to the rest of this section in the following verse.

* Benefits:
What we mentioned in parsing His words, the Exalted: «فلا وربك» is the preferred view in our opinion, and we think it complete for the benefit to cite some of what has been said about it. Know that the redundant «لا» with an oath is frequent in the Noble Qur'an where the oath is by a verb, such as: «فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم», «لا أقسم بهذا البلد», «لا أقسم بيوم القيامة» and others. The benefit of it is to confirm the magnification of what is sworn by, and it is known that one swears by a thing only to magnify it; so it is as if He were saying: "My magnification of these things by oath is as no magnification", meaning that they are of such greatness and grandeur that they deserve more than that and require what is above it. An example in poetry is his saying:
فلا وأبيك ابنة العامر ... يّ لا يدعي القوم أني أفرّ
(No, by your father, O daughter of al-ʿĀmirī, let the people not claim that I flee.)
More of its discussion will come in its coming places in this wonderful book. There are sayings of the scholars on this construction which we record because they are not without merit, among them:
1- That «لا» is a rejection of a statement whose implied form is "they will not do so", or "the matter is not as they claim, that they have believed in what was sent down to you"; then the oath is begun anew with His words: وربك لا يؤمنون. On this view the pause at «لا» is complete, and al-Ṭabarī approved it, and that suffices.
2- The second is that the first «لا» was put before the oath out of concern for the negation, then repeated for emphasis.
3- The third is that the second «لا» is redundant and the oath is parenthetical between the particle of negation and the negated verb, the implied form being "so, by your Lord, they will not believe"; thus the analyses of it are four.

dervis-irab:66-68.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ أَنَّا كَتَبْنا عَلَيْهِمْ أَنِ اقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ): A resumptive statement, introduced to rebuke those who hang back from responding to the Messenger and obeying him. The واو is resumptive; لو is conditional; أن and what is within its scope are the agent of an omitted verb, i.e. "had Our prescribing been established" (its like has already been given); أن with its ism, and the clause كتبنا is its khabar; عليهم is attached to كتبنا; أن is maṣdar-forming; اقتلوا is an imperative verb and the واو is the agent; the interpreted maṣdar is the object of كتبنا. It was also said that أن is explicative (mufassira), because كتبنا contains the meaning of saying without its letters. أنفسكم is a mafʿūl bihi. (أَوِ اخْرُجُوا مِنْ دِيارِكُمْ): conjoined to اقتلوا أنفسكم, and من دياركم is attached to اخرجوا. (ما فَعَلُوهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ مِنْهُمْ): The clause has no position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. The pronoun in «فعلوه» refers to one of the two matters, or to what was prescribed for them. إلا is a particle of restriction; قليل is a badal from the واو in «فعلوه», because it is an exception from a complete, non-affirmative statement; and منهم is attached to an omitted element functioning as naʿt of قليل. It has also been read in the accusative, as an exception from them. (وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ فَعَلُوا ما يُوعَظُونَ بِهِ): Conjoined to what preceded; the i'rab of this construction was given a little earlier. ما is a relative noun and mafʿūl bihi, and the clause يوعظون به is a ṣila of the relative. (لَكانَ خَيْراً لَهُمْ وَأَشَدَّ تَثْبِيتاً): The لام occurs in the apodosis of لو; كان and its latent ism; خيرا is its khabar; أشد is conjoined to «خيرا»; and تثبيتا is a tamyīz. (وَإِذاً لَآتَيْناهُمْ مِنْ لَدُنَّا أَجْراً عَظِيماً): The واو is a conjunction; إذن is a particle of response and consequence made inoperative because it occurs after one of the two conjunctions, namely the wāw and the fāʾ; and it is the answer to an implied question, as if it had been said: "And what would be theirs after being firmly established?" So it was said: "And then, had they been firmly established…, We would have given them". The لام is the apodosis of the implied لو; آتيناهم is a verb, agent and first mafʿūl bihi; من لدنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آتيناهم; أجرا is a mafʿūl bihi; and عظيما a naʿt. (وَلَهَدَيْناهُمْ صِراطاً مُسْتَقِيماً): Conjoined as well; صراطا is a second mafʿūl bihi or accusative by removal of the preposition, to which reference was made in al-Fātiḥa; and مستقيما is a naʿt.

* Benefits:
A picture of the marvels of Arab-Islamic heroism:
History relates that al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām and Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa brought a dispute before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over shirāj (water channels) by which they used to water their palm trees, which is a watercourse. He said: "Water, O Zubayr, then send the water to your neighbour." Ḥāṭib became angry and said: "Because he is your cousin?" The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed, and then he said: "Water, O Zubayr, then hold back the water until it returns to the base of the trees, and take your full due, then send it to your neighbour." He had advised al-Zubayr with an opinion that gave leeway to him and to his opponent, but when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was angered he gave al-Zubayr his full right in an explicit ruling.
Then the two went out and passed by al-Miqdād, who said to him: "For whom was the judgment?" The Anṣārī said: "He judged for his cousin," and twisted his mouth. A Jew exploited the situation and said: "They testify that he is the Messenger of Allah, then accuse him in a judgment he passes between them! By Allah, we once committed a sin in the lifetime of Moses, and he called us to repent of it and said: 'Kill yourselves,' and we did so, and our slain reached seventy thousand until He was pleased with us." Thābit, Ibn Masʿūd and ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir said: "If Muḥammad had commanded us to kill ourselves, we would have killed them." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, among my community are those whose faith is more firmly fixed in their souls than the towering mountains."

dervis-irab:69-70.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ): A resumptive statement, introduced to show the merit of obeying Allah and His Messenger. من is conditional and in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; يطع الله is the protasis; and الرسول is conjoined to الله. (فَأُولئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ وَالشُّهَداءِ وَالصَّالِحِينَ): The فاء links the apodosis; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; مع is an adverb of place attached to an omitted element functioning as khabar; الذين is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause joined with the فاء is in the position of jussive as apodosis; the clause أنعم الله عليهم is a ṣila of the relative; من النبيين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element functioning as ḥāl; and what follows it is conjoined to النبيّين. (وَحَسُنَ أُولئِكَ رَفِيقاً): The واو is a conjunction; حسن is a past verb that contains the meaning of praise and wonder; أولئك is a demonstrative and agent; and رفيقا is a tamyīz or, in the opinion of al-Akhfash, a ḥāl. The word رفيق is the same for one and many, and likewise الصديق and الخليط. (ذلِكَ الْفَضْلُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ عَلِيماً): The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and الفضل a badal from it, and من الله is attached to an omitted element functioning as khabar; it is also permissible that الفضل be the khabar and من الله be attached to an omitted element functioning as ḥāl. The demonstrative clause is resumptive. كفى is a past verb; the باء is a redundant preposition; الله is the agent in position and genitive in form; and عليما is a tamyīz or ḥāl, whose i'rab has already been given. The clause كفى is resumptive.

dervis-irab:138-140.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بَشِّرِ) البشارة is the gladdening report. The gladdening report is called بشارة because it makes joy appear on the بشرة, i.e. the outer skin. More on it will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(العزة): well known; its origin in the language is severity. From it the hard, severe ground is called عزاز with fatḥa on the ʿayn, and it was said: قد استعزّ على المريض, when [the illness] grew severe upon the sick man; and from it was said: عزّ عليّ أن يكون كذا وكذا, i.e. it is hard upon me.

* I'rab:
(بَشِّرِ الْمُنافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً) A resumptive speech, meant to denounce the hypocrites. بشر المنافقين: an imperative verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; the bāʾ is a preposition, and أن with what is in its scope is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to «بشّر»; لهم is attached to an omitted khabar of أن, preposed; عذابا is its postposed noun; and أليما is an adjective. (الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكافِرِينَ أَوْلِياءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) الذين is an adjective of the hypocrites, or accusative as an expression of censure (naṣb ʿalā al-dhamm), because they take the Jews as allies; the clause يتخذون is the ṣila of the relative noun, the wāw being the fāʿil; المؤمنين is [Translator's note: the source states «والمؤمنين مفعول به أول»; as written the first mafʿūl is in fact الكافرين, while المؤمنين is the genitive after دون; translated as written]; أولياء is the second mafʿūl bihi; and من دون المؤمنين is attached to an omitted ḥāl from the fāʿil of يتخذون, or to an adjective of أولياء. (أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ؟) The hamza is for a disapproving question; يبتغون is an imperfect verb and the wāw the fāʿil; عندهم is an adverb attached to يبتغون; العزة is the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause is resumptive, meant to rebuke them, and you may make it accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "imagining that they have honour with them". (فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعاً) The fāʾ is for giving a reason; إن and its noun; لله, the preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of it; جميعا is a ḥāl; and the clause is explanatory of the reason, with no position. (وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتابِ أَنْ إِذا سَمِعْتُمْ آياتِ اللَّهِ يُكْفَرُ بِها وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِها) The wāw is resumptive and قد is a particle of certainty; نزل is a past verb with a latent fāʿil; عليكم is attached to نزل; في الكتاب is also attached to نزل or to an omitted ḥāl. أن with fatḥa on the hamza is the lightened form of the heavy أنّ, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter, and it is interpreted as a maṣdar, the mafʿūl of «نزل»; إذا is an adverb of the future containing the sense of a condition; the clause سمعتم is in the position of the genitive by annexation; آيات الله is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause "إذا with its protasis and its apodosis" is the khabar of «أن»; the clause يكفر بها is a ḥāl clause; the clause ويستهزأ بها is conjoined to it; and بها, a preposition and its genitive noun, takes the place of the nāʾib fāʿil in both verbs. (فَلا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ) The fāʾ is connecting for the apodosis of إذا; لا is prohibitive and تقعدوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; معهم is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl; حتى is a particle of limit and genitive; يخوضوا is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تقعدوا; في حديث is attached to يخوضوا; and غيره is an adjective of حديث. (إِنَّكُمْ إِذاً مِثْلُهُمْ) إن and its noun; إذن is a particle of response and a neglected element (not operating) because it is in the middle; مثلهم is the khabar of إن. It did not agree between the noun and the khabar, so «مثل» was made singular and predicated of a plural, as it did agree in another place, where He said: «وحور عين كأمثال اللؤلؤ المكنون», because «مثل» has the sense of a maṣdar, the implied meaning being "your disobedience is like their disobedience"; and the clause has no position because it gives the reason for the prohibition. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ جامِعُ الْمُنافِقِينَ وَالْكافِرِينَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ جَمِيعاً) The clause is a second reason for the likeness; more on this likeness will come in the section on Rhetoric; إن with its noun and khabar; في جهنم is attached to جامع; and جميعا is a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
1- Sarcasm (tahakkum) in His saying «بشر». In its original linguistic sense, التهكم is the collapse of a structure; one says تهكمت البئر when the well collapsed; and also intense anger and regret over a missed matter. In the rhetorical technical sense it is mockery and ridicule of the arrogant by addressing them with a word of exaltation where contempt is meant, glad tidings where warning is meant, and promise where threat is meant. We have expanded on this art in some detail because the Qur'an overflows with examples of sarcasm, which will come in their places. Among the delightful instances of this art in poetry is the saying of Ibn al-Rūmī:
فيا له من عمل صالح ... يرفعه الله إلى أسفل
(What a righteous deed! Allah raises it to the bottom.)
And he has, in describing Ibn Ḥuṣayna the hunchback, verses of utmost sarcasm which place praise where mockery and ridicule are meant:
لا تظنّنّ حدبة الظهر عيبا ... فهي في الحسن من صفات الهلال
وكذاك القسيّ محدودبات ... وهي أنكى من الظّبا والعوالي
وإذا ما علا السنام ففيه ... لقدوم الجمال أي جمال!!
وأرى الانحناء في منسر البا ... زي ولم يعد مخلب الرئبال
ما رأتها النساء إلا تمنّت ... لو غدت حلية لكل الرجال
(Do not think the humped back a fault; in beauty it is among the attributes of the crescent moon. / So too the bows are bent, yet they wound more than swords' edges and spears. / And when the hump rises, in it, for the arrival of camels, what beauty! / And I see the curve in the beak of the falcon, and the claw of the lion is not without it. / The women never saw it but they wished it would become an adornment for all men.)
And Ibn al-Rūmī ended this mocking artistic picture with his saying:
وإذا لم يكن من الهجر بدّ ... فعسى أن تزورني في الخيال
(And if there is no avoiding estrangement, perhaps you will visit me in imagination.)
2- The explicit derivative metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya) in His saying «بشر», because بشارة is the gladdening report, and it was called بشارة because it makes joy appear on the بشرة, i.e.
the outer skin.
3- Simile in His saying: «إنكم إذن مثلهم». The likeness between the disbelievers and the hypocrites appears in the verse between those who sit and those who are sat with. For those who side with the disbelievers and ally with them and stretch out to them hands of submission and abasement, although they are able to stand firm and defy, are like the disbelievers, even if they are not of them; indeed their evil is greater, and the danger from them is more deserving of caution, because if they do not denounce them they are pleased, and whoever is pleased with disbelief is a disbeliever.

dervis-irab:141-141.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَتَرَبَّصُونَ بِكُمْ): they wait for whatever renews for you of victory or failure.
In al-Miṣbāḥ: «تربصت الأمر تربّصا: I waited for it. And الرّبصة, on the pattern of غرفة, is a noun from it; and تربصت الأمر بفلان: I waited for it to befall him.» It is commonly followed by the word الدوائر (the turns of fortune), which is always used for evil, because it is دائرة, i.e. the matters that turn and occur in time of calamities and trials; but here it is open to good and evil together, by the evidence of the breakdown in His saying: «فإن كان لكم فتح» etc.
(نَسْتَحْوِذْ): imperfect of استحوذ, which is irregular in analogy though eloquent in usage, because by right it should transfer the vowel of its weak letter to the quiescent letter before it and turn it into an alif, like استقام and استعاد and the like. الاستحواذ is overpowering a thing and gaining mastery over it; one says حاذ and أحاذ, so it is triliteral and quadriliteral with one meaning.
And أحوذ; of the speech of those who said أحوذ is the saying of Labīd, in describing a wild ass and she-asses:
إذا اجتمعت وأحوذ جانبيها ... وأوردها على عوج طوال
(When they were gathered, and he mastered both their flanks and brought them to water on long, crooked [legs].)

* I'rab:
(الَّذِينَ يَتَرَبَّصُونَ بِكُمْ) The relative noun is an adjective of the hypocrites or accusative as an expression of censure, and the clause يتربصون بكم is the ṣila of the relative noun. (فَإِنْ كانَ لَكُمْ فَتْحٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ قالُوا: أَلَمْ نَكُنْ مَعَكُمْ؟) The fāʾ is resumptive and إن conditional; كان is a defective past verb, the protasis; لكم is attached to an omitted khabar of it, preposed; فتح is its postposed noun; من الله is attached to an omitted adjective of فتح; قالوا is a verb and fāʿil in the position of the jussive, the apodosis; the clause ألم نكن معكم is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech; and معكم is an adverb attached to an omitted khabar of نكن. (وَإِنْ كانَ لِلْكافِرِينَ نَصِيبٌ) The wāw is a conjunction and إن conditional; كان is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive, the protasis; وللكافرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of كان, preposed; and نصيب is its postposed noun. (قالُوا أَلَمْ نَسْتَحْوِذْ عَلَيْكُمْ) قالوا is a verb and fāʿil in the position of the jussive, the apodosis; and the clause ألم نستحوذ عليكم is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech. (وَنَمْنَعْكُمْ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) نمنعكم is conjoined to نستحوذ, and من المؤمنين is attached to نمنعكم. (فَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) The fāʾ is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يحكم is the khabar; بينكم is an adverb attached to يحكم, and likewise يوم القيامة. (وَلَنْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لِلْكافِرِينَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ سَبِيلًا) The wāw is a conjunction; لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; يجعل is an imperfect verb made accusative by لن; الله is the fāʿil; وللكافرين is attached to يجعل, serving as its first object; and سبيلا is its second object. وعلى المؤمنين is attached to an omitted ḥāl because it was an adjective of سبيلا and was put before it.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse is a mujāz mursal, namely in His saying «فتح»: He called the victory that the Muslims attained "opening" (fatḥ) with regard to what the victory leads to, because it is a matter in which souls rejoice, hearts are reassured, and the gates of heaven are opened.
The poets have gazed at the sky of this meaning, and the foremost in this field was Abū Tammām al-Ṭāʾī in his poem "Fatḥ al-Futūḥ" (The Conquest of Conquests), in which he praised al-Muʿtaṣim billāh and described the battle of ʿAmmūriyya, which he composed in the year two hundred and twenty-three of the Hijra.
ʿAmmūriyya was one of the greatest cities of the Byzantines in Asia Minor. The reason for al-Muʿtaṣim's march against it was that Theophilus son of Michael, king of the Byzantines, went out into the lands of the Muslims and reached Zibaṭra, a town in Asia Minor between Malatya and Samosata, in which al-Muʿtaṣim was born; he sacked it with killing and captivity, then raided Malatya and others, killing, taking captives and mutilating the prisoners. The news reached al-Muʿtaṣim and he considered it monstrous; and it was said that an Arab woman cried out while she was in the hands of the Byzantines: "O Muʿtaṣim!" and he answered, while on his couch: "At your service, at your service." He rose, called for mobilisation and marched to ʿAmmūriyya. The Arabic account says that it was the city in which Theophilus was born; he besieged it, located a weak point in the wall, and shot at the wall from that side, which cracked; the Arabs entered the city, slaughtered its inhabitants, burned it and took its women and children captive. Abū Tammām was in his company and witnessed the battle himself. The astrologers had claimed to al-Muʿtaṣim that the time did not suit conquest and that the city would be conquered only at the ripening of figs and grapes, but al-Muʿtaṣim did not listen to what they said, and marched with his army and conquered it. We find Abū Tammām speaking of all this in his poem, as though it were a historical register of this great battle; and he opened it with his saying:
السيف أصدق أنباء من الكتب ... في حده الحد بين الجد واللعب
بيض الصفائح لا سود الصحائف في ... متونهن جلاء الشك والريب فتح الفتوح تعالى أن يحيط به ... نظم من الشعر أو نثر من ا
لخطب فتح تفتح أبواب السماء له ... وتبرز الأرض في أثوابها القشب
(The sword is truer in tidings than the books: in its edge is the dividing line between earnest and play. / The white blades, not the black pages: in their surfaces is the clearing of doubt and misgiving. The conquest of conquests, too exalted to be encompassed by verse composed or prose of oration. / A conquest for which the gates of heaven are opened, and the earth comes forth in its new garments.) [Translator's note: the lines run together at this point in the source, and the word «الخطب» is split across a line break; reproduced as printed.]
Then he says, addressing al-Muʿtaṣim:
لقد تركت أمير المؤمنين بها ... للنار يوما ذليل الصخر والخشب
(You left the Commander of the Faithful there, for the fire one day, a humbled thing of rock and wood.)
And he speaks of the defeat of the king of the Byzantines:
لما رأى الحرب رأي العين توفلس ... والحرب مشتقة المعنى من الحرب
ولى وقد ألجم الخطي منطقه ... بسكتة تحتها الأحشاء في صخب
تسعون ألفا كآساد الشرى نضجت ... جلودهم قبل نضج التين والعنب
(When Theophilus saw war with his own eyes — and war is derived in meaning from plunder — he turned away, the spear having bridled his speech with a silence beneath which the bowels were in uproar. / Ninety thousand like lions of Sharā, their skins were cooked before the ripening of fig and grape.)
Of the rhetoric of high standing is that He called the victory of the Muslims "opening" (fatḥ) and the victory of the disbelievers "share" (naṣīb), to magnify the standing of the former and to proclaim that the inevitable outcome belongs to the patient believers who shelter behind a creed that neither wavers nor weakens, and to signal that the victory of the disbelievers is, in the span of time, only a lowly portion and a moment of this world that they obtain, a stretch of living in whose current they swim.
